title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Shared combinational radix-4 divider with tapered trial subtractors
motivation:
The baseline measures 12.12 CoreMark iterations/second at 5.442 MHz.
Its reported worst path has 156 cells and passes through forwarding and
the combinational ALU. The four signed/unsigned division and remainder
expressions in alu.sv are a strong candidate for this arithmetic depth;
the available timing summary does not identify the individual operator.
There are no prior divider experiments or recorded lessons. Reducing
divider depth locally can improve Fmax without sacrificing CoreMark
iterations/cycle or changing the pipeline's stall and retirement rules.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU arithmetic in alu.sv with one
explicitly unrolled, combinational unsigned radix-4 restoring divmod
network, surrounded by RV32M sign and special-case handling. This is a
local arithmetic implementation change: retain the ALU interface, zero
extra cycles, all pipeline registers and handshakes, and nret=1.

For DIV/REM, form unsigned two's-complement magnitudes of a and b;
DIVU/REMU use the original operands. Precompute D, 2*D and 3*D as
34-bit unsigned values once. Consume the dividend from most-significant
to least-significant two-bit groups in sixteen combinational steps.
Each step forms T = 4*R + next_pair and calculates T-D, T-2D and T-3D
in parallel. Select the highest non-borrowing candidate, giving quotient
digit 3, 2, 1 or 0 and the associated next remainder. Do not implement
this as three serial compare/subtract operations or derive the remainder
by multiplying a quotient back by the divisor.

Statically taper the trial arithmetic: after processing W dividend bits,
T fits in W bits, with W = 2, 4, ..., 32. For each divisor multiple M,
calculate a W+1-bit unsigned difference between zero-extended T and
M[W-1:0]. A candidate is eligible only when its borrow bit is clear AND
M[33:W] is zero. This high-bit guard is essential; truncating a large
divisor multiple must never make it appear subtractable. Use constant
generate widths so synthesis sees three parallel narrow subtractors per
step, rather than a chain of full-width comparisons and subtraction.

Restore quotient sign with sign(a) XOR sign(b) for signed operations;
restore remainder sign from sign(a) alone. Explicitly preserve quotient
0xffffffff and remainder a for division by zero, and quotient 0x80000000
and remainder zero for signed INT_MIN/-1. Keep the existing per-operation
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas unchanged and exclude the real divider from
that configuration. Multiplication and all base-integer operations keep
their existing implementations.

The expected benefit is fewer dependent quotient-selection steps and
less duplicated division logic, improving the measured ALU path and
routing pressure. Extra radix-4 selection and divisor-multiple fanout
are the main timing risks. Validate real arithmetic with cocotb, run the
existing formal and stalled CoreMark cosim gates, then compare median
Gowin Fmax and fitness against the baseline. CoreMark bracketed cycles
should remain unchanged; the hypothesis succeeds only if the measured
fitness exceeds 12.12 by more than 4.6 percent with all checks intact.

changes.description:

branch with the shared sixteen-step radix-4 divmod network described
above, using unsigned sized intermediates, tapered parallel trial
subtractors with high-bit guards, and exact RV32M sign/exception
handling. Preserve the combinational module interface, every ALTOPS
formula, multiplication, and other ALU operations.

Extend real-arithmetic DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU coverage against an independent
integer reference that truncates signed division toward zero. Exercise
all sign combinations, zero divisors, INT_MIN/-1, INT_MIN divisors,
high-bit unsigned operands, powers of two and their neighbors, and
cases around D, 2D and 3D to cover all quotient digits and high-bit
rejection. Include exhaustive small unsigned operand pairs and
deterministic random full-width pairs, checking quotient and remainder
separately and checking a=q*b+r plus remainder bounds for nonexceptional
inputs. Retain all existing ALU and arithmetic invariant checks.

title: Replace combinational division with a bounded iterative execute unit
motivation:
The only recorded experiment is the baseline: fitness 12.12, median
Fmax 5.442 MHz, 12312 LUT4s, and a 199.837 ns, 156-cell worst path
through forwarding and u_ex/u_alu. No LESSONS.md or previous structural
attempts are present. The ALU currently synthesizes signed and unsigned
division and remainder as combinational / and % operators. These are a
strong candidate for the unusually deep execute path, although the
recorded module-level timing report does not identify individual operators.
Every instruction pays the resulting clock-period cost. Sharing a bounded
sequential divide/remainder datapath should substantially improve Fmax
and reduce logic area at the cost of extra cycles on DIV/REM instructions.

hypothesis.motivation:
The only recorded experiment is the baseline: fitness 12.12, median
Fmax 5.442 MHz, 12312 LUT4s, and a 199.837 ns, 156-cell worst path
through forwarding and u_ex/u_alu. No LESSONS.md or previous structural
attempts are present. The ALU currently synthesizes signed and unsigned
division and remainder as combinational / and % operators. These are a
strong candidate for the unusually deep execute path, although the
recorded module-level timing report does not identify individual operators.
Every instruction pays the resulting clock-period cost. Sharing a bounded

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make precisely one structural change: decouple DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU
from the single-cycle ALU into a shared multicycle execute resource.
Keep the existing pipeline, single retirement channel, multiplication,
branch policy, register file and memory interfaces. Implement the resource
inside alu.sv and extend its internal interface with clock/reset and a
start/completion/consume handshake so the actual unit remains directly
covered by test_alu.py. Remove synthesizable / and % operations from the
core's real arithmetic path; do not retain a combinational divider behind
an output mux or substitute results specific to CoreMark.

Use unsigned restoring division with four explicitly chained quotient-bit
steps per clock, reusing the same four subtract/select stages for eight
iteration clocks. Each step forms a 33-bit trial remainder by shifting in
the next dividend bit, subtracts the zero-extended divisor, and selects
the new remainder and quotient bit using the borrow/comparison result.
Capture post-forwarding operands and op once on start, form magnitudes
for signed operations, and retain original operands/signs for RVFI and
exception handling. The eighth iteration registers the completed unsigned
quotient and remainder and asserts completion. Apply sign correction and
quotient/remainder selection from those stable registered values during
result consumption, without an additional correction-state clock. A
completed result must remain available until EX/MEM actually accepts it.
Preserve truncation toward zero, dividend-signed remainder, divide-by-zero
results, and INT_MIN/-1 overflow exactly. Non-divide ALU operations keep
their current latency. Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS retain the exact existing
XOR constants/formulas, but use the same request, eight-cycle wait,
completion, backpressure and consumption protocol as real division.

On a valid DIV/REM in EX, hold PC and ID/EX until completion can transfer.
Launch only when the older EX/MEM instruction is not blocked by dmem.
Older instructions must drain normally: while EX waits and dmem is ready,
inject a fully inert EX/MEM bubble, clearing both valid and side-effect
controls instead of retaining and repeatedly issuing the older operation.
During an older dmem stall, hold its request and existing forwarding state
using the current memory-stall behavior. Capture the divide's forwarded
rs1/rs2 and RVFI operand values at launch so draining older stages cannot
change them. On completion transfer exactly one result and instruction
payload to EX/MEM, release the front end, and allow ordinary EX/MEM
forwarding to dependent ALU, branch and memory instructions. Prevent
repeated starts, duplicate retirements, wrong-path starts and redirects
from instructions that cannot advance. Reset cancels an outstanding divide.
Execute-busy must hold ID/EX rather than invoke the load-use bubble rule.

Keep the bounded schedule tight: one launch clock, eight iteration clocks,
then transfer on the following edge. With ready buses, consecutive divides
must retire no more than ten clocks apart, preserving the existing formal
liveness window without modifying any checker. Verify this bound with the
real and ALTOPS paths. This hypothesis trades at most nine extra execute
stall cycles per ordinary divide for a much shorter global clock period;
actual CoreMark DIV/REM frequency and remaining multiplier timing must be
measured rather than assumed. Validate using unchanged formal/cosim gates,
exact M-extension arithmetic tests and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker
checks, then compare Gowin median Fmax times measured iterations/cycle.
Accept only fitness above 12.67752, the required 4.6 percent improvement.

changes.description:
Replace all four real combinational DIV/REM cases with one shared
eight-iteration, four-bits-per-clock unsigned restoring divider and
internal start/completion/consume ports. Retain signed correction,
exception semantics and reset handling. Keep completed state stable
under backpressure. Preserve existing non-divide arithmetic and exact
ALTOPS formulas, with identical divide handshake timing in both modes.

Launch valid divides with latched forwarded operands; retain operand
metadata until transfer. Expose execute-wait to hazard control and
distinguish dmem blocking from divider waiting. Drain older EX/MEM
entries with inert bubbles while waiting, hold an older blocked memory
request, and transfer/consume each completed divide once. Gate redirect
and request issuance by valid execution and advancement conditions.

title: Early direct-control-flow prediction with a small bimodal table
motivation:
The baseline predicts every control transfer sequentially and flushes on every
taken conditional branch, JAL, or JALR. Its IF/ID bundle is combinational, so a
taken transfer normally wastes one issue opportunity, not two. CoreMark's
repeated loops and direct calls should make many of these bubbles avoidable.
The only recorded experiment is the baseline; LESSONS.md is absent and there
are no previous predictor results. The measured critical path is through
forwarding and the combinational ALU, so this proposal targets iterations per
cycle while keeping added prediction logic out of that arithmetic path.

hypothesis.motivation:
The baseline predicts every control transfer sequentially and flushes on every
taken conditional branch, JAL, or JALR. Its IF/ID bundle is combinational, so a
taken transfer normally wastes one issue opportunity, not two. CoreMark's
repeated loops and direct calls should make many of these bubbles avoidable.
The only recorded experiment is the baseline; LESSONS.md is absent and there
are no previous predictor results. The measured critical path is through
forwarding and the combinational ALU, so this proposal targets iterations per
cycle while keeping added prediction logic out of that arithmetic path.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one instruction-aware direct-control-flow predictor: a 128-entry bimodal
branch history table with two-bit saturating counters, indexed by PC[8:2],
combined with early B/J immediate target calculation. Initialize counters to
weakly not taken. For a legal conditional BRANCH, use the counter MSB to
choose between PC+4 and PC+sign_extended_B_immediate. Always predict legal
direct JAL to PC+sign_extended_J_immediate. Other instructions, including
JALR, retain sequential prediction. Fetch already exposes the instruction
combinationally to decode, so this needs no new pipeline stage, target cache,
target tags, return stack, or global history. Compute predictions from raw
imem_data and the PC, never from a flush-generated NOP. Validate BRANCH
funct3 before predicting; the authoritative decoder and trap rules remain
unchanged. Only speculate to word-aligned targets in instruction memory
[0x00000000, 0x00100000); otherwise predict PC+4 and let EX resolve normally.

Carry the exact predicted_next_pc with the instruction through IF/ID and
ID/EX. Use it for both the accepted fetch's PC update and that instruction's
metadata. Recompute the actual next PC in EX from forwarded operands and
existing trap rules, including PC+4 on misalignment. Redirect and flush only
when a valid, advancing EX instruction's actual next PC differs from its
recorded prediction. Thus a correct taken prediction accepts the target
instruction without a bubble, a falsely taken prediction returns to PC+4,
and an unpredicted taken transfer redirects to its resolved target. RVFI
pc_wdata must continue to contain the actual next PC, never the prediction.

Consume a prediction only on the same edge that ID/EX accepts its fetched
instruction: imemReady, no load-use hold, no data-memory hold, and no older
recovery. Keep PC and prediction metadata stable across holds. Defer EX
recovery while EX/MEM is held by dmem backpressure; when EX can advance,
recovery overrides an instruction-bus stall and a new prediction. Train the
resolving branch's indexed counter exactly once on valid EX advancement,
including correctly predicted branches, and never for bubbles, held
instructions, jumps, illegal instructions, or misalignment traps. Saturate
toward taken/not-taken using the resolved condition. A simultaneous read
and update may use the pre-edge table value, provided the latched prediction
is exactly the one used to update the PC. No prediction may enable a
wrong-path register write, data-memory request, or retirement.

Expect roughly 9 percent fewer bracketed CoreMark cycles, giving about
10 percent higher fitness if median Fmax stays near baseline. This is an
estimate, not a measurement: direction aliasing, imem stalls overlapping
redirect bubbles, and FPGA placement changes can reduce the benefit.
Keep the table small and the target calculation separate from the main ALU.
Acceptance still requires all existing correctness gates and measured
median-Fmax times iterations/cycle exceeding 12.12 by more than 4.6 percent.

title: Shared radix-8 combinational divider with one-hot digit selection
motivation:
The champion still uses native combinational signed/unsigned division
and remainder, and its 195.006 ns worst path crosses the ALU. The prior
micro_opt hyp-20261002-001-r1s0 replaced these with a shared tapered
radix-4 network: LUT4 use fell from 12312 to 4866, but median Fmax rose
only from 5.442 to 5.839 MHz and the worst path still had 220 cells.
That result suggests arithmetic sharing is useful but dependent digit
stages remain expensive. The iterative-divider attempt failed
the fixed retirement-liveness check, so a local combinational rewrite
offers a way to shorten the clock period without adding any stall cycles.

micro_opt hyp-20261002-001-r1s0 replaced these with a shared tapered
radix-4 network: LUT4 use fell from 12312 to 4866, but median Fmax rose
only from 5.442 to 5.839 MHz and the worst path still had 220 cells.
That result suggests arithmetic sharing is useful but dependent digit
stages remain expensive. The iterative-divider attempt failed
the fixed retirement-liveness check, so a local combinational rewrite
offers a way to shorten the clock period without adding any stall cycles.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only real DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU arithmetic in rtl/alu.sv with one
shared, explicitly unrolled unsigned radix-8 restoring divmod network.
The distinguishing optimization is eleven dependent digit stages with
parallel subtractors and a priority-free one-hot result mux, instead of
sixteen radix-4 stages or a serial bit-at-a-time divider. Preserve the
combinational ALU interface and instruction latency, the champion's
existing branch predictor, pipeline controls, and nret=1 contract.

For signed DIV/REM, convert both operands to unsigned two's-complement
magnitudes; for DIVU/REMU use the raw operands. Precompute the unsigned
multiples M[k] = k*D for k=1..7 in 35 bits, with explicit zero extension
before shifts or additions. Use wiring for D, 2D, and 4D, and parallel
shift/add or shift/sub expressions for 3D, 5D, 6D, and 7D; do not build
a serial chain of seven additions or infer multipliers for constants.

Consume dividend bits [31:30] in an initial two-bit stage, followed by
ten three-bit stages consuming [29:27] down to [2:0]. Start with R=0.
At each stage concatenate the previous remainder and the next dividend
group to form T. The total prefix width W is 2, 5, 8, ..., 32; T fits
within W bits because the previous remainder never exceeds the consumed
dividend prefix. Keep these widths static and explicit in generate
blocks so early stages use narrow arithmetic.

For each k=1..7, calculate diff[k] = {0,T} - {0,M[k][W-1:0]} in W+1
unsigned bits, all in parallel. Set ge[k] only when diff[k][W] is zero
AND M[k][34:W] is zero. The upper-bit guard must be retained even at
W=32: a truncated large divisor multiple must never be accepted.
In the first stage only k=1..3 are needed and the quotient digit is
two bits; all later stages use k=1..7 and three-bit digits.

Let K be 3 for the first stage and 7 otherwise. Define ge[0]=1 and
ge[K+1]=0. Since the exact comparisons are monotone, the winning digit
has onehot[k] = ge[k] AND NOT ge[k+1], for k=0..K. Select the next
remainder with a balanced OR reduction of onehot-masked candidates:
candidate[0]=T, candidate[k]=diff[k][W-1:0]. Generate each quotient
digit bit by OR-ing the corresponding onehot terms and concatenate
the eleven digits to form the 32-bit quotient. Do not encode a nested
priority if/else chain, perform a second subtraction after selecting
a digit, or recover the remainder with quotient-times-divisor logic.

Restore quotient sign from sign(a) XOR sign(b), and remainder sign
from sign(a), for signed operations only. Explicitly preserve divide
by zero (quotient 0xffffffff, remainder original a) and signed
INT_MIN/-1 (quotient 0x80000000, remainder zero). Retain every existing
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formula and constant exactly, with the real divider
excluded from ALTOPS builds. Leave multiplication and base-integer
arithmetic unchanged.

Fewer dependent digit stages should improve the timed ALU path while
retaining the champion's CoreMark iterations/cycle. More parallel
subtraction, divisor fanout, and wider selection can offset that gain;
this is a timing hypothesis, not a measured result. Use real-arithmetic
ALU tests plus the existing formal and stalled CoreMark cosim gates,
retaining all CRC, UART, memory, marker, and retirement checks. Measure
median Gowin Fmax and require fitness above 13.99548, which is more
than 4.6 percent above the 13.38 champion. Bracketed CoreMark cycles
should equal the champion for the same bus-stall sequence.

A width-accurate software model of this recurrence passed 45380 operand
pairs in both unsigned and signed modes, including every digit at every
stage, high-bit rejection, and one-hot uniqueness. This supports the
arithmetic construction; RTL correctness and FPGA timing remain to be
established during implementation.

title: Four-iteration shared divider with retirement-gap headroom
motivation:
The current champion scores 13.38 at 5.623 MHz, and its reported worst
path takes 195.006 ns through the register file, execute stage and ALU.
The real ALU still contains combinational signed/unsigned division and
remainder. Dividing their long dependency chain across clocks should
improve the clock period for every instruction. The module-level timing
report supports this diagnosis but does not identify individual operators.
The combinational radix-4 attempt reached only 5.839 MHz. The previous
structural attempt passed 52 of 53 formal checks, but its eight iteration
clocks plus launch/consume and a load-use bubble caused an eleven-cycle
retirement gap. LESSONS.md therefore requires budgeting the full gap,
not merely the spacing of back-to-back divides.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU's combinational implementation with a
shared four-iteration execute resource. Process eight quotient bits per
iteration clock, reusing eight chained radix-2 restoring steps across
four clocks. This single structural change trades five extra execute
stall cycles per divide for a much shorter global arithmetic path and
reduced duplicated division logic. Retain the champion's 128-entry
bimodal predictor and early JAL prediction, ordinary ALU/multiply latency,
pipeline topology outside divide control, memory contract and nret=1.

Implement the sequential divider inside alu.sv, extending its internal
interface with clock/reset and request/completion/consume signals so the
existing ALU unit-test runner exercises the actual hardware. At launch,
latch the post-forwarding operands and operation; form unsigned operand
magnitudes for signed operations and record quotient/remainder signs,
the original dividend, and exception flags. Initialize remainder to zero
and the combined dividend/quotient shift register to the magnitude of a.
Each restoring step shifts in the next most-significant dividend bit,
subtracts the zero-extended divisor from the trial remainder, and uses
that subtraction's borrow to select the next remainder and quotient bit.
Use explicitly sized unsigned intermediates and sufficient width for
the shifted remainder and borrow. Avoid separate serial comparison and
subtraction networks. Eight such steps form the reusable per-clock
combinational network; four iterations process exactly 32 dividend bits.

Use one launch edge, four iteration edges, and one transfer/consume edge.
The fourth iteration registers the final unsigned quotient/remainder
and asserts completion. Select quotient versus remainder and restore
sign from those registered results during consumption, without another
correction-state clock. Completion and its result persist until consumed.
Signed division truncates toward zero; signed remainder follows a's sign.
Explicitly return quotient 0xffffffff and remainder a for divisor zero,
and quotient 0x80000000 and remainder zero for signed INT_MIN/-1. Keep
these cases on the same bounded schedule to simplify control. Remove all
synthesizable / and % operators from the core arithmetic path. Under
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS retain the exact existing per-op formulas/constants,
capturing the stand-in result at launch but exposing it through the same
four-iteration wait and consumption protocol as real division.

Distinguish divider waiting from an older blocked data-memory request.
A valid divide launches once, only when the older EX/MEM instruction can
advance. Save its forwarded rs1/rs2 values for both arithmetic and RVFI;
do not recompute them after older forwarding sources drain. While the
divide waits, hold PC and ID/EX, allow older instructions to retire, and
inject a completely inert EX/MEM bubble when that register can advance.
Clear side-effect controls as well as valid in that bubble: the existing
memory interface and forwarding logic also inspect control fields.
Preserve the original dmem-stall behavior for an older blocked load/store,
including MEM/WB forwarding data retention and request stability. Do not
freeze or repeatedly issue the older memory operation for the whole
divide latency. Divider wait must hold ID/EX, never flush the divide via
the load-use bubble rule. When the completed result can transfer, consume
it once, release ID/fetch subject to their other stall causes, and use the
ordinary EX/MEM bypass for its consumers. Gate redirect and predictor
training by actual instruction advancement, preserve predicted_next_pc
across holds, prevent wrong-path launches, and cancel outstanding work
on reset. Retire every instruction exactly once on channel 0.

With ready buses, the intended back-to-back divide retirement spacing is
six clocks; a preceding load-use bubble adds one, leaving headroom within
the unchanged ten-cycle formal allowance. Check the entire retirement
stream, including load-use-to-divide and control-flow-to-divide sequences,
rather than asserting only consecutive-divide spacing. Run the existing
liveness check early, then all unchanged formal and cosim gates; verify
real arithmetic independently because ALTOPS does not prove division.
Stalled-bus tests must also verify eventual completion, operand stability,
precise retirement and no repeated accepted stores; their wall-clock
retirement bound must account for externally imposed stalls.

Measure canonical CoreMark bracketed cycles and median Gowin Fmax after
correctness passes. Eight full-width restoring steps can still limit
timing, and division frequency determines the cycle cost; multiplier or
fetch logic may become the next bottleneck. These are measurement risks,
not grounds for changing the checker or adding unrelated optimizations.
The hypothesis succeeds only if measured fitness exceeds the current
13.38 champion by more than 4.6 percent, i.e. exceeds 13.99548, with every
invariant and the canonical CRC/UART/marker checks intact.

title: Prediction-driven fetch ahead across execute backpressure
motivation:
The previous predictor hypothesis improved fitness to 13.38 by adding a
128-entry bimodal table and early direct-JAL targets. Its measured critical
path still runs through the execute ALU. A fresh trace of the unchanged
champion reproduces 4,202,272 bracketed CoreMark cycles and contains
2,922,016 instructions, 529,588 conditional branches and only 13,735 JALRs.
An architectural branch-trace replay estimates 54,467 direction misses
for the existing bimodal table; a larger table saves only about 15,000.
These are replay estimates, not exact pipeline misprediction counters.
Better direction or return prediction alone has insufficient cycle-saving
headroom for the required 4.6 percent gain. The valuable unused capability
of the existing predictor is producing a speculative fetch stream while
decode is blocked: today stall_if freezes the fetch PC on load-use and
data-memory stalls even when the instruction bus could deliver data.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Extend the existing predictor into a bounded fetch-ahead engine with a
four-entry FIFO of predicted instructions. Retain the existing 128x2-bit
bimodal direction table, legal direct-control-flow predecode, direct-target
calculation and EX comparison of actual_next_pc with predicted_next_pc.
The single architectural change is to let that predicted fetch stream
advance independently of decode backpressure while FIFO space remains.
This is a stream queue, with no instruction cache, address-based replay,
new direction predictor, return stack, or change to arithmetic latency.

Separate the bus fetch PC from the instruction presented to ID. Each FIFO
entry holds the existing if_id_t payload: pc, instr, predicted_next_pc and
valid. Compute each prediction from the fetch PC and raw imem_data when
that bus response is accepted. Preserve the identical predicted_next_pc
in the queued payload and fetch-PC transition; never recompute a buffered
instruction's prediction after the table changes. On an ordinary accepted
response advance the fetch PC to that prediction, even if decode is held
by load-use or an older dmem operation. Stop fetching when the FIFO is full.
Never enqueue an instruction while imemReady is zero.

Use an empty-FIFO combinational bypass so zero-wait instruction delivery
retains its current latency. ID sees the oldest buffered entry whenever
the FIFO is nonempty; otherwise it sees the current bus response only if
imemReady is high. A ready bus response consumed directly by ID is not
also enqueued. If ID cannot accept it, enqueue it once and advance the
fetch PC. When buffered ID delivery and bus acceptance occur together,
pop the old head and append the new fetched payload in order. Include the
full-FIFO simultaneous-pop/push case. A head presented during load-use or
dmem backpressure must remain intact until ID/EX actually captures it.
Keep output instruction selection independent of consume/hold decisions
so source-address hazard detection cannot form a combinational loop.

Replace the hazard unit's raw-imemReady issue decision with frontend
instruction availability. Buffered instructions may issue during an imem
stall; an empty queue with an unavailable bus injects a bubble without
consuming a slot. Keep load-use detection against the presented head,
the existing load-use bubble, dmem hold priority and MEM/WB forwarding
preservation. Pass ID acceptance/backpressure separately from bus ready
to IF; do not freeze the speculative fetch PC merely because ID is held.

An advancing EX misprediction atomically invalidates the entire younger
queue and current bypass response, redirects the fetch PC to the actual
target and bubbles ID/EX. Recovery overrides a simultaneous queue push,
pop or imem stall; an older dmem hold still defers EX recovery exactly as
today. Correct predictions preserve the queued target stream. Train the
BHT only from valid, legal, advancing EX branches, exactly once, including
correct predictions; speculative fetch and dequeue never train it. Reset
clears occupancy and restores the existing PC and table initialization.
Preserve the existing aligned, in-range speculative-target guard. At the
last in-range instruction word, suspend autonomous enqueue and fetch-PC
advancement until older queued instructions drain and ID can consume that
word directly. This bounds additional speculative lookahead while keeping
the bus at an in-range address. Recovery must still override this hold.
Preserve ordinary architectural demand/recovery behavior outside the
speculative window; do not truncate addresses, wrap the PC, or deadlock
the symbolic streams used by the unchanged liveness checker.

An isolated exploratory four-entry RTL prototype, using the unchanged
simulation harness and both bus-stall modes, reduced bracketed CoreMark
cycles from 4,202,272 to 3,980,323, a 5.28 percent reduction. It passed
canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/completion/OOB checks and stalled full-RVFI
cosim of selftest plus all three random programs. Gowin placement options
0/1/2 gave 5.305/5.617/5.617 MHz: the 5.617 MHz median implies fitness
14.1119, or 5.47 percent above 13.38. Its area was 13,468 logic cells and
1,135 registers. Two entries retained most cycle savings but reached only
5.436 MHz median and fitness 13.6196; eight entries saved just 1,282 more
cycles than four. Thus choose exactly four entries.

These are feasibility measurements of a prototype, not completed
correctness approval of the proposed implementation. Full formal and
directed boundary/backpressure verification remain required, and the
final RTL must be remeasured. With about 22 percent stalls on each bus,
the mechanism overlaps instruction-bus waiting with load-use and dmem
holds. Main risks are wrong-path queue traffic, queue-control feedback,
boundary handling and placement pressure; the measured acceptance margin
is narrow. Keep queue control outside the execute arithmetic datapath.
Preserve nret=1, all RVFI semantics and all existing correctness gates.
Acceptance requires measured median-Fmax times iterations/cycle strictly
above 13.99548, which is 4.6 percent above the 13.38 champion.

title: Four-cycle radix-4 divider with registered multiples and parallel digit selection
motivation:
The current champion scores 74.76 at a median 31.417 MHz. Its recorded
worst path runs from u_ex/u_alu/quotient_q to u_ex/u_alu/remainder_q,
with 250 cells and 37.189 ns arrival time. The four-cycle divider now
dominates timing through eight dependent restoring subtract/select
steps per clock. Shortening this local arithmetic recurrence improves
the clock period of every instruction without changing divide latency.

Prior micro_opt attempts hyp-20261002-001-r1s0 and -001-r2s0 tried fully
combinational radix-4 and radix-8 dividers. They reduced area and raised
Fmax modestly, but retained long dependent digit chains and did not win
their rounds. The accepted -002-r2s1 supplies a registered four-cycle
foundation for applying parallel digit selection to a much shorter
recurrence. LESSONS.md also records that eight iteration clocks failed
the ten-cycle retirement-gap check. Preserve the accepted four clocks.

Replace only the real divider's per-cycle arithmetic in rtl/alu.sv:
compute eight quotient bits with four radix-4 restoring steps instead
of eight radix-2 restoring steps. Preserve the existing request, busy,
done and consume interface, launch edge, four iteration edges, result
holding, reset cancellation and final sign/exception handling. This is
a local datapath optimization within the existing sequential resource.

At the existing launch edge, register the unsigned divisor magnitude D
and its 34-bit multiple 3D. Form 3D from the current launch operand's
magnitude using a zero-extended shift and add; do not calculate it from
the previous divisor_q value in a nonblocking assignment. D and 3D
remain stable until the request is consumed. Derive 2D by wiring from
the registered D. Registering 3D removes its adder from the recurrent
critical path without adding a preparation cycle. Use explicit widths
before shifting so high bits of 2D and 3D cannot be truncated.

Each iteration begins with the existing 32-bit quotient register Q and
32-bit remainder R, and applies four identical combinational steps.
A step forms the 34-bit trial T = {R, Q[31:30]}. In parallel compute
diff[k] = {1'b0,T} - {1'b0,M[k]} in 35 unsigned bits for k=1,2,3,
where the 34-bit M values are D, 2D and 3D. Let ge[k] = !diff[k][34].
The leading difference bit is the borrow; retain the full divisor
multiples for these comparisons. No separate compare followed by a
subtraction is needed.

Decode the winning digit with adjacent monotone comparisons:
select[0] = !ge[1]; select[1] = ge[1] && !ge[2];
select[2] = ge[2] && !ge[3]; select[3] = ge[3].
Select the next remainder using a balanced OR of four one-hot-masked
candidates T, diff[1], diff[2], diff[3]. The quotient digit is
{ge[2], ge[3] || (ge[1] && !ge[2])}; shift Q left two bits and append
that digit. Avoid a priority if/else chain or a second subtraction
after digit selection. After step four register the new Q and R.

For nonzero D, the invariant 0 <= R < D implies T < 4D and the selected
remainder is again below D, so only its low 32 bits need to be stored
or passed to the next step. Trial arithmetic and borrow generation
still require the full widths above. Use these widths in every reused
step; the narrow early-stage widths of the prior fully unrolled
dividers cannot simply be reused on later iteration clocks.
Division by zero still completes on the normal fixed schedule and
uses the existing explicit architectural result override.

truncation toward zero, dividend-signed remainder, INT_MIN/-1 and zero
divisor handling. Preserve the exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas and
the same four-iteration handshake in that build; keep the real radix-4
logic excluded there. Preserve multiplication, base-integer arithmetic,
pipeline controls, predictor, memory interfaces and nret=1 RVFI.

Halving the number of dependent remainder selections should outweigh
the extra parallel subtractors and improve median Gowin Fmax. Risks
are additional routing/fanout, the wider four-way result mux, and the
launch path through magnitude conversion and 3D generation. Other
paths may become limiting. The expected 20 percent fitness gain is
an estimate, not a measurement; use the unchanged vendor timing flow.

title: Retiming the shared divider to six bounded iterations
motivation:
The champion scores 74.76 at 31.417 MHz. Its measured worst path runs
from u_ex/u_alu/quotient_q to u_ex/u_alu/remainder_q, with 37.189 ns
reported arrival time: the eight dependent restoring steps inside each
divider iteration now limit the clock. The successful structural change
established that reusing division hardware across clocks is profitable.
The earlier eight-iteration version failed liveness because launch,
consume and a preceding load-use bubble exceeded the ten-cycle
retirement allowance. Six iterations offer a shorter datapath while
retaining headroom for that bubble. The previous predictor-only core
and the current divider champion both recorded 4,202,272 bracketed
CoreMark cycles, suggesting low sensitivity to divide latency in this
workload; this must be checked for the proposed implementation.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one structural change: reschedule the existing shared sequential
DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU datapath from four eight-bit iterations to six bounded
iterations with at most six dependent restoring steps per clock.
Retain the existing launch, busy, done and consume interface and the
pipeline's current execute-wait protocol. Do not add a new pipeline
stage or change multiplication, prediction, forwarding or memory policy.

Implement six unsigned restoring quotient-bit steps in the reusable
combinational chain. For iteration indices 0 through 4, register the
quotient and remainder after step 6, consuming thirty dividend bits
over five clocks. For iteration 5, register the outputs after step 2,
consuming exactly the final two bits, then deassert busy and assert
done. Widen the iteration counter to three bits. Select the step-2
versus step-6 register input by decoding the registered iteration count;
never run six effective steps on the final clock, truncate the result
afterward, or zero-pad the dividend and silently change its value.
Keep each trial at 33 bits and the existing 34-bit zero-extended
subtraction so borrow detection remains correct for high-bit divisors.

Capture forwarded operands, magnitudes, signs and exception flags once
at launch using the existing logic. Preserve RV32M divide-by-zero,
INT_MIN/-1 overflow, truncation toward zero and dividend-signed remainder.
Apply sign correction to the completed registered state during the
existing consume phase, with no additional correction clock. Completed
state must remain stable until consumed and reset must cancel it.
Retain the exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas, with the same six-iteration
busy/done timing as real arithmetic; do not shorten the formal schedule.

Keep EX's existing operand snapshots, older-instruction drainage,
inert EX/MEM bubbles, held memory requests and exactly-once result
transfer. With ready buses, a divide occupies one launch edge, six
iteration edges and one consume edge. Consecutive divides should retire
eight clocks apart, and a preceding load-use bubble should extend the
relevant retirement gap to nine clocks. Verify the entire stream,
including branch recovery and startup, against the unchanged ten-cycle
liveness check; do not infer correctness solely from consecutive divides.

An isolated prototype changed only this divider schedule and the
latency-specific unit-test expectations. Gowin placement options 0/1/2
measured 34.438/34.321/34.321 MHz, giving a 34.321 MHz median versus
31.417 MHz for the champion. Logic fell from 3,819 to 3,757 cells and
registers rose from 885 to 886. The worst path moved outside the
divider to register-file/redirect/hazard logic ending at ID/EX. This
new bottleneck limits the gain below the ideal one-third speedup from
reducing eight dependent arithmetic steps to six; keep this hypothesis
focused on divider retiming rather than also modifying that path.

for ten iterations. Its measured frequency and cycle count imply
fitness 81.6725, about 9.25 percent above 74.76. All 53 checks generated
from the unchanged single-retirement formal configuration passed,
including liveness and register consistency. These are prototype
measurements, not an
exemption from rerunning the final implementation's correctness and
median Gowin fitness gates. Require all formal checks and retain the
same real and ALTOPS schedules, arithmetic and pipeline assertions.
Preserve nret=1 and every external port and correctness invariant.
Acceptance requires measured fitness strictly above 78.19896, which
is 4.6 percent above the current 74.76 champion.

title: Compact prediction-token fetch ahead on the iterative-divider core
motivation:
The champion already predicts direct JAL and conditional branches with a
128-entry bimodal table. Prior branch-trace analysis found only about
54,467 direction misses and 13,735 JALRs in 4,202,272 bracketed cycles,
giving direction-table or return-prediction changes too little headroom
for a reliable 4.6 percent gain. The predictor can instead supply useful
future instructions while decode waits for a load-use hazard or dmem.
hyp-20261002-003-r2s2 demonstrated 3,980,323 cycles with four predicted
instructions buffered, but its 5.567 MHz median on the old combinational
divider gave only 4.56 percent higher fitness and was rejected. The new
champion retains exactly 4,202,272 cycles, but its critical path is now
internal to the iterative divider and its area is much smaller. Revisit
prediction-driven lookahead with a narrower queue to reduce the placement
pressure that erased the previous candidate's small acceptance margin.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a four-entry fall-through FIFO to the existing predictor so its fetch
PC advances independently of decode backpressure whenever an instruction
response is ready and there is queue capacity. Preserve the existing
128x2-bit BHT, early direct-JAL prediction, direct-target range checks,
exactly-once EX training and EX misprediction recovery. This is one
predictor-stream buffering change; leave arithmetic, direction policy,
memory semantics and pipeline depth intact.

The distinguishing implementation is compact prediction metadata. Each
queue entry contains the full 32-bit instruction, full 32-bit fetch PC,
and one frozen use_direct_target bit, rather than a 32-bit predicted PC.
Set that bit only when the existing legal BRANCH/JAL predecode actually
selects its aligned, in-range direct target. All other predictions are
PC+4. Reconstruct the queued instruction's exact predicted_next_pc from
its saved PC, saved instruction and saved bit at delivery to ID; do not
consult the current BHT or reinterpret its direction. This is lossless
for the present predictor, which never predicts indirect JALR targets.
Preserve full-width PC arithmetic and sign extension, including PC+4
wrap semantics. Retain the existing 32-bit predicted_next_pc in IF/ID
and ID/EX and the authoritative EX actual-next-PC comparison. Compact
entries save 124 payload bits across four slots relative to the prior
96-bit entries. Use per-entry enables and circular read/write pointers,
avoiding a wide shift of every payload on each dequeue. Reset occupancy
and pointers; unused payload need not be reset if it cannot become valid.

Keep the empty-queue combinational bypass so a ready response can issue
immediately without an added stage. With a nonempty queue, present the
oldest saved payload independently of downstream hold/consume signals.
If decode consumes a bypassed response, do not also enqueue it. If decode
is blocked, enqueue an accepted response once and advance the fetch PC
using that response's prediction. Permit simultaneous dequeue/enqueue,
including when initially full. A queued head remains intact until ID/EX
actually accepts it. Never enqueue or advance from unready imem data.
Reconstructing queued metadata must not be in the speculative fetch-PC
feedback path: keep raw-bus prediction and queued-head reconstruction
as parallel logic. Freeze the exact prediction used for each accepted
response, even on a simultaneous same-index EX BHT update.

Connect raw imemReady to this front end and give hazard control a separate
instruction-available signal. A saved head may issue while imemReady is
low. Preserve load-use bubbling against that head, dmem hold priority,
retained MEM/WB forwarding, and the champion's execute_wait handling.
Division holds ID/EX while older instructions drain; fetch ahead may
fill available slots during this hold, but cannot alter divider launch,
completion, consume or the ten-cycle formal retirement-gap contract.
Avoid combinational feedback from load-use/consume to head selection.

Keep recovery out of the payload-write enable path. Compute queue pop,
empty bypass consumption and candidate enqueue from occupancy, decode
hold and bus ready, without gating these candidates with redirect.
Similarly, head instruction bits depend only on queue occupancy and
instruction availability, not redirect; on recovery make out.valid zero
and let the existing higher-priority ID/EX flush kill that instruction.
In the PC/count/pointer sequential block, reset is highest priority and
redirect is next: redirect clears occupancy and both pointers and sets
PC to the actual target instead of applying ordinary push/pop/advance.
Payload banks may receive a write on the same recovery edge, because all
slots become invalid and every slot must be overwritten before becoming
occupied again. This separates physical payload writes from logical
acceptance; no redirected response may become a valid queued entry.
Keep payload writes suppressed during reset. This avoids the long path
EX redirect -> masked head -> load-use logic -> queue write enable while
retaining atomic recovery and simultaneous-full dequeue/enqueue.

Older dmem holds still defer EX recovery. Train only legal, nontrapping
advancing EX branches, never speculative fetches, dequeue events or held
instructions. Correct taken predictions preserve the queued target
stream. Wrong-path instructions must never generate data-memory effects,
architectural writes or retirement. Recovery overrides imem backpressure.

Preserve the existing aligned [0x00000000,0x00100000) speculative-target
guard. At the final in-range instruction word, stop autonomous enqueue
and fetch-PC advancement until the queue drains and decode can consume
that word directly. Recovery overrides this boundary hold. Do not mask,
truncate or wrap architectural addresses to implement a speculation
bound; preserve ordinary architectural demand and recovery behavior so
symbolic-stream liveness and trap semantics are unchanged.

An isolated current-champion RTL prototype of this compact queue and
recovery control reproduces 3,980,323 bracketed CoreMark cycles for ten
iterations, versus the champion's 4,202,272. The unchanged simulator
passes canonical CRC/UART, completion, bracket and bounds checks with
both stall modes enabled. All eight full-RVFI selftest/random1/random2/
random3 comparisons pass, covering ready buses and combined iStall/dStall.
Gowin placement options 0/1/2 give 30.565/31.509/31.509 MHz, a median of
31.509 MHz and estimated fitness 79.162, 5.89 percent above 74.76.
Option 0 reports 4,131 logic cells and 1,152 registers; its worst path
remains inside the unchanged divider. A first compact prototype that
gated payload writes with redirect reached only 30.757 MHz median; its
worst path crossed recovery and queue-write control, motivating the
validity-based recovery implementation specified above.

These are exploratory feasibility measurements, not completed correctness
approval. Full formal, targeted queue/boundary tests and final vendor
timing remain implementation gates. The acceptance threshold is 78.19896
iterations/second; at the measured cycle count this requires median Fmax
above approximately 31.126 MHz. Preserve all existing formal, decoder,
RV32M, RVFI, cosim, canonical CoreMark CRC/UART, bounds and timing-marker
checks. Measure the complete product and reject gains of at most 4.6
percent. No current-core arithmetic or retirement contract changes.

title: Remove recovery from the fetch-to-decode payload path
motivation:
The champion scores 81.67 at 34.321 MHz with 4,202,272 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its recorded critical path starts in the register
file and traverses execute, fetch, and hazard logic before ending at
ID/EX. LESSONS.md reports that six-iteration divider retiming moved
the bottleneck here. Prior micro_opt attempts -001-r1s0, -001-r2s0,
and -001-r3s0 concentrated on divider arithmetic; even the last one's
34.195 MHz result was limited by the register-file/recovery path.
In the current RTL, EX recovery replaces the fetched instruction with
a NOP before register addressing, decode, immediate generation and
load-use comparison. Recovery also clears the entire ID/EX payload.
These redundant wide kill dependencies needlessly lengthen a late
control path, although only validity and side-effect controls must
be squashed to prevent wrong-path execution.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one local control-cone optimization: remove flush and redirect
from the combinational instruction payload and from ID/EX payload
write enables. Carry raw imem_data through IF/ID even on a killed or
unavailable fetch, and implement bubbles at the ID/EX validity and
control boundary. Keep every pipeline stage, branch prediction policy,
instruction latency, divider schedule and external handshake intact.

In if_stage, drive out.instr directly from imem_data, retaining the
existing out.valid qualification and prediction metadata. Preserve
reset and redirect priority in the PC update, including recovery
while imemReady is low. Raw payload bits on an invalid bundle are
irrelevant; the instruction must never acquire live controls.

In id_stage, separate payload capture from squash control. Reset
retains its defined initialization. Otherwise capture pc, prediction,
operands, immediate, register addresses and instruction whenever
!stall, without qualifying this payload enable or zeroing these
fields with flush, redirect or in.valid. For ctrl and valid only,
preserve priority: reset clears; flush clears even if stall is also
asserted; otherwise stall holds; otherwise a valid fetch captures
decoded controls and valid=1, and an invalid fetch captures ctrl='0
and valid=0. A stalled instruction's full payload and controls remain
stable. Clearing controls as well as valid is essential because the
existing memory, hazard and forwarding logic examines controls without
universally gating them by validity. Do not change legal decoding or
rely on valid alone to suppress writes, memory requests or forwarding.

In hazard_unit, compare the now-raw source fields for load-use, with
imem_ready qualifying that dependency. Do not gate the source fields
or dependency comparison with redirect, flush_if or out.valid: those
would reintroduce recovery into the operand-selection path. Recovery
already overrides PC hold, and flush_id already overrides ID/EX hold
when EX advances. Preserve dmem and execute-wait hold priority and
the existing exactly-one-cycle real load-use interlock. This removes
the serial redirect-to-NOP-to-address/decode/hazard path without adding
a register, changing prediction accuracy, or removing a real hazard.

A small RTL prototype of exactly these three module changes measured
Gowin Fmax of 39.888, 40.357 and 40.357 MHz for placement options 0, 1
and 2: median 40.357 MHz versus the champion's 34.321 MHz. Logic use
fell from 3,757 to 3,656 and registers remained 886. The reported
worst path moved to the existing divider recurrence, supporting the
proposed removal of recovery from the payload path. Leave that divider
unchanged; this hypothesis is solely the local squash optimization.

The prototype passed lint and the existing pipeline suite in real and
ALTOPS modes, including sixteen additional combinations of killed raw
instructions and imem availability while an older store is stalled.
Selftest and all three random programs passed full-RVFI cosimulation
with and without bus stalls. Canonical stalled CoreMark passed CRC,
UART, OOB and marker validation and retained 4,202,272 bracketed cycles
for ten iterations. The measured median Fmax and cycles imply fitness
96.036, approximately 17.59 percent above the 81.67 champion. All 53
checks from the unchanged single-retirement formal configuration
passed, including register consistency and liveness. These prototype
results do not replace final implementation verification.

and stalled RVFI cosimulation
including canonical CoreMark CRCs, UART, address bounds and markers.

backpressure, checking no wrong-path side effects, no duplicate

title: Separate pipeline validity from payload to shorten redirect recovery
motivation:
The champion reaches 81.67 iterations/second at 34.321 MHz with
4,202,272 bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md and the structural
history show that six divider iterations removed the original
arithmetic bottleneck. The new worst path runs from register-file
storage through execute, fetch recovery and hazard logic into ID/EX,
with 34.332 ns reported arrival time and 51 logic cells. Redirect
currently forces a NOP onto the combinational instruction bundle and
clears the entire ID/EX payload, coupling late branch resolution to
instruction decode, register addresses and wide pipeline input muxes.
This is now a more promising structural target than further extending
division, whose latency is constrained by the ten-cycle liveness check.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one structural change: represent pipeline occupancy independently
of instruction payload and enforce side effects at valid instruction
boundaries. Remove the combinational redirect-to-NOP-to-decode path
and the requirement to clear wide payload registers when squashing an
instruction. Keep the present stage count, prediction policy, divider
schedule, single retirement channel and memory protocol.

Drive the combinational IF/ID instruction directly from imem_data.
An unavailable fetch is represented by validity, not a replacement
instruction. EX recovery updates PC with highest nonreset priority
and clears ID/EX validity; it must not change the instruction bits,
register-file read addresses, immediate or decoded data in that cycle.
Keep predictor targets and metadata paired with each accepted PC.
Correct predictions still have no recovery bubble, and mispredictions
still squash exactly the same younger instruction as today.

Split ID/EX payload updates from its valid-bit update. Reset or a
permitted flush clears validity. An older dmem hold or active divide
retains the current instruction. A load-use bubble clears validity
while preserving payload; ordinary issue captures raw payload and
fetch validity. No redirect-driven mux or clear may remain on the
operand, immediate, source-register or instruction payload flops.
Payload reset may remain for deterministic simulation, independently
of recovery. Apply the same valid/payload separation to EX/MEM bubbles
while older instructions drain during a divide.

Because invalid entries can now contain real control bits, qualify
every architectural action and hazard with the owning entry's
validity: load-use detection, EX/MEM memory blocking and requests,
register writes, forwarding eligibility, divider launch, redirects,
predictor updates and RVFI retirement. Invalid entries cannot start
a divide, issue a store, forward a destination or create a stall.
Load-use source comparisons should use raw instruction addresses;
do not recreate the recovery path by gating them with redirect.
PC recovery overrides any fetch-side stall, and older memory/divide
holds retain priority over bubble insertion as in the current core.

Preserve the special held-WB forwarding behavior explicitly. During
a dmem stall the previous WB entry stops retiring but its value may
still be needed by the held EX instruction. Add a separate forwarding
ownership bit, captured from valid incoming MEM instructions and
retained with the WB payload during a dmem hold. Use this bit plus
reg_write and nonzero rd for WB bypass eligibility; never replace it
with the retirement pulse alone. Clear ownership on a normal incoming
bubble and reset. Continue EX/MEM-over-WB priority, x0 semantics and
exact forwarded operand snapshots for a launched divide.

A prototype of exactly this restructuring measured Gowin placement
options 0/1/2 at 39.820/40.482/40.482 MHz, giving a 40.482 MHz median
versus the champion's 34.321 MHz. Option 0 used 3,727 logic cells and
887 registers, versus 3,757 and 886 previously. Its worst path moved
back into the unchanged divider, from quotient_q to remainder_q,
with 30.407 ns arrival time. This supports the proposed removal of
recovery fanout rather than merely relying on placement variation.

The prototype passed lint, both real and ALTOPS pipeline suites,
and all 53 checks from the unchanged single-retirement formal
configuration, including liveness and register consistency. Full
RVFI selftest and all three random programs passed both with and
without bus stalls. Canonical stalled CoreMark passed CRC, UART,
address-bound and marker checks, retiring ten benchmark iterations
in exactly 4,202,272 bracketed cycles. Combining that cycle count
with median vendor Fmax gives fitness 96.3336, 17.95 percent above
the 81.67 champion. The prototype RTL is restored after measurement;
this file specifies the implementation to reproduce and revalidate.

Preserve the narrow prototype scope: raw fetch payload, independent
ID/EX validity, valid-only divide bubbles, valid-qualified hazards
and side effects, and one extra retained WB forwarding-valid bit.
Do not expand the change into a stage addition or a divider redesign;
the newly limiting divider sets a practical ceiling on this proposal.
These measurements do not replace the final implementation's formal,
cosim and median Gowin evaluation. Acceptance requires measured
fitness strictly above 85.42682, 4.6 percent above the 81.67 champion.
Preserve all decoder legality checks, real and ALTOPS arithmetic,
ten-cycle liveness coverage, nret=1 ports and every hard invariant.

title: Direction-token prediction recovery with a shallow squash path
motivation:
The champion reaches 81.67 iterations/second at 34.321 MHz and 4,202,272
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its latest reported critical path runs from
register-file data through execute, fetch recovery and hazard control to
ID/EX. The existing predictor compares a fully selected 32-bit actual
next PC against a saved predicted PC, then masks fetch instruction bits
with redirect before those bits feed load-use detection and decode.
Earlier predictor work already removed most control-transfer bubbles;
the two fetch-ahead proposals saved cycles but lost their acceptance
margin to frequency and placement costs. Shortening prediction recovery
is therefore more promising than another larger predictor or queue.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace full-next-PC comparison for direct control transfers with an
exact direction-token recovery predicate, and make recovery squash
ID/EX through validity/control priority rather than through the fetched
instruction's 32-bit data path. This is one predictor-recovery change:
retain the 128-entry bimodal table, its update policy, early direct JAL
prediction, the current pipeline, and the six-iteration divider.

IF emits a predicted_direct bit that records whether the existing
validated BRANCH/JAL prediction actually selected its direct target,
including the current word-alignment and [0,0x00100000) target guard.
Capture it with the instruction on the same edge that updates fetch PC;
hold it during ID/EX stalls and clear it on reset or squash. Do not use
a fresh table lookup at resolution. Record direct_is_fallthrough in ID
from the decoded B/J immediate equaling 32'd4, so a direct target equal
to PC+4 never causes a spurious redirect. Retain saved predicted_next_pc
initially for validation; remove it from timed direct-recovery logic.

In EX compute actual_direct = !misalign_fault &&
(in.ctrl.is_branch ? branch_cond : direct_jal), where direct_jal is a
legal direct jump, not JALR. For legal direct BRANCH/JAL instructions,
misprediction is (actual_direct XOR predicted_direct) AND
!direct_is_fallthrough. Their target is a deterministic function of the
same saved PC and instruction, so this is equivalent to comparing the
two next PCs, including target-range fallback and misalignment traps.
JALR remains predicted sequentially: use a separate full-width
indirect_miss = in.ctrl.is_jalr && !misalign_fault &&
(jump_target != in.pc + 32'd4). This is equivalent to its old comparison
but avoids feeding the selected actual-next-PC mux into recovery enable.
Ordinary instructions cannot redirect.
Select these predicates using decoded instruction kind, independently
of the 32-bit actual-next-PC mux. Keep redirect gated by valid EX
advancement, reset, older dmem holds and execute_wait exactly as today.
The actual target arithmetic and architectural PC/RVFI semantics stay
full width and unchanged; the target still drives the recovery PC input.

Remove redirect from IF instruction-bit masking. Raw instruction bits
may reach combinational decode on a recovery cycle, but recovery must
invalidate that instruction and synchronously clear ID/EX controls and
validity with priority over load-use. On unavailable imem, retain the
existing NOP/invalid handling, independently of redirect. Set
hazard_unit.flush_if = !imem_ready so redirect cannot reach source-
address extraction through flush_if; retain IF out.valid =
!(flush || redirect) and out.instr = flush ? NOP : imem_data.
A load-use indication on a wrong-path
instruction is harmless only if recovery overrides PC hold and the
ID/EX bubble overrides load-use hold. Preserve dmem and divide hold
priority, deferred EX recovery, exactly-once BHT updates, and MEM/WB
forwarding retention. No wrong-path operation may enter EX/MEM or
generate a register write, memory request, or retirement. Do not add a
registered recovery stage or another redirect bubble.

title: Three radix-4 steps per clock in the six-iteration divider
motivation:
The champion scores 96.28 iterations/second at 40.459 MHz with
4,202,272 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path runs from
divisor_q to remainder_q entirely inside u_ex/u_alu, with 185 cells
and 30.5 ns arrival time. The six dependent restoring subtract/select
steps now limit timing after direction-token recovery shortened the
previous register-file/redirect path. The r3s0 micro_opt attempt used
four radix-4 steps per clock and reached 34.195 MHz, but its worst path
was outside the divider in the then-unoptimized recovery cone. That
result supports revisiting radix-4 on the current six-iteration design:
only three dependent digit selections are needed per clock, and the
previous external bottleneck has been removed. Increasing divide
latency risks the established ten-cycle liveness limit.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real divider's intra-cycle recurrence in rtl/alu.sv
with three radix-4 restoring digit steps, leaving its request/busy/done/
consume protocol and exact six-iteration schedule unchanged. Process
six quotient bits on each of the first five iteration clocks and two
bits on the sixth. This is a local arithmetic optimization, with no
added pipeline stage, preparation cycle or change in issue behavior.

At the existing launch edge capture the unsigned divisor magnitude D
and its 34-bit multiple 3D. Compute 3D from the current launch operand's
magnitude, not from the previous divisor_q value. Zero-extend before
shifting or adding; 3*0xffffffff must not overflow the chosen width.
Derive 2D by wiring from D. Hold D and 3D until completion is consumed.
Registering 3D removes its addition from the recurrent timing path.

Each radix-4 step takes a 32-bit remainder R and quotient register Q,
forms the 34-bit trial T={R,Q[31:30]}, and computes three 35-bit
unsigned differences diff[k]={1'b0,T}-{1'b0,M[k]} in parallel,
where M[1]=D, M[2]=2D and M[3]=3D are explicitly 34 bits. Define
ge[k]=!diff[k][34]. Keep these full widths in every reused step;
prefix-width tapering from a fully unrolled divider is inapplicable.
Select the digit with one-hot enables s0=!ge[1],
s1=ge[1]&&!ge[2], s2=ge[2]&&!ge[3], s3=ge[3]. Form the next remainder
as a balanced OR of the four masked candidates T[31:0],
diff[1][31:0], diff[2][31:0], diff[3][31:0]. Append quotient digit
{ge[2], ge[3]||(ge[1]&&!ge[2])} to Q[29:0]. Avoid a priority mux
or another subtraction after digit selection. For D!=0, R<D gives
T<4D and guarantees the selected remainder fits in 32 bits.

Chain exactly three such steps. On iteration indices 0 through 4,
register the step-3 quotient and remainder. On index 5 register the
step-1 tap, processing precisely the final two bits, then assert done
exactly as today. Division by zero follows the same bounded schedule
and keeps its existing explicit result override. Preserve signed
magnitude conversion, truncation toward zero, dividend-signed
remainder, INT_MIN/-1, result retention and reset cancellation.
Preserve every RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formula and the six-clock handshake
in that build; exclude real digit arithmetic from ALTOPS. Leave all
other ALU operations, pipeline controls, prediction, RVFI and nret=1
unchanged.

An isolated RTL prototype of exactly this change measured Gowin Fmax
of 49.216, 49.411 and 49.411 MHz across placement options 0/1/2, giving
a 49.411 MHz median. Option 0 used 4,020 logic cells and 890 registers,
versus the champion's 3,697 and 857. The reported divider path fell to
25.611 ns arrival time with 95 cells, nearly tied with a 25.613 ns
register-file-to-memory path. This supports a real reduction in the
divider recurrence depth, while showing the next external timing limit.

The prototype passed lint and the expanded ALU and existing pipeline
suites in both real and ALTOPS configurations. Full-RVFI selftest and
three random programs passed with ready buses and with combined bus
stalls. Canonical stalled CoreMark passed CRC, UART, address-bound and
marker validation, retaining exactly 4,202,272 bracketed cycles for
ten iterations. Combined with the median vendor frequency this implies
fitness 117.5816, approximately 22.12 percent above the 96.28 champion.
All 53 checks from the unchanged single-retirement formal configuration
passed, including liveness and register consistency. That formal run
uses ALTOPS; real arithmetic was exercised by the expanded ALU vectors
and cosimulation, not claimed proven by the ALTOPS checks. The temporary
prototype RTL and test edits were restored after measurement.
These measurements are prototype evidence; the final implementation
must rerun correctness gates and median vendor timing.

The parallel subtractors and four-way selection increase area/fanout,
and magnitude-to-3D generation can become a new launch path. Keep the
proposal limited to this arithmetic change. Validate real and ALTOPS
ALU tests, existing pipeline and retirement-gap tests, unchanged formal
and stalled full-RVFI cosim, and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/address/
marker checks. Preserve every invariant and the nret=1 contract.
Acceptance requires measured fitness strictly above 100.70888, more
than 4.6 percent above 96.28; at unchanged cycles this needs median
Fmax above 42.320611 MHz.

and its final-iteration step-2 versus step-6 mux disappears. Do not
add an iteration: even though seven iterations might fit some steady-
state gaps, the existing first-instruction divide test already uses
the complete startup allowance with six.

Let A and D be the unsigned operand magnitudes already computed at
launch, and P=A[31:30]. Compute the initial two-bit quotient Qp and
remainder Rp of P divided by D using a small exact predecode. For
D=1 use Qp=P,Rp=0; for D=2 use Qp={0,P[1]},Rp={0,P[0]}; for D=3
use Qp=(P==3 ? 1 : 0),Rp=(P==3 ? 0 : P). For D>=4 use Qp=0,Rp=P.
Classify small divisors only when D[31:2]==0: truncating a large
divisor to its low bits would be incorrect. For D=0 use Qp=3,Rp=P,
matching the original restoring recurrence before exception override.
Initialize quotient_q={A[29:0],Qp} and remainder_q=zero_extend(Rp).
Initialize divisor_q and all existing metadata as before. Express
this prefix as a small case/compare network, not division operators
or two full-width subtractors on the operand-forwarding path.

Every busy edge, including the sixth and last, now captures step 5.
Keep 33-bit trial remainders and 34-bit zero-extended differences with
correct borrow detection. Do not shift in extra padding or discard
effective quotient steps. Preserve signed quotient/remainder
correction, divide-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1 results. Completion and
result must remain stable until consumed, and reset must cancel work.
The real and RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS branches must have identical six-
iteration handshake timing, with all existing ALTOPS formulas intact.
Keep EX's operand snapshots, held memory requests, older-instruction
drainage and exactly-once transfer unchanged. Preserve nret=1 and all
top-level ports, decoder checks, prediction, multiplication and memory
behavior.

Keep every existing latency assertion: six busy iteration clocks,
eight-clock consecutive divide retirement spacing, nine-clock
load-use/recovery-to-divide gaps, and the ten-clock first-instruction
divide check. Run the unchanged liveness check and full pipeline
tests in real and ALTOPS configurations. The external cycle schedule
is unchanged, so CoreMark should retain 4,202,272 marker-bracketed
cycles; verify this experimentally.

A prototype of this exact redistribution measured Gowin placement
options 0/1/2 at 46.994/48.327/48.327 MHz, a 48.327 MHz median
versus the champion's 40.459 MHz. Option 0 used 3,612 logic cells
and 857 registers, versus 3,697 and 857 for the champion. Its worst
path remains divider remainder feedback, now 26.574 ns and 156 cells;
nearby register-file/multiplier and recovery paths limit further gain.
Stalled canonical CoreMark retained exactly 4,202,272 bracketed cycles
for ten iterations and passed CRC, UART, completion, address-bound
and timing-marker validation. The measured product gives fitness
115.0021, approximately 19.45 percent above 96.28.

The prototype passed lint, both real and ALTOPS ALU/pipeline suites
with every original latency assertion intact, all 53 unchanged
single-retirement formal checks, and all eight full-RVFI comparisons
of selftest plus three random programs with ready and stalled buses.
Added real-arithmetic tests exercise every leading dividend pair and
small-divisor class, high-bit divisor aliases and signed magnitudes.
A separate combinational SAT miter proved the actual launch-prefix
logic equivalent to two original restoring steps for every 32-bit
unsigned dividend and divisor, including zero. This local equivalence
proof complements the arithmetic tests; the normal formal suite still
uses ALTOPS and is not a full formal-deep arithmetic proof.
Prototype RTL and test edits are restored after measurement; reproduce
the specified change and rerun the final implementation's gates.

Validate real arithmetic, matching ALTOPS protocol, unchanged formal
and full-RVFI cosim, and canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/marker
checks. Measure median vendor Fmax times actual iterations/cycle.
Acceptance requires fitness above 100.70888, more than 4.6 percent
above 96.28. At unchanged cycles this requires Fmax above 42.3206 MHz.
The main risks are moving the critical path into the launch magnitude
and prefix-selection logic, another path outside the divider becoming
limiting, and placement variation offsetting the shorter feedback
chain. Keep the proposal confined to this divider work redistribution.

title: Fixed-head predicted fetch queue with direct-token recovery
motivation:
The current predictor stops fetching whenever decode waits on a load-use
dependency, data memory, or division, wasting instruction-bus acceptance
opportunities. The earlier four-entry predicted-stream queues reduced
bracketed CoreMark cycles from 4,202,272 to 3,980,323, but their final
fitness missed acceptance. The champion now has shallow direction-token
recovery and keeps redirect out of source-address masking. A compact
queue with a fixed head can exploit that improvement while avoiding an
indexed queue-read mux ahead of decode and register-file access.

hypothesis.motivation:
The current predictor stops fetching whenever decode waits on a load-use
dependency, data memory, or division, wasting instruction-bus acceptance
opportunities. The earlier four-entry predicted-stream queues reduced
bracketed CoreMark cycles from 4,202,272 to 3,980,323, but their final
fitness missed acceptance. The champion now has shallow direction-token
recovery and keeps redirect out of source-address masking. A compact
queue with a fixed head can exploit that improvement while avoiding an
indexed queue-read mux ahead of decode and register-file access.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add exactly four entries of predicted instruction fetch-ahead buffering
to the current frontend. Preserve the 128-entry bimodal direction table,
early direct JAL prediction, legal predecode and target guards. The one
architectural change is buffering the predicted stream while decode is
blocked. Do not change the divider, pipeline depth, direction policy,
indirect-jump policy, architectural memory semantics or retirement width.

Each entry stores only the full 32-bit instruction, full 32-bit PC and
frozen predicted_direct bit. Use a fixed head in entry zero and compact
entries toward the head on a dequeue, rather than reading a circular
array through a pointer-indexed payload mux. Decode selects entry zero
when occupied, otherwise the raw bus response. Empty-queue fall-through
must preserve present zero-wait issue latency. The saved direction bit
reaches EX unchanged and uses the champion's direction-XOR recovery with
its offset +4 exception. Existing predicted_next_pc may be reconstructed
from a queued entry only as verification metadata; it must not feed the
timed recovery or autonomous fetch-PC path. Never redo a BHT lookup for
a queued instruction. Keep full-width PC arithmetic and target semantics.

Separate fetch bus readiness from instruction availability at decode.
Availability is queue_nonempty OR io_imemReady. Give IF the decode hold
for load-use, dmem backpressure and execute_wait, independently of raw
instruction-bus readiness. With a saved head, decode can issue even when
io_imemReady is zero. Compute source addresses and head selection without
dependence on dequeue/hold so load-use detection has no combinational
feedback. Preserve load-use bubbling, older dmem hold priority and the
retained MEM/WB forwarding fields.

Candidate consumption is availability AND NOT decode_hold. Pop only
when consuming a buffered head. Accept a raw bus response only when
io_imemReady and either occupancy is below four or a simultaneous pop
creates space. Bypass a response directly when the queue is empty and
decode consumes it; otherwise append it once. Append index is old count
minus pop. Support full simultaneous pop/push: old entries 1..3 move to
0..2 and the new response becomes entry 3. For each entry give an append
write priority over its shift write. No queue-valid entry may be created
from an unavailable response. Advance the fetch PC using the prediction
of the raw response actually accepted, even while decode is held.

Keep recovery out of payload movement and ordinary acceptance candidate
logic. Candidate shifts/appends may physically write on a recovery edge,
but reset then redirect take priority over ordinary PC/count updates.
Redirect sets the fetch PC to the actual target, atomically empties the
queue and synchronously squashes ID/EX controls and validity. A payload
write on that edge remains unreachable; each new occupied entry must
have been overwritten since the clear. Do not reset unused payload banks.
Keep raw/head instruction masking dependent only on availability, never
redirect. An older dmem hold still defers EX recovery, while a permitted
recovery overrides an instruction-bus stall. Correct predictions retain
the queued stream. Train the BHT only on the current exactly-once legal,
nontrapping EX advancement event, never fetch, dequeue or held execution.

Preserve the current aligned [0x00000000,0x00100000) speculative-target
guard. At fetch PC 0x000ffffc, prohibit autonomous enqueue/PC advance
until the queue is empty and decode can consume that response directly.
Continue draining older entries and allow recovery to override this
boundary hold. Preserve ordinary architectural demand/recovery behavior
outside the speculative window, full-width PC wrapping and formal
liveness; never clamp, mask or alias architectural addresses.

An isolated RTL prototype of this fixed-head queue on the current
champion measured 3,980,323 bracketed cycles for ten CoreMark iterations
with both bus-stall modes enabled. The unchanged canonical CRC/UART,
completion, timing-marker and bounds validators passed. All eight
full-RVFI selftest/random1/random2/random3 comparisons passed, covering
ready buses and combined iStall/dStall. Gowin placement options 0/1/2
measured 39.566/40.210/40.210 MHz, median 40.210 MHz. This implies
fitness 101.02195, 4.925 percent above 96.28. Option zero used 3,960
logic cells and 1,120 registers; its worst path remained inside the
unchanged divider. These are prototype feasibility measurements, not
approval of the eventual implementation.

Both real-arithmetic and ALTOPS pipeline suites passed, 32 cocotb cases
each, with observation-only adaptations distinguishing bus fetch from
queued-head delivery. Architectural assertions were retained. Additional
directed cases passed for a divide filling the queue before a redirect
squashes buffered stores, and a divide near the final instruction-memory
word followed by an in-range jump back; no OOB fetch or wrong-path store
occurred under ready buses or deterministic bus stalls.
All 53 checks from the unchanged single-retirement formal configuration
passed, including register consistency, PC flow, uniqueness and liveness.

The measured margin is narrow: at this cycle count, median Fmax must
exceed 40.08539 MHz to clear acceptance. Queue enables, head bypass and
added placement pressure remain timing risks. Require unchanged formal,
real/ALTOPS unit, full-RVFI cosim and canonical stalled CoreMark checks
on the final implementation. Score median Gowin Fmax times iterations/
cycle and accept only fitness above 100.70888, more than 4.6 percent
above 96.28. Preserve nret=1 and every existing invariant.
