title: Move M-extension selection ahead of arithmetic
motivation:
The champion scores 115.00 at median Gowin Fmax 48.327 MHz and
4,202,272 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst path crosses five
restoring subtract/select steps, while prior r5s0 timing exposed a
nearly tied register-file/multiplier/result-selection path. Local
prototypes confirm that shortening only division reaches 49.619 MHz
and moves the bottleneck into multiplication, below the required
50.54913 MHz threshold. Sharing only multiplication leaves division
limiting. The promising angle is one coordinated ALU mapping change:
move wide M-extension result selection to the arithmetic inputs,
addressing both limiting paths without changing instruction latency.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 115.00 at median Gowin Fmax 48.327 MHz and
4,202,272 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst path crosses five
restoring subtract/select steps, while prior r5s0 timing exposed a
nearly tied register-file/multiplier/result-selection path. Local
prototypes confirm that shortening only division reaches 49.619 MHz
and moves the bottleneck into multiplication, below the required
50.54913 MHz threshold. Sharing only multiplication leaves division
limiting. The promising angle is one coordinated ALU mapping change:
move wide M-extension result selection to the arithmetic inputs,
addressing both limiting paths without changing instruction latency.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Eliminate late wide result selection in the existing M-extension ALU.
Use non-restoring division to replace each subtract-and-restore mux
with one selected-divisor addition, and use operand sign extension
to select multiplication semantics before one shared product. Both
are local arithmetic substitutions in alu.sv: keep the pipeline,
launch plus six iteration clocks, consume protocol and nret=1 intact.

Retain the current exact two-bit launch prefix, signed input magnitude
conversion, quotient initialization and exception metadata. Widen the
running remainder to 33 bits, interpreted as two's-complement signed.
At the same launch edge capture D as today and negative_divisor_q =
33'b0 - {1'b0,D}; compute it from the current operand magnitude, never
the old divisor register. Initialize the remainder by zero-extending
the existing two-bit remainder_prefix into 33 bits.

Each busy clock still consumes five dividend bits, through five serial
combinational non-restoring steps. For each step, choose the 33-bit
addend from the incoming remainder sign: +D when R[32]=1, otherwise
the registered -D. Compute Rnext = {R[31:0],Q[31]} + addend in exactly
33 bits and Qnext = {Q[30:0],!Rnext[32]}. Capture step 5 on each of
the six busy edges and assert done at iteration index 5 as before.
There is no wide restore mux after each addition. For nonzero D the
invariant is -D <= signed(R) < D; its corrected unsigned remainder
is R+D if R is negative, otherwise R. The 33-bit modular arithmetic
represents each next signed remainder exactly, even when shifting R
momentarily needs more bits before the addend cancels them.

Apply that final correction combinationally to the REM/REMU magnitude
before the existing dividend-sign correction. Quotient bits are already
in ordinary binary, so DIV/DIVU need no quotient conversion. Preserve
explicit division-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1 overrides, all result retention,
reset cancellation, repeated-request rejection and fixed completion
timing. Do not add a preparation or final-correction cycle.

Replace mul_ss, mul_uu and mul_su with one signed 33-by-33 multiplication.
Set Aext={signed_a && a[31],a}, with signed_a true only for MULH/MULHSU;
set Bext={signed_b && b[31],b}, with signed_b true only for MULH. Declare
both extended operands signed [32:0] and their product signed [65:0].
MUL reads product[31:0]; MULH, MULHU and MULHSU all read product[63:32].
The two extra product bits are intentionally unused. This covers the
complete unsigned operand range and signed high products without a
post-product correction subtractor or selection among three products.
MUL's low half is identical for every signedness interpretation.

Preserve every RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formula and the same handshake in
that build; exclude real divider arithmetic there. Keep all non-M ALU
operations, EX operand snapshots, bus holds, branch prediction, memory
behavior, decoder checks, RVFI ports/order and retirement-gap limits.
This hypothesis changes arithmetic mapping only, with no extra stages
or instructions in flight and no contract or evaluation changes.

The benefit should come from eliminating repeated wide restore muxes
and reducing multiplier resources and output selection. Independent
prototypes measured two DSP blocks for the shared product versus six
originally, and exposed why both limiting cones need the same treatment.
The combined prototype measured Gowin placement options 0/1/2 at
48.912/50.687/50.687 MHz, a 50.687 MHz median. Option 0 used 3,561
logic cells, 890 registers and two DSP blocks, versus the champion's
3,612 logic cells, 857 registers and six DSP blocks. The worst option-0
divider path was 25.739 ns, nearly tied with a 25.721 ns multiplier
path. Canonical stalled CoreMark passed CRC, UART, address-bound and
marker checks and retained exactly 4,202,272 bracketed cycles. The
product implies fitness 120.6181, a 4.885 percent improvement over
115.00. This narrowly exceeds the required 4.6 percent margin; final
implementation timing must reproduce it before acceptance.

The prototype passed lint and all eight existing real/ALTOPS ALU and
pipeline test configurations, preserving every latency assertion.
Selftest and three random programs passed full-RVFI cosimulation with
ready buses and combined bus stalls. Of the 53 unchanged single-retirement
formal checks, 52 passed, including liveness; reg_ch0 was still solving
at the proposal cutoff. The complete formal gate is therefore not yet
claimed passed. Temporary prototype RTL edits were restored after the
measurements. Risks include the final remainder
correction/sign path, launch negation, sign-control fanout and placement
variation. These are prototype measurements, not final implementation
acceptance; rerun the unchanged correctness and median timing gates.

A local combinational SAT miter proved the non-restoring step's quotient
decision and corrected remainder equivalent to the original restoring
step for arbitrary nonzero D, R<D, incoming quotient bit and either
signed representation of R. This does not prove the full multiplier
or replace real-arithmetic testing. Validate both real and ALTOPS ALU
and pipeline suites, unchanged formal, stalled full-RVFI cosimulation,
and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/address/marker checks. Retain every
six-iteration and startup/retirement-gap assertion. The identical cycle
schedule should preserve 4,202,272 bracketed cycles. Require measured
fitness strictly above 120.29, more than 4.6 percent above 115.00.

with alternating non-restoring remainder signs, final negative
remainders, exact division, maximum unsigned divisors, signed
extremes, zero divisors and delayed consumption. Exercise shared
multiplier signedness with every sign combination, high-bit unsigned
operands and negative-by-unsigned products. Use independent integer
references and seeded full-width random operands for every M op;
retain reset, repeated-request and ALTOPS coverage.

title: Separate arithmetic completion from the memory pipeline
motivation:
The champion scores 115.00 at 48.327 MHz with 4,202,272 CoreMark cycles.
Its five-step restoring-divider feedback remains the worst reported path,
at 26.574 ns and 156 cells. Prior structural retiming improved frequency,
but r1s1 showed that eight iterations followed by ordinary EX/MEM/WB transit
violate the ten-cycle retirement limit. The current first-instruction divide
also exhausts the startup allowance. Instead of adding latency to that same
route, a divide-specific completion-to-retirement route can reclaim the two
downstream transit cycles after all older instructions have drained.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 115.00 at 48.327 MHz with 4,202,272 CoreMark cycles.
Its five-step restoring-divider feedback remains the worst reported path,
at 26.574 ns and 156 cells. Prior structural retiming improved frequency,
but r1s1 showed that eight iterations followed by ordinary EX/MEM/WB transit
violate the ten-cycle retirement limit. The current first-instruction divide
also exhausts the startup allowance. Instead of adding latency to that same
route, a divide-specific completion-to-retirement route can reclaim the two
downstream transit cycles after all older instructions have drained.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one structural change: specialize execution into an arithmetic
completion route and a dedicated effective-address pipeline. Give the
blocking divider a direct completion-to-retirement route, and spend its
reclaimed downstream cycles on eight iterations of four restoring steps.
Other instructions retain their current pipeline latency. This couples the shortened divider datapath to the retirement
route that makes its latency legal; it is not an independent optimization
of prediction, memory policy or multiplication.

At launch capture the forwarded operands, magnitudes, signs, original dividend
and exception flags as today. Initialize quotient_q to the full unsigned
dividend magnitude and remainder_q to zero; remove launch-prefix arithmetic.
Reuse four full-width unsigned restoring steps on each of eight busy edges,
processing exactly 32 bits. Keep 33-bit trial remainders, 34-bit differences
and correct borrow detection. Assert done after iteration index 7. Apply
signed result correction from completed registered state, preserving all
RV32M divide-by-zero, signed-overflow and remainder rules. Preserve matching
eight-iteration request/busy/done/consume behavior under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS,
including all existing stand-in formulas. Reset cancels outstanding work.

When a valid divide is done and may advance, present its completed result and
saved instruction/operand metadata directly at the existing single-channel
retirement and register-file write boundary. Do not send a second copy through
EX/MEM or MEM/WB: EX/MEM must capture an inert bubble on both waiting and
consumption cycles. Select normal MEM/WB until the divide completion is valid.
Older memory operations still block launch until accepted, and older pipeline
entries drain during the eight iterations, so normal WB and divide completion
cannot legitimately overlap. Assert this exclusion in tests and preserve
older-first behavior; never silently discard an older valid retirement.

Expose a separate registered-state-derived divider-result output from alu.sv
for this completion route. Do not feed the general combinational ALU result
back through the retirement mux into its own WB forwarding input: that creates
a structural combinational loop even if divide opcode selection masks it.
Use the captured forwarded rs1/rs2 for divide RVFI, pc_next=pc+4 and zero memory
masks/data/address for the divide. Keep completion stable until consumed,
retire and write exactly once, increment the existing order counter once,
and release ID/fetch on consumption subject to their other stalls.

The instruction accepted behind the divide must see its result through the
existing write-first register-file bypass on the completion/consumption cycle.
If fetch is stalled, the register-file write still completes once and later
consumers read the committed value. Feed EX's ordinary MEM/WB bypass from the normal MEM/WB data mux, before
the retirement-source selection. The direct divide result belongs on the
register-file write and write-first decode path; feeding it back through EX's
ordinary WB bypass adds an unnecessary long timing path into the held
divide's live operands. Keep retained ordinary-WB forwarding
ownership and memory-stall behavior intact; do not qualify held forwarding
solely with the retirement pulse. Preserve nret=1, every external port,
decoder legality, branch prediction, ordinary ALU/multiply latency and memory
handshakes.

This route is intended to preserve the ten-clock first-divide startup bound
and the load-use/redirect-to-divide retirement bounds, while consecutive
divides retire ten clocks apart instead of eight. Validate the entire
retirement stream with the unchanged liveness check; do not infer safety from
steady-state arithmetic latency. Unit tests must reflect eight busy iterations
and direct retirement without weakening arithmetic, order, startup or the
ten-cycle liveness checks. Test simultaneous would-be WB/completion ownership,
all divide consumers, x0, stalled fetch, older stalled loads/stores, reset,
wrong paths and exactly-once stores/retirement in real and ALTOPS modes.

Measure canonical stalled CoreMark cycles as well as median Gowin Fmax.
The frequency benefit must outweigh any added cycles from consecutive divides;
CoreMark's dynamic divide frequency must be measured. Acceptance requires
fitness strictly above 120.29, more than 4.6 percent above 115.00. Run unchanged
formal and full-RVFI cosim and canonical CRC/UART/address/marker validation.
The main risks are new retirement-mux fanout, the remaining multiplier path,
and a subtle startup/retirement gap or completion-bypass hazard. No checker,
benchmark, wrapper, nret declaration or other core may change.

Complete this path separation with a dedicated EX/MEM effective_addr field,
computed by a simple forwarded base-plus-immediate adder independently of the
selected general ALU result. MEM uses that field for dmem_addr, lane masks,
misalignment, load extraction and RVFI aligned memory address. Preserve the
ordinary ALU-result field for register writeback and bypassing. Non-memory
arithmetic results must not drive the physical data-memory address port.
This removes the register-file/multiplier-to-dmem path that becomes limiting
after the divider feedback is shortened. Preserve full 32-bit address
arithmetic, memory requests, byte lanes and existing memory-stall holds.

Prototype evidence: direct divide retirement with isolated ordinary-WB
forwarding, before the dedicated address field, measured placement options
0/1/2 at 46.975/50.199/50.199 MHz. With 4,202,272 canonical stalled CoreMark
cycles its median implies fitness 119.4568, only 3.88 percent above the
champion and below acceptance. Its worst option-0 path is register-file
through multiplication to data-memory addressing (26.582 ns, 15 cells).
That result motivates the dedicated address field in this final proposal;
it does not establish that the final combined design clears acceptance.
Real and ALTOPS eight-iteration ALU tests, direct-retirement pipeline tests

implementation_notes:
Implemented the requested arithmetic completion / effective-address separation.

- The divider captures complete magnitudes at launch, performs four full-width restoring steps on each of eight busy edges, and completes at iteration 7. Trial remainders remain 33 bits and subtraction/borrow detection remains 34 bits. Signed correction and exception overrides use registered state. A dedicated div_result port supplies completion independently of the general ALU result. Real and ALTOPS modes share the same protocol; ALTOPS formulas are unchanged.
- EX builds a direct retirement bundle using held instruction metadata and the operands captured after forwarding at launch. EX/MEM captures a completely inert bubble on waiting and consumption cycles. A valid older normal WB explicitly defers consumption; the divide remains held until it can retire. Normal WB and completion exclusion is checked throughout pipeline tests, and isolated tests force a collision to verify older-first behavior.
- The single retirement mux drives the existing register-file write/write-first decode path, RVFI channel 0, and order counter. Ordinary EX forwarding remains connected to the normal MEM/WB data mux and retained ownership controls, independently of retirement validity and direct completion.
- EX/MEM now has a separate 32-bit effective_addr, computed from forwarded rs1 plus immediate. Non-memory instructions capture zero in this field. MEM uses it for the physical address, alignment, lane masks, load extraction, and aligned RVFI address. Ordinary arithmetic writeback and bypass data remain separate.
- Expanded tests cover all four divide operations, signed extremes, seeded full-width operands, changed live inputs, held completion, reset at every phase, x0/self destinations, ALU/multiply/divide/branch/JALR/load/store consumers, write-first decode, stalled fetch, older stalled loads/stores, wrong paths, and exactly-once stores/retirement. Address tests cover forwarding, wraparound/high bits, byte/halfword/word accesses, misalignment, and retained WB during memory stalls. Original startup and ten-cycle retirement bounds are unchanged: first divide retires at cycle 10, load-use/redirect-to-divide gaps are 9, consecutive divides are 10 apart.

No functional deviations from the hypothesis. No external ports, nret declaration, decoder, predictor, multiplier, memory handshake, checker, benchmark, wrapper, or other core was changed.

Validation on the final RTL:

- Verilator lint with the requested flags: PASS, no warnings. ALTOPS lint also PASS.
- pytest -q cores/bench/test: 14 runners PASS, including real and ALTOPS arithmetic, pipeline, and completion-route tests.
- RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=8 bash formal/run_all.sh: 53 passed, 0 failed on the first RTL attempt, including unchanged liveness, unique, register, PC, and instruction checks. No formal repair attempts were needed. This is the standard ALTOPS formal gate; formal-deep was not run.
- make bench, then NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench: PASS for 5 ELFs. Selftest and random1/random2/random3 were compared field-by-field against the unchanged ISS, both without stalls and with canonical instruction/data stalls. CoreMark passed canonical CRC/UART/address validation.
- NRET=1 make fpga TARGET=bench: PASS. Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured 50.289 / 53.914 / 53.914 MHz; median 53.914 MHz. Area: 3655 logic cells, 889 registers, 8 LUT-RAM, 6 BSRAM, 6 DSP.
- Canonical stalled CoreMark: 4,202,272 marker-bracketed cycles, 10 iterations, markers at cycles 14,996 and 4,217,268. EBREAK reached, no out-of-bounds accesses, all five canonical CRCs matched, and UART included "Correct operation validated." Actual compilation used the unchanged canonical -O3, TOTAL_DATA_SIZE=2000 configuration.
- Fitness = 53.914e6 * 10 / 4,202,272 = 128.2972639563 (evaluator reports 128.30): strictly above 120.29 and 11.5628% above 115.00.
- Dynamic division frequency was measured by streaming the unchanged simulator's full canonical stalled retirement trace. The complete run retired 2,937,037 instructions, including two DIVU instructions. Between the start/stop marker retirements there were 2,922,015 instructions and zero DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU instructions. Both divides occur outside the measured interval, explaining the unchanged CoreMark cycle count.

Remaining tradeoffs: consecutive divides take two more clocks than the previous implementation, so division-heavy workloads may lose throughput. The option-0 worst reported path is now register-file to ID state through ID/EX control, 25.179 ns and 18 cells; it no longer ends at the physical data-memory address. The requested local acceptance threshold is met; the orchestrator still performs its independent validation.

Invocation detail: the initial plain make fpga command used build.sh's default NRET=2 and failed compiling the single-channel harness. Re-running with NRET=1, matching core.yaml, fixed the invocation without changing any contract file. Validation logs and Gowin reports are under cores/bench/generated/.

title: Three-entry predicted-stream buffer with lossless compact PC tokens
motivation:
The champion stops its predicted instruction stream whenever decode
waits on execution or data memory. Earlier four-entry queues reduced
CoreMark from 4,202,272 to 3,980,323 bracketed cycles, but did not beat
the contemporaneous winner. The current champion has a faster divider;
a smaller queue can expose those saved cycles with less added routing
and state. Branch-trace replay found only 54,467 conditional direction
misses in 529,588 branches, versus 4.2 million cycles; enlarging the
direction table therefore offers too little cycle reduction by itself.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a three-entry elastic queue of predicted instructions between the
fetch PC and combinational decode. This is one predictor-stream
buffering change. Preserve the existing 128x2-bit bimodal predictor,
direct JAL and sequential JALR policies, frozen direct prediction token,
shallow EX recovery, pipeline depth, and arithmetic implementation.

Each slot contains the full instruction, PC[19:2] and one predicted_direct
bit: 51 bits per slot. Only aligned PCs inside [0,0x00100000) may be
buffered, making omitted PC bits known zeros. Reconstruct the full PC
as {12'b0, saved_pc_word, 2'b0}; never truncate the live fetch PC or any
architectural target arithmetic. Keep a fixed head at entry zero and
a two-bit occupancy count from zero to three. A buffered head takes priority over
raw imem_data; an empty queue bypasses a ready bus response directly to
decode without an extra stage. On a pop, shift entries one and two to
zero and one. An append writes old occupancy minus pop and takes
priority over a shift to that same slot. Full simultaneous pop/push
moves old entries one/two to zero/one and writes the new response into
entry two. Increment count on append without pop, decrement on pop
without append, and otherwise hold it. Keep comparisons and arithmetic
explicitly two bits wide. This uses 153 payload bits, versus 260 in the
previous four-entry full-PC queue, and avoids a pointer-indexed read mux.
Do not reset unused payload flops; clear occupancy on reset/recovery.

Give IF raw io_imemReady and decode_hold independently. Existing stall_id
already represents load-use, older dmem backpressure and execute_wait.
Expose instruction availability as queue_nonempty OR io_imemReady and
use that for hazard-unit fetch masking. Select the head and source
addresses without dependence on consume so load-use detection has no
combinational loop. A buffered instruction can issue while imem stalls.
Preserve all load-use bubbling, older dmem holds and retained WB data.

Consume when available AND NOT decode_hold; pop only a consumed queued
head. Accept a raw response when io_imemReady AND (occupancy below three
OR pop), subject to the boundary guard below. When empty and consuming,
bypass without also appending. Otherwise append an accepted response
exactly once. Advance the fetch PC with that response's own prediction
whenever it is accepted, including while decode is held. Save that
decision permanently with its queue entry; never redo its BHT lookup.
The saved direct bit reaches ID/EX and the existing XOR recovery path.
Reconstruct predicted_next_pc only for verification metadata, keeping
it out of the timed recovery and autonomous fetch-PC logic.

Reset and permitted EX recovery take priority over ordinary PC/count
updates. A redirect sets the fetch PC to actual_next_pc, empties the
queue, and synchronously clears ID/EX controls and validity. Candidate
payload writes on that edge may occur but become unreachable, and
subsequent occupied entries must be overwritten before use. Keep
redirect out of instruction/source-address masking and payload movement.
EX still defers recovery while an older memory access is held; recovery
then overrides an imem stall. Correct predictions preserve the queue.
Train only on the existing exactly-once advancing legal branch event.

Preserve the aligned [0,0x00100000) predicted-target guard. Whenever the
live PC is outside this range, unaligned, or equal to 0x000ffffc, inhibit
autonomous acceptance until the queue is empty and decode can consume
that full-width response directly. Such responses must never be stored
in compact slots. This guard makes compression lossless and prevents
speculative fall-through beyond the final word. Older entries continue
draining and recovery must override this boundary hold. Do not clamp
or alias architectural PCs; retain full-width wrapping arithmetic and
existing demand-fetch, trap, forward-progress and RVFI semantics.

An isolated prototype of this compact three-entry design completed the
canonical ten-iteration CoreMark run in 3,981,775 bracketed cycles with
both bus-stall modes, passing CRC/UART, completion, marker and bounds
validation. Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured 47.294/49.622/49.622
MHz, median 49.622 MHz. This implies fitness about 124.62, 8.37 percent
above 115.00. Option zero used 3,756 logic cells and 1,012 registers;
its worst reported path crossed WB/forwarding/execute to data memory.
All eight full-RVFI comparisons for selftest and random1/2/3 passed
with ready buses and with combined instruction/data stalls.

These are prototype measurements, not approval of the eventual RTL.
Placement sensitivity remains material: this cycle count requires median
Fmax above 47.89678 MHz. Require all existing correctness gates, canonical
stalled CoreMark validation and median Gowin timing on the final design;
fitness must exceed 120.29, more than 4.6 percent above 115.00.

title: Fabric operand capture with registered forwarding decisions
motivation:
The champion scores 128.30 at 53.914 MHz with 4,202,272 CoreMark cycles.
Its worst reported path crosses the register-file/execute/control cone.
Prior micro_opt attempts focused on arithmetic and recovery logic.
Local probes found that removing wide squash fanout, using a flop
register file, and flattening operand muxes did not clear the acceptance
margin. In particular, the flop-register-file probe exposed a worst
path from registered source/destination addresses through forward_unit
and the ALU into EX/MEM. Comparing tags and selecting forwarding within
EX consumes timing budget before the useful arithmetic begins.

The registered-forwarding prototype alone reached 54.566 MHz, below the
acceptance margin: its next worst path again starts at the inferred
BSRAM register-file output. Conversely, explicit flop storage alone
reached 54.934 MHz and exposed forwarding comparisons as the limiter.
These complementary results motivate changing the whole operand-capture
mapping at the existing ID/EX boundary in this final proposal.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement the register file as 31 independent scalar 32-bit word registers
inside constant-index generate blocks, each synchronously cleared on
reset and written only when w_en && w_addr equals its constant index.
Do not store x0. Decode each read address into per-word one-hot selects,
mask each word and combine 32 leaves including a zero x0 leaf through
an explicit balanced binary OR tree. Use static wiring, not a variable
indexed RAM read or a serial OR accumulator. Preserve both read ports,
all bits, synchronous reset/write behavior, and final read priority:
x0 is zero; otherwise an enabled matching write bypasses w_data;
otherwise return the selected stored word. Verify Gowin maps storage to
fabric flops and keeps operand capture in fabric at ID/EX, removing the
slow BSRAM launch that otherwise limits the registered-forwarding change.

Optimize operand acquisition at the existing ID/EX boundary by coupling
fabric register-file reads with registered forwarding decisions.
Compute the two operand forwarding selections while an instruction is
in decode and register those selections on the same edge that accepts
its ID/EX payload. EX then receives registered 00/01/10 selectors for
its existing operand muxes, removing tag comparison and youngest-writer
priority logic from the start of the execute datapath. Add no pipeline
stage, instruction latency, speculation or extra issue capability.

The decode comparisons must use the destinations and write ownership
that will exist AFTER the accepting edge, not the current EX/MEM and
MEM/WB tags. For next EX/MEM, use the current ID/EX destination and
EX's ctrl_with_trap.reg_write, suppressed when the current instruction
is a divide because that route inserts an EX/MEM bubble even on consume.
For next ordinary MEM/WB, use the current EX/MEM destination and MEM's
ctrl_with_trap.reg_write. Export these small next-write qualifiers from
their owning stages so jump-target and memory-misalignment traps cannot
create phantom writers. These qualifiers describe an advancing edge;
ID acceptance already excludes a dmem hold. Do not compute either
qualifier from the selected arithmetic result or a retirement mux.

Compare incoming IF/ID instruction source fields against those next
destinations. Preserve nonzero-destination guards and EX-over-WB-over-
local priority. Register both two-bit selections with the exact ID/EX
control priority: reset clears, flush_id clears even when stall_id is
asserted, otherwise !stall_id captures, otherwise hold. Keep the
existing instruction masking when imem is unavailable. A load-use
bubble clears selectors; the dependent instruction accepted one cycle
later selects the load entering MEM/WB on that same edge.

During a dmem hold, ID/EX and EX/MEM are held and ordinary MEM/WB keeps
its data, destination and write ownership even after valid clears.
Hold the registered selectors as well, and never qualify ownership
solely with retirement valid. When a divide waits in ID/EX, selectors
may hold while older entries drain: its architectural operands have
already been captured on div_request, and waiting/consumption inject
an inert EX/MEM bubble. Preserve that launch snapshot discipline.
A divide held behind stalled older memory must launch with the correct
retained selectors when the memory request finally advances. On direct
divide consumption, the next accepted instruction gets the divide
value through the unchanged register-file write-first path; the divide
must not masquerade as an EX/MEM or ordinary MEM/WB forwarding owner.

Keep EX operand muxes, ALU/multiplier/
divider arithmetic and latency, branch predictor, squash behavior,
memory requests and single-channel RVFI unchanged. This is a local
control retiming within the current pipeline. It targets the common
forwarding-to-arithmetic path rather than changing benchmark cycles.
Risks are next-state ownership mistakes, trap handling, and moving the
limiting path into decode or the next-write qualifiers.

Validate next-cycle selectors against the original combinational rule
whenever an ordinary instruction executes and whenever a divide launches.
Cover EX/WB simultaneous matches, x0, both source ports, all forwarding
source combinations, load-use bubbles, repeated memory stalls with WB
valid cleared, flush-plus-hold priority, trap-suppressed writers,
consecutive divides and completion-to-ID consumers. Retain all original

title: Register operand delivery before EX forwarding and recovery
motivation:
The champion scores 128.30 at 53.914 MHz and 4,202,272 CoreMark cycles.
A fresh Gowin option-0 run reproduces 50.289 MHz: its 25.179 ns worst path
starts at the register-file BSRAM output, passes through operand selection
and JALR recovery, and ends at ID/EX reset. The inferred memory has absorbed
part of the operand capture boundary: BSRAM clock-to-output and read bypass
logic remain ahead of EX forwarding. Previous structural hypotheses mostly
retimed division; r4s1 changed validity, and r6s1 separated arithmetic completion
from memory addressing. The remaining register-file storage topology is a
new structural opportunity. Retain single-cycle issue and move the raw
register read mux ahead of explicit operand flops by changing the RF storage.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one structural change: move register selection and source/destination
matching ahead of a physical operand-delivery boundary. Use 31 explicit,
independently written 32-bit RF flop banks with decoded one-hot reads, and
register forwarding-match tokens alongside the existing ID/EX operands. The existing
ID/EX operand registers must remain a real physical pipeline boundary,
separating register selection from EX forwarding, arithmetic and recovery.
Keep the architectural reg_file interface and all pipeline cycle
boundaries unchanged; this is a storage and operand-collection topology
change, not an added pipeline stage or an ISA change.

Give each x1..x31 bank a statically elaborated data register and a local
write enable w_en && w_addr == bank_number. Reset each bank to zero as
before. Do not code the bank writes as a variable-index memory access, and
do not code reads as regs[rs_addr]; these encourage the same inferred BSRAM
and output-register absorption as the champion. Decode each read address
once into 31 one-hot selects, mask each bank's word, and OR the selected
words with an explicitly balanced tree if needed to keep synthesis from
building a serial priority chain. x0 is a constant zero and has no writable
bank. Preserve the exact same-cycle write-first read bypass, including
priority of x0 over bypass and independent matching for rs1 and rs2.

Use portable synthesizable SystemVerilog and structurally elaborated fixed
bank accesses. No vendor black boxes or simulation-only implementation may
replace the functional register file. Verify in Gowin's synthesis report
that the RF is implemented as flop banks and that ID/EX operand values have
physical flop endpoints rather than only registered RAM addresses and
post-RAM bypass logic. The expected cost is about 992 storage flops plus
read selection logic, offset by removing the two RF BSRAMs. Keep within the
Tang Nano 20K's resources and the 10,000-LUT target. All 32 architectural
bits and all source/destination addresses remain fully supported.


Precompute four equality tokens in decode: incoming rs1/rs2 versus the
current ID/EX destination (which will become EX/MEM), and versus the current
EX/MEM destination (which will become MEM/WB). Register these tokens on the
same edge that accepts the associated instruction into ID/EX. Reset and
flush clear them; a true ID/EX hold retains them. EX forwarding consumes
these registered equalities instead of doing five-bit comparisons in its
critical cycle. Continue qualifying each match with the actual live source's
reg_write and nonzero destination, and keep EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB-over-register
priority. Registering equality alone avoids predicting eventual write
eligibility: alignment traps, bubbles and the divider's direct retirement
can still cancel an apparent producer before it reaches a forwarding slot.

Keep the retained ordinary WB source and match tokens stable across an
older dmem hold even after its retirement pulse clears. During divider
waiting the older slots drain, but division uses operands captured at
launch; no stale match token may resample operands or determine completion.
A younger instruction accepted on direct divide retirement uses the
existing RF write-first path, and its new tokens must reflect the now-empty
ordinary EX/MEM/WB slots. Do not forward the direct result through the
ordinary WB-to-EX input. Test load-use bubbles, recovery plus holds,
back-to-back writes to one destination, trap-cancelled writers and all
divide consumers. No additional operand stage or dependency bubble is added.

Preserve the current EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB forwarding priority, retained WB
ownership during memory stalls, ordinary write-first decode behavior, and
direct divide completion writes into the RF. Leave branch prediction,
recovery timing, divider/multiplier arithmetic and latency, dedicated
memory address path, memory handshakes, decoder legality and nret=1 unchanged.
Thus the canonical stalled CoreMark interval should remain 4,202,272 cycles;
any difference must be explained as a bug or unintended scope change before
acceptance. The intended fitness gain comes from higher Fmax only.

Run existing register-file, real/ALTOPS pipeline and arithmetic tests,
unchanged formal gates, and full-RVFI selftest/random cosimulation with and
without stalls. Retain all reset/x0/write-first checks and cover writes and
reads of every register, simultaneous same-address reads, distinct read
ports, back-to-back writes, all data bits, and divide-completion-to-decode
bypass under fetch stalls. Preserve canonical CoreMark CRCs, UART text,
address bounds, marker timing and the ten-cycle liveness bound.

Compare median Gowin Fmax times measured iterations/cycle, not cell counts
alone. Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 134.2018, or approximately
56.395 MHz if the cycle count is unchanged. The primary risks are routing
congestion from the extra flops/read trees and a newly limiting divider or
multiplier path. Do not add unrelated arithmetic or predictor changes if
those paths become limiting; report the measured result for this one
structural hypothesis. Any prototype evidence appended below is preliminary
and must be reproduced by the implementation phase.

Prototype evidence for this exact combined operand-delivery topology:
Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured 61.185 / 62.631 / 62.631 MHz,
median 62.631 MHz. Option 0 used 4,884 logic cells and 1,824 registers,
with zero LUT-RAM, four BSRAM and six DSP blocks. The RF BSRAMs are gone;
the worst option-0 path is now ordinary WB destination/control through
EX/multiplication to the ALU-result register, 21.638 ns and 13 cells.
The flop-bank-only intermediate reached 55.051 MHz, below acceptance;
registering the forwarding equalities is an essential part of completing
this operand boundary, not an optional cleanup.

The exact combined prototype passed all 14 existing pytest runners,
including real and ALTOPS ALU/pipeline suites, with their original
architectural, stage-timing and liveness assertions unchanged. All 53
unchanged formal checks passed. Full-RVFI selftest and three random ELFs
passed both without stalls and with canonical instruction/data stalls.
Canonical CoreMark passed all five CRCs, UART text, address-bound and
marker checks; ten iterations took exactly 4,202,272 bracketed cycles,
with markers at 14,996 and 4,217,268. Fitness computed from measured
median Fmax is 149.0408 iterations/s, about 16.17 percent above 128.30,
comfortably above 134.2018. Formal-deep was not run; arithmetic RTL is
unchanged. These measurements are prototype evidence, not a replacement
for independent final implementation evaluation.

For reproducibility the measured bank implementation uses a generate
loop with one always_ff per x1..x31, a fixed bank-number write comparison,
and combinational OR reductions of the 31 masked words for each read port.
Synthesis balances those reductions; no manual extra pipeline registers
or timing attributes are needed. Four match bits in core.sv use exactly
reset-or-flush clearing and else-if-not-stall capture, and forward_unit
retains its original two-bit selection encoding and live eligibility tests.
The only prototype RTL files changed were reg_file.sv, core.sv and
forward_unit.sv. Research RTL is restored after measurement; implement
this specified structure and add the directed test extensions above.

implementation_notes:
# Register operand delivery before EX forwarding and recovery

Implemented the combined structural hypothesis in `cores/bench/rtl/reg_file.sv`,
`core.sv`, and `forward_unit.sv` only. Directed coverage was added to
`cores/bench/test/test_reg_file.py` and `test_pipeline.py`.

## Implementation

- RF x1..x31 each have a statically elaborated 32-bit `data_q` register and
  their own synchronous reset/local decoded write enable. There is no x0
  bank, variable-index write, or address-indexed storage read.
- Each read address is decoded into 31 one-hot selects. Fixed bank words
  are masked and combinationally OR-reduced. Gowin balances the reductions;
  no vendor primitives, timing attributes, or extra operand registers are used.
- x0 still overrides write-first bypass; each port independently bypasses
  the current architectural writeback value.
- Four equality bits compare decode sources with current ID/EX and EX/MEM
  destinations. They clear on reset or ID/EX flush, capture on ID/EX accept,
  and retain on a true hold. EX retains live reg_write/nonzero-rd eligibility
  and EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB priority. Ordinary retained WB remains the only WB
  forwarding source; direct division reaches decode through RF write-first.
- No changes to pipeline boundaries, hazard rules, prediction/recovery,
  arithmetic/latency, dedicated effective-address path, memory handshakes,
  decoding, or nret=1.

## Verification

- Requested Verilator `--lint-only -Wall -Wno-MULTITOP` command: PASS,
  without warnings.
- `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench bash formal/run_all.sh`: PASS,
  53 passed / 0 failed on the first RTL attempt. No formal fix attempts.
  Formal configuration and wrappers were unchanged. Formal-deep was not
  run; multiplier/divider RTL is unchanged.
- All 14 pytest runners passed across the full run and targeted rerun.
  This includes real/ALTOPS arithmetic and pipeline suites, decoder,
  immediate, RF, and isolated stage tests. Both final pipeline suites
  passed all 34 cocotb cases. Original assertions were retained, including
  stage timing, prediction/recovery, divide ownership, and ten-cycle liveness.
- RF extensions cover every architectural register, walking ones and zeros
  in all 32 bits of every bank, all 1,024 read-port pairs, both independent
  bypass ports, consecutive writes, deterministic reference-model traffic,
  x0, and reset of populated banks with an enabled write.
- Pipeline extensions check token capture/flush/hold on every sampled edge,
  forwarding against a live-address oracle at consumption, ordinary WB
  decode bypass, all-bank dependencies and repeated destinations, retained
  WB forwarding during a six-cycle memory hold followed by recovery,
  trap-cancelled JALR/load writers, and all four divide operations delivering
  to bank-boundary consumers before/after fetch stalls. Existing divide
  consumer tests still cover arithmetic, branches, jumps, loads, and stores.
- The initial new fetch-stall test incorrectly required reg_write=0 in
  every ordinary WB bubble. Fetch bubbles are ADDI x0,x0,0, so its assertion
  was corrected to require invalid WB with no eligible nonzero destination.
  No RTL or pre-existing assertion changed for this correction. The initial
  12 other runners passed; both affected pipeline runners then passed.
- `make bench` and `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench`: PASS, five ELFs.
  Full RVFI selftest/random1/random2/random3 comparisons passed both ready
  buses and canonical instruction/data stalls. The plain Makefile command
  initially defaulted its C++ harness to NRET=2; setting NRET=1 selected the
  existing correct single-channel harness without editing it.
- Stalled CoreMark independently reproduced start=14,996, stop=4,217,268,
  and exactly 4,202,272 bracketed cycles for ten iterations. EBREAK,
  address bounds, markers, and canonical UART text passed. CRCs matched:
  e9f5 / e714 / 1fd7 / 8e3a / fcaf.

## Independent Gowin measurement

Ran `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` using the unchanged
vendor evaluation flow. Placement options 0/1/2 measured
**57.369 / 60.721 / 60.721 MHz**, median **60.721 MHz**.

Fitness = 60.721e6 * 10 / 4,202,272 = **144.4956 iterations/s**, strictly
above 134.2018 and **12.62% above 128.30**. These are this implementation's
measurements; the preliminary prototype's 62.631 MHz was not reproduced.
There is no cycle-count difference to explain.

Option 0 uses **4,871 logic cells, 1,824 registers, zero LUT-RAM,
four BSRAMs, and six DSP blocks**. It fits the Tang Nano 20K and the
10,000-LUT target. All three options completed placement/routing.

Physical-boundary evidence:

- `cores/bench/generated/timing/gowin_p0/impl/gwsynthesis/core_bench_syn_rsc.xml`
  and `core_bench_syn_resource.html` report u_rf with **992 registers**,
  1,532 LUTs, and **no BSRAM/SSRAM**. The four BSRAMs belong to core_bench's
  benchmark memories. u_id retains 156 registers; the core has four local
  token registers.
- Option-0 `impl/pnr/core_bench.tr` explicitly terminates a setup path at
  `cpu/u_id/reg_q.rs1_val_24_s0/D`, with a physical CLK pin/setup check.
- Option-1/2 timing reports likewise terminate paths at
  `cpu/u_id/reg_q.rs2_val_29_s0/D` and bits 5, 9, 7, and 2, each with
  physical CLK/setup checks. Both operand values remain physical flops.

The limiting option-0 path is now inside the unchanged divider:
`divisor_q_3_s0` to `remainder_q_3_s1`, arrival 22.725 ns, 127 reported
cells. Options 1/2 are limited by `quotient_q_31_s1` to `remainder_q_0_s1`,
21.763 ns, 119 cells. Arithmetic was deliberately left unchanged as required.
Remaining concern is placement/routing sensitivity and divider timing;
there are no known functional failures or architectural deviations.

title: Two-entry compact predicted-stream buffer on the direct-retirement core
motivation:
The current core stops its predicted fetch stream whenever decode waits
for a load-use dependency, data memory or execution. Previous four- and
three-entry predictor queues saved about 5.3 percent of CoreMark cycles,
but their timing cost prevented them from replacing the winner. The new
champion has separated divide retirement and the physical memory address
from general arithmetic. A smaller two-entry queue on this exact champion
preserves most of the fetch overlap with only 102 payload bits and two
occupancy bits. Direction-table growth alone offers little upside: the
prior branch replay found only 54,467 conditional misses in 529,588 branches.

hypothesis.motivation:

for a load-use dependency, data memory or execution. Previous four- and
three-entry predictor queues saved about 5.3 percent of CoreMark cycles,
but their timing cost prevented them from replacing the winner. The new

from general arithmetic. A smaller two-entry queue on this exact champion
preserves most of the fetch overlap with only 102 payload bits and two

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add exactly two fixed-head elastic entries to the existing predicted
fetch stream. This is one predictor-stream buffering change. Retain the
champion's 128-entry bimodal direction table, early direct JAL targets,
sequential JALR prediction, direction-token recovery, pipeline depth,
divider schedule and direct divide retirement. Do not register recovery
or change the arithmetic, forwarding or architectural memory interfaces.

Each entry holds instruction[31:0], PC[19:2], and predicted_direct: 51 bits.
Only aligned instruction-memory PCs in [0,0x00100000) may be buffered.
Reconstruct their full PC as {12'b0, saved_pc_word, 2'b0}. Keep the live
fetch PC and all target arithmetic 32 bits. Entry zero is always the
oldest response; a two-bit occupancy counter ranges from zero to two.
A nonempty queue supplies decode independently of raw imemReady. When
empty, bypass an available raw response without adding a pipeline stage.
Decode-head selection must not depend on downstream acceptance, avoiding
a loop through source-address extraction and load-use detection.

Give IF separate raw bus_ready and decode_hold inputs. Use the existing
stall_id as decode_hold, covering load-use, older dmem holds and division.
Report available = (count != 0) OR bus_ready to hazard control in place
of raw imemReady. Define consume = available AND NOT decode_hold and
pop = (count != 0) AND consume. Accept a raw response when bus_ready AND
(count < 2 OR pop), subject to the boundary restriction below. Append it
exactly when accepted AND (count != 0 OR NOT consume); an empty bypass
consumed immediately must not also be appended. Advance the fetch PC
using that raw response's own prediction on every accepted response,
even while decode is held. Otherwise hold the fetch PC.

On pop, shift old entry one into zero. On append, write index count-pop,
with append taking priority over a shift to that same entry. Thus full
simultaneous pop/push moves old entry one to zero and writes the new
response to one; one-entry replacement writes the response to zero.
Increment count for append without pop, decrement for pop without append,
and otherwise retain it. Use explicit two-bit count arithmetic and local
per-entry write conditions. Clear occupancy on reset and recovery;
unoccupied payload registers need no reset or synchronous squash.

Freeze predicted_direct with each accepted response. Its stored value
reaches ID/EX unchanged despite any intervening same-index BHT training.
Reconstruct predicted_next_pc for the existing metadata from the saved
full PC, saved instruction immediate and saved direction bit, never by
rereading the BHT. Keep this reconstruction outside autonomous fetch-PC
selection and timed EX recovery. Direct recovery retains the champion's
direction XOR and offset-4 exception; indirect recovery is unchanged.

Compute candidate queue movement without redirect in payload write
enables. Reset has highest priority in the PC/count update, then existing
advancing EX recovery: install its actual target, invalidate both entries,
and squash the younger ID/EX instruction through the existing control
path. A candidate payload write on that edge is harmless because no slot
remains occupied. Recovery overrides imem stalls; EX still defers recovery
behind an older dmem hold. Correct predictions preserve the stream.
Train only on the existing exactly-once advancing legal branch event.
Preserve retained MEM/WB forwarding and all load-use/divide interlocks.

Preserve the existing aligned, in-range speculative-target guard. When
the live PC is outside [0,0x00100000), unaligned, or exactly 0x000ffffc,
allow raw-response acceptance only with an empty queue and immediate
decode consumption. Such responses bypass with their full-width PC and
must never enter compact slots. Queued entries may continue draining;
recovery always overrides the boundary hold. This prevents autonomous
lookahead past the last word without truncating demand addresses,
changing trap semantics or deadlocking symbolic instruction streams.

An isolated two-entry prototype on the supplied champion RTL completed
canonical stalled CoreMark in 3,991,298 marker-bracketed cycles versus
4,202,272, a 5.02 percent cycle reduction. The unchanged evaluator passed
completion, canonical CRC/UART, bounds and timing-marker validation.
All eight full-RVFI comparisons of selftest and random1/2/3 passed across
ready buses and combined instruction/data stalls. Gowin placement options
0/1/2 measured 52.878/56.034/56.034 MHz, median 56.034 MHz. Option zero
used 3,544 logic cells and 993 registers, with unchanged 8 LUT-RAM,
6 BSRAM and 6 DSP. These results imply about 140.39 iterations/second,
9.42 percent above 128.30. A one-entry probe saved fewer cycles and had
a lower median Fmax, supporting the choice of exactly two entries.
A 4,000-cycle randomized IF-stage model test also passed, including
349 full pop/push events, 266 buffered deliveries during raw bus stalls,
749 boundary cycles and 483 recoveries. It checked complete saved PCs,
instructions and predictions against a software queue and BHT model.
All 53 unchanged single-channel formal checks passed, including liveness,
PC consistency, uniqueness and register consistency. Strict Verilator
lint passed after removing the unused internal stall_if interface; the
quoted timing and simulation runs preceded that unused-output cleanup.

These are exploratory measurements, not final implementation approval.
Require unchanged formal, real/ALTOPS arithmetic and pipeline tests,
full-RVFI cosim, canonical stalled CoreMark and median vendor timing
on the final implementation. Preserve nret=1, every external port and
all hard invariants, including the ten-cycle ready-bus retirement bound.
Final fitness must exceed 134.2018 iterations/second, strictly more than
4.6 percent above the champion; do not accept a cycle-only improvement.

title: Reduce dependent selection in M-extension arithmetic
motivation:
The champion scores 151.03 at median Gowin Fmax 63.469 MHz and
4,202,272 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path runs
from quotient_q[31] to quotient_q[0] entirely inside u_ex/u_alu,
with 130 cells and 21.382 ns arrival time. Four dependent full-width
restoring subtract/select steps now limit timing after r7s0 removed
the register-file and forwarding bottlenecks. The earlier r5s0
micro_opt radix-4 attempt improved arithmetic timing but encountered
an external register-file/multiplier path and lost to another slot.
The current design needs only two radix-4 digits per iteration, and
both fabric operand capture and the independent memory address path
are already present. A current-champion divider-only prototype reached
64.985 MHz median, just 2.4 percent above baseline; its next worst path
crosses a multiplier and the ALU result-selection chain. Earlier r6s0
also found that division and multiplication can impose complementary
limits. Optimize these two cones with one local arithmetic-mapping
approach: resolve operation choices before dependent arithmetic and
eliminate unnecessary late wide selection, retaining all latencies.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 151.03 at median Gowin Fmax 63.469 MHz and
4,202,272 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path runs
from quotient_q[31] to quotient_q[0] entirely inside u_ex/u_alu,
with 130 cells and 21.382 ns arrival time. Four dependent full-width
restoring subtract/select steps now limit timing after r7s0 removed
the register-file and forwarding bottlenecks. The earlier r5s0
micro_opt radix-4 attempt improved arithmetic timing but encountered
an external register-file/multiplier path and lost to another slot.
The current design needs only two radix-4 digits per iteration, and
both fabric operand capture and the independent memory address path
are already present. A current-champion divider-only prototype reached
64.985 MHz median, just 2.4 percent above baseline; its next worst path
crosses a multiplier and the ALU result-selection chain. Earlier r6s0
also found that division and multiplication can impose complementary
limits. Optimize these two cones with one local arithmetic-mapping
approach: resolve operation choices before dependent arithmetic and
eliminate unnecessary late wide selection, retaining all latencies.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Reduce dependent arithmetic and result-selection depth inside alu.sv:
use two parallel-trial radix-4 digits in the divider and one multiplier
whose signed operand extensions select the M operation before the
product. This is a single micro_opt proposal for M-extension mapping,
with no pipeline, predictor or memory redesign. Replace the real
divider's four serial binary restoring steps per busy clock with two
radix-4 restoring digit steps. Retain exactly
eight busy iteration clocks, the existing launch/done/consume protocol,
direct divide retirement, and nret=1. Process four dividend bits per
iteration as before; add no preparation, correction or pipeline cycle.

At the existing launch edge capture unsigned divisor magnitude D and
its 34-bit multiple 3D. Compute 3D from the current launch operand's
magnitude, never the previous divisor_q. Explicitly zero-extend before
shifting and adding so that 3*0xffffffff is represented exactly.
Derive 34-bit D and 2D by wiring from divisor_q. Hold the registered
multiples throughout busy and done; reset the new register normally.
This removes divisor-multiple generation from the recurrent path.

Each digit step takes 32-bit remainder R and quotient Q, forms the
34-bit trial T={R,Q[31:30]}, and computes three independent 35-bit
unsigned differences diff[k]={1'b0,T}-{1'b0,M[k]}, with 34-bit
M[1]=D, M[2]=2D and M[3]=3D. Set ge[k]=!diff[k][34]. These widths
are required for full-range unsigned division; do not truncate high
divisor bits or use prefix-width tapering in a reused iterative step.

Use mutually exclusive selects s0=!ge[1], s1=ge[1]&&!ge[2],
s2=ge[2]&&!ge[3], s3=ge[3]. Select the next 32-bit remainder with
a balanced OR of four masked candidates: T[31:0], diff[1][31:0],
diff[2][31:0], diff[3][31:0]. Append the binary quotient digit
{ge[2], ge[3]||(ge[1]&&!ge[2])} to Q[29:0]. Avoid a serial
priority chain, a separate compare followed by subtraction, or a
post-selection subtraction. For D!=0, R<D implies T<4D and the
selected remainder is again below D and fits in 32 bits.

Chain exactly two such steps and capture step 2 on every busy edge.
Iteration indices 0 through 7 still consume exactly 32 dividend bits;
iteration 7 asserts done at the existing edge. Preserve launch
initialization, signed magnitude conversion, quotient and remainder
sign restoration, explicit divide-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1 results,
result retention until consume, reset cancellation, and rejection
of requests while busy or done. Keep every RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS
formula and its eight-clock protocol unchanged, with real arithmetic
excluded from that configuration.

Replace the three separate signedness-specific 64-bit products with
one signed 33-by-33 multiplication. Form signed [32:0] operands
Aext={(op==MULH || op==MULHSU) && a[31],a} and
Bext={(op==MULH) && b[31],b}, and a signed [65:0] product P=Aext*Bext.
MUL selects P[31:0]; MULH, MULHU and MULHSU share P[63:32]. The extra
product bits are deliberately unused. Explicit signed declarations
are essential: zero extension must retain the full unsigned range,
while sign extension encodes negative operands for the high products.
Do not use a correction subtraction after an unsigned product. Keep
the existing ALTOPS multiplication formulas exactly, and leave base
ALU operations, forwarding, memory, prediction, RVFI and pipeline
controls unchanged. Retain the existing case-based ALU output
selection; the three high-multiply arms now return the same product
slice. An explicit masked-OR output tree was slower on this device.
This removes selection among three wide products
and reduces multiplier resources and operand fanout on the limiting
forwarded-operand path, complementing the shorter divide recurrence.

Halving the number of dependent digit decisions should improve Fmax
without changing iterations/cycle. Parallel subtractors and wider
selection cost area and fanout; magnitude-to-3D launch timing, multiplier
sign controls and a newly exposed non-arithmetic path are risks.

A temporary prototype of this exact combined mapping measured Gowin
placement options 0/1/2 at 63.608/71.026/71.026 MHz, a 71.026 MHz
median. Option 0 used 4,921 logic cells, 1,857 registers and two DSPs,
versus the champion's 4,747 logic cells, 1,824 registers and six DSPs.
Its worst option-0 path now crosses writeback, operand selection and
multiplication rather than the divider feedback loop. The prototype
passed lint, all 12 existing ALU/pipeline test configurations, all 53

title: Fabric-first divider preparation with two radix-4 steps
motivation:
The champion scores 151.03 at 63.469 MHz with 4,202,272 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. After fabric operand storage and registered forwarding
removed the previous pipeline bottleneck, its worst reported path runs
from quotient_q to quotient_q inside u_ex/u_alu: 21.382 ns and 130 cells.
Four serial full-width restoring subtract/select steps now determine the
clock period. Prior structural work established direct divide retirement
and an eight-iteration schedule that fits the unchanged ten-cycle
liveness bound. Prior radix-4 attempts shortened the arithmetic path but
still chained several digit selections and encountered external paths
that the current champion has since shortened. Reorganizing the divider
into a registered divisor operand and fewer parallel digit-selection
stages can remove that serial recurrence without extending latency.

CoreMark cycles. After fabric operand storage and registered forwarding
removed the previous pipeline bottleneck, its worst reported path runs

Four serial full-width restoring subtract/select steps now determine the
clock period. Prior structural work established direct divide retirement
and an eight-iteration schedule that fits the unchanged ten-cycle
liveness bound. Prior radix-4 attempts shortened the arithmetic path but

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one structural change to the sequential divider: overlap preparation
of a registered 3D operand with a narrow fabric first-four-bit operation, then
reuse a two-step radix-4 digit resource for the remaining seven clocks.
Keep launch, eight busy clocks, completion retention and direct retirement
exactly as in the champion. The new preparation/iteration decomposition
must add no clock, pipeline stage or retirement channel. In particular,
do not put 3D generation after magnitude conversion on the launch path.

Launch captures the same signed/unsigned magnitudes, original dividend,
signs and exceptions as today, initializes R=0, and places the dividend
magnitude in Q. On busy iteration zero, register 3D in 34 bits from the
already registered divisor, using zero extension BEFORE shift/add:
dwide={2'b0,divisor_q}; triple_q=(dwide<<1)+dwide. D remains available
in divisor_q and 2D is wiring. Hold triple_q through all later iterations.

Simultaneously consume the first four dividend bits using FOUR NARROW
binary restoring steps in fabric. Initialize a four-bit prefix remainder
r=0 and four-bit prefix quotient q=Q[31:28]. Each step forms five-bit
t={r,q[3]} and six-bit diff={1'b0,t}-{2'b0,D[3:0]}. A successful
subtraction requires BOTH !diff[5] and D[31:4]==0. Select the next r
from diff[3:0] on success or t[3:0] otherwise, and shift q left one bit
appending the success flag. After four steps, register Q={Q[27:0],q}
and R={28'b0,r}. The consumed dividend prefix never exceeds 15, so all
prefix remainders fit four bits. For D>=16 every step rejects subtraction;
for D=0 every step accepts, yielding digit 15 and the unmodified prefix
remainder, compatible with the existing divide-by-zero result override.
The high-divisor guard is mandatory, including D with low nibble zero.

Implement this prefix network with explicit narrow wires/subtractions,
not an indexed ROM or complete case-table that Gowin can map into BSRAM.
Keep the prefix result and subsequent remainder in physical fabric flops.
A prototype table was absorbed into BSRAM and put its slow output on the
next full-width feedback path, negating the shorter digit recurrence.
Check the synthesis resource/path report for this structural boundary:
no divider BSRAM, and no BSRAM launch into the quotient/remainder loop.
Preparing 3D and the four-bit prefix in parallel on the first busy edge
hides setup without lengthening launch or adding an iteration.

On busy iterations one through seven use exactly TWO radix-4 restoring
steps in series, consuming four dividend bits total per clock. Each step
forms the 34-bit T={R,Q[31:30]}. Compute THREE parallel 35-bit unsigned
differences against exact 34-bit D,2D,3D. The leading difference bit is
borrow; let ge1,ge2,ge3 be its inverse for each multiple. Decode one-hot
winner bits w0=!ge1, w1=ge1&&!ge2, w2=ge2&&!ge3, w3=ge3. Select the
next remainder by balanced OR of the four masked low-32-bit candidates
T,diff1,diff2,diff3; append digit {w2|w3,w1|w3} to Q[29:0]. The second
identical step consumes the first step's R and Q, and its outputs become
the registered iteration result. Avoid priority muxes and a second
subtraction after digit selection. Keep all 34-bit multiples and 35-bit
differences until borrow is known: truncation falsely accepts large D.
For nonzero D, R<D gives T<4D and the chosen remainder fits 32 bits.
Four initial bits plus seven four-bit iteration groups consume all 32 bits.

Keep current result sign correction, exceptional RV32M results, stable
done/result until consume, reset cancellation, launch operand capture and
exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas. ALTOPS keeps the same eight busy clocks
and excludes the real digit arithmetic. Preserve the direct completion
path, ordinary retained WB forwarding, effective-address path, decoder,
prediction, multiplier, memory handshakes, full RV32 width and nret=1.

This reduces the recurrent path from four dependent full-width binary
subtract/select stages to two radix-4 stages. A registered 3D bank avoids
recalculating multiples inside that recurrence; overlapping its preparation
avoids a new operand-launch bottleneck. The area tradeoff is six trial
subtractors in place of four, a 34-bit bank register and a narrow
first-digit fabric network. Stay within device capacity and the 10,000-LUT target.
Do not add unrelated branch, memory, multiplier or pipeline changes.

Preliminary exploration measured a larger one-step radix-16 resource
using the same first-digit/preparation overlap, initially with a table. It passed arithmetic,
pipeline, all 53 standard formal checks, selftest/random RVFI cosimulation
with and without stalls, and canonical CoreMark at 4,202,272 measured
cycles. However, its 64.987 MHz median gave only about 2.4 percent gain,
below acceptance, with 5,781 logic cells, 2,114 registers and five BSRAMs.
Its worst paths had moved to ordinary WB/multiply and branch-update logic.
Therefore the proposed final resource uses TWO radix-4 steps and only 3D
storage to reduce routing pressure while still shortening the divider.
A first two-step prototype using the ROM table reached only 58.245 MHz;
the critical source was that table's BSRAM DO pin. The final hypothesis
explicitly replaces the table with the four narrow fabric steps above.
These intermediate measurements are negative evidence, not results for
the final fabric implementation.

Retain all existing arithmetic/protocol assertions. Extend real ALU tests
across all first-nibble/small-divisor combinations, every radix-4 digit,
divisors near powers of two and 0xffffffff, upper-multiple rejection,
signed extremes, zero divisors and seeded full-width random operands
against an independent integer reference. Check eight busy iterations,
changed live inputs after launch, held completion, consecutive operations
and reset at every phase. Exercise changing divisors so stale 3D state
cannot pass. Run real/ALTOPS pipeline tests, unchanged formal gates and
stalled full-RVFI cosimulation, including load-to-divide and consecutive
divides under the existing ten-cycle retirement bound. Standard formal
uses ALTOPS; it does not prove real division arithmetic. Use exact-result
testing and formal-deep when feasible without altering any checker.

Canonical CoreMark should retain exactly 4,202,272 bracketed cycles,
all five CRCs, required UART text and address bounds. A cycle change needs
explanation before acceptance. Prior dynamic measurement found zero
divides in the timed interval, but this must remain a general RV32IM
resource. Accept only measured fitness strictly above 157.97738 iter/s,
more than 4.6 percent above 151.03, requiring about 66.3864 MHz at the
existing cycle count. Evaluate median Gowin Fmax times measured
iterations/cycle, including any new limiting path and area cost.
Final fabric-prefix prototype evidence: Gowin placement options 0/1/2
measured 67.169 / 66.653 / 66.653 MHz, median 66.653 MHz. It used
5,091 logic cells, 1,858 registers, zero LUT-RAM, four BSRAMs and six
DSPs. The first-digit ROM BSRAM is gone. Option zero's divider feedback
path is 20.180 ns and 63 cells, versus the champion's 21.382 ns and
130 cells. Ordinary WB-to-ALU now narrowly limits median timing. The
final prototype passed expanded real and ALTOPS ALU suites, both full-core
pipeline suites, and all five cosimulation ELFs. Stalled canonical
CoreMark retained exactly 4,202,272 bracketed cycles for ten iterations,
with all CRC/UART/address checks passing. This gives 158.61182 iter/s,
a 5.0201 percent improvement over 151.03 and above 157.97738. These are
preliminary prototype measurements. The final fabric variant also passed
all 53 unchanged standard formal checks; these use ALTOPS. Formal-deep
was not run. Independently repeat validation and timing during
implementation. The margin over the 4.6 percent threshold is small.

For reproducibility, first-prefix logic uses four statically generated
four-bit remainder/quotient pairs, five-bit trials and six-bit differences.
It shares the full-width divisor-high-zero predicate across all four
steps. triple_q is a 34-bit resettable flop updated only on busy iteration
zero. Each normal radix-4 step uses three parallel differences and a
four-term masked OR; the quotient bits use w2|w3 and w1|w3. Iteration
zero selects the prefix result; all other iterations select step two.
Keep both real and ALTOPS launch/control schedules unchanged. Prototype
research changes are restored after measurement; implement the described
structure and retain all existing checks.

title: Two-entry predictor run-ahead on the fabric-register-file core
motivation:
Earlier predictor-stream queues reduced the canonical stalled CoreMark
interval from 4,202,272 to about 3,980,323 cycles, but lost to competing
timing improvements. Their last recorded critical path originated in
the old RAM register file and crossed execute recovery into fetch. The
current champion has removed that launch path with a fabric register
file and registered forwarding decisions; its limiting path is now
inside the divider. This changes the timing case for a compact queue.
Prior trace analysis found only 54,467 conditional misses and 13,735
JALRs, so direction or return prediction alone has insufficient headroom.

hypothesis.motivation:
Earlier predictor-stream queues reduced the canonical stalled CoreMark
interval from 4,202,272 to about 3,980,323 cycles, but lost to competing

current champion has removed that launch path with a fabric register

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a two-entry fixed-head elastic queue to the existing predicted
instruction stream on the supplied champion. The single change is
prediction-driven fetch run-ahead across load-use, memory and execute
holds. Retain the 128-entry bimodal table, direct-JAL prediction,
sequential JALR policy, frozen direction-token recovery, pipeline
boundaries, fabric register file, registered forwarding and divider.

Each entry stores instruction[31:0], PC[19:2] and predicted_direct,
totaling 51 bits. Store only aligned PCs in [0,0x00100000). Reconstruct
full saved PCs by zero extension; retain full-width live PC, target
arithmetic, recovery and architectural address semantics. Entry zero
always supplies the oldest buffered instruction. Empty bypass preserves
the existing no-extra-stage behavior. Head selection depends only on
occupancy and raw bus availability, never on decode acceptance.

Give IF independent raw bus_ready and decode_hold inputs. Existing
stall_id supplies decode_hold. Return available = nonempty OR bus_ready
to hazard control in place of raw imemReady. Define consume = available
AND NOT decode_hold, pop = nonempty AND consume, and accept = bus_ready
AND (count < 2 OR pop), subject to the boundary restriction below.
Append an accepted response exactly when nonempty OR NOT consume; an
empty response consumed directly is never also enqueued. Every accepted
response advances the fetch PC using its own prediction even while
decode is held. Otherwise retain the fetch PC.

On pop, shift remaining occupied entries toward the fixed head. Append
at old count minus pop with priority over a shift to the same entry.
Use an explicitly sized two-bit occupancy count and constant-index
payload banks with local enables; avoid variable-index head reads.
Simultaneous full pop/push keeps occupancy two and replaces the tail.
Clear occupancy on reset/recovery; unused payload need not be reset.
Compute candidate payload writes without redirect in their enables;
recovery invalidates all slots on that edge, making such writes inert.

Freeze predicted_direct when accepting each raw response. Reconstruct
saved predicted_next_pc from that token, instruction and saved PC only
for delivery metadata; never reread the current direction table and
never put reconstruction into fetch feedback or timed EX recovery.
Keep the existing direct-direction XOR and offset-four exception.
Train only on the existing advancing legal branch event. Recovery has
priority over PC/count movement and imem backpressure, installs the
full actual target, empties the queue and synchronously squashes ID/EX
controls. Older dmem holds still defer recovery. Preserve retained WB
forwarding, load-use bubbling and all divide interlocks.

When live PC is unaligned, outside the compact range, or 0x000ffffc,
accept a response only with an empty queue and immediate decode
consumption. Such a response bypasses with its full PC and is never
buffered. Let existing entries drain and always permit recovery. This
prevents autonomous lookahead beyond the memory boundary without
truncating demand addresses or changing traps or symbolic liveness.

An isolated prototype on the supplied champion completed canonical
stalled CoreMark in 3,991,298 bracketed cycles versus 4,202,272,
a 5.02 percent cycle reduction. The unchanged evaluator passed exact
CRC/UART, completion, marker and bounds validation. Gowin placement
options 0/1/2 measured 64.336/64.234/64.234 MHz, median 64.234 MHz.
This implies about 160.94 iterations/second, 6.56 percent above 151.03.
A four-entry version saved slightly more cycles but reached only
62.310 MHz and failed the required fitness threshold. The two-entry
choice reduces payload to 102 bits plus two occupancy bits while
preserving most of the useful run-ahead.

The selected two-entry prototype passed all 53 unchanged single-channel
formal checks, including liveness, PC consistency, uniqueness and
register consistency. All eight full-RVFI comparisons of selftest and
random1/2/3 passed with ready buses and combined instruction/data stalls.
A 6,000-cycle independent IF queue/BHT model test passed, including
466 full pop/push events, 257 buffered deliveries during raw bus stalls,
572 recoveries and 3,241 boundary cycles. Strict Verilator lint passed.
Repeating all three Gowin options after a constant-width lint cleanup
reproduced the same frequencies. Option zero used 4,895 logic cells,
1,928 registers, zero LUT-RAM, four BSRAM and six DSP blocks.

These are exploratory measurements, not approval of the eventual RTL.
Require unchanged formal and RVFI cosim, directed queue tests, canonical
stalled CoreMark and all three vendor placement options on the final
implementation. Fitness must exceed 157.97738 iterations/second,
4.6 percent above 151.03; at 3,991,298 cycles this requires median Fmax
above 63.05348 MHz. Preserve nret=1, every port and all hard invariants.

title: Preselect writeback data feeding a shared signedness-controlled multiplier
motivation:
The champion scores 169.11 iter/s at 71.063 MHz with 4,202,272
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at ordinary
MEM/WB read_data and crosses writeback, forwarding and multiplication
before reaching EX/MEM alu_result. Prior micro_opt r8s0 reduced six DSPs
to two by sharing the product but remained limited by operand delivery.
The current champion has already shortened the divider recurrence.
Removing selection before and after multiplication is a focused next
step that preserves instruction timing and the current pipeline.

The champion scores 169.11 iter/s at 71.063 MHz with 4,202,272
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at ordinary
MEM/WB read_data and crosses writeback, forwarding and multiplication
before reaching EX/MEM alu_result. Prior micro_opt r8s0 reduced six DSPs
