hypothesis.hypothesis:
Shorten the existing combinational multiply path by selecting ordinary
load-versus-ALU writeback data before MEM/WB and selecting multiply
signedness before a single shared product. These changes address the
two selection costs surrounding the same critical arithmetic resource.
Keep all pipeline stages, instruction latencies, forwarding decisions,
branch prediction and the nret=1 interface unchanged.

Add a 32-bit wb_value field to mem_wb_t immediately after read_data.
On each advancing MEM edge capture
in.ctrl.mem_to_reg ? load_data : in.alu_result into wb_value, alongside
the existing control, destination and data fields. Reset clears it.
On hold_wb, retain wb_value exactly like the other ordinary WB payload
fields while clearing only valid. Keep the original alu_result and
read_data metadata for verification; synthesis may prune fields that
no longer feed architectural hardware. Do not add an extra data stage.

Drive core's normal_wb_data directly from mem_wb_w.wb_value. Make
wb_stage use the selected retirement bundle's wb_value directly,
preserving its write enable and destination rules. Populate direct
divide completion's wb_value with div_result alongside alu_result.
Direct divide completion continues to reach RF and write-first ID only;
EX forwarding must remain connected to retained ordinary WB data.
Never gate this retained data or ownership with retirement valid: an
older memory hold clears valid while held EX operands still need it.

Replace the three real signedness-specific products in alu.sv with
one signed 33x33 product. Declare signed [32:0] mul_a and mul_b, and
signed [65:0] mul_product. Set
mul_a={(op==ALU_MULH || op==ALU_MULHSU) && a[31],a};
mul_b={(op==ALU_MULH) && b[31],b};
mul_product=mul_a*mul_b.
MUL returns mul_product[31:0]. MULH, MULHU and MULHSU all return
mul_product[63:32] through the existing case-based ALU output mux.
The unused top two bits are intentional. Explicit signed declarations
and the 33-bit extensions preserve negative signed operands and the
full unsigned 32-bit range. Do not add a post-product sign-correction
subtraction, a second product, or a masked-OR ALU output tree.
Preserve every RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formula and constant exactly.

Retain the champion's existing EX forwarding case muxes followed by
AUIPC/PC and immediate operand muxes. Retain its combinational divide
classification from the registered opcode. Do not add operand-mask
registers, a predecoded divide flag, or flatten these muxes as part of
this hypothesis. Divider arithmetic, eight busy clocks, launch and
completion retention, dedicated effective addresses, memory handshakes,
x0, youngest-writer priority, trap-suppressed writers and single-channel
retirement remain exactly as before.

This moves the ordinary writeback mux away from the MEM/WB-to-multiply
feedback path, removes selection among three high-half products, and
reduces DSP operand fanout. Main risks are moving the limiting path
into load extraction before MEM/WB, synthesis rebuilding the writeback
mux after the register, or a nearly tied divider/branch path limiting
the total gain. Evaluate the actual vendor netlist and median Fmax;
resource reduction alone does not establish a fitness improvement.

Update the packed WB test layout without dropping any existing
assertions. Check wb_value against an independent selection of the
existing alu_result/read_data fields for every load width and sign,
ALU/load alternation, reset, and repeated holds after valid clears.
Exercise both operand ports from local, EX and WB sources, simultaneous
matches, x0, immediate/AUIPC overrides, load-use bubbles, branch recovery,
divide launch behind memory stalls, and direct completion to a younger
ID consumer. Keep ten-cycle liveness and exactly-once memory/retirement
checks. Extend real multiplication tests using independent full-width
integer products over signed extrema, high unsigned values, negative
by unsigned pairs, powers of two and seeded random pairs. Keep every
existing real and ALTOPS arithmetic and divider-protocol assertion.

Run unchanged formal gates and real/ALTOPS ALU and pipeline tests,
selftest RVFI cosimulation with ready and stalled buses, and canonical
CoreMark validation. Standard formal uses ALTOPS and is not proof of
real M arithmetic. CoreMark should retain exactly 4,202,272 bracketed
cycles for ten iterations under the same stall sequence, all five CRCs,
required UART text and address bounds. Acceptance requires fitness
strictly above 176.88906 iter/s, more than 4.6 percent above 169.11,
corresponding to approximately 74.334 MHz at the unchanged cycle count.
Do not change evaluator, benchmark, formal or interface contracts.

Preliminary exploration is negative evidence about nearby alternatives,
not a measured claim for this final circuit: preselected WB with flat
EX operand masks and the original multipliers reached 70.146 MHz.
Adding the shared multiplier to that flat-mux variant reached 73.606

title: Retimed multiply and unified registered completion in MEM
motivation:
The champion scores 169.11 iter/s at 71.063 MHz with 4,202,272 measured
CoreMark cycles. Its recorded worst path begins at MEM/WB read_data and
crosses writeback, EX forwarding and multiplication before returning to
EX/MEM alu_result (20.678 ns, 11 cells). Earlier structural changes have
already shortened division and registered forwarding selection. The r8s0
multiplier-sharing attempt still exposed forwarding-to-product timing.
Move the multiply operation across an existing register boundary so its
clock period no longer includes operand delivery. This targets the newly
exposed bottleneck without adding a stage to ordinary ALU or branch work.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 169.11 iter/s at 71.063 MHz with 4,202,272 measured
CoreMark cycles. Its recorded worst path begins at MEM/WB read_data and
crosses writeback, EX forwarding and multiplication before returning to
EX/MEM alu_result (20.678 ns, 11 cells). Earlier structural changes have
already shortened division and registered forwarding selection. The r8s0
multiplier-sharing attempt still exposed forwarding-to-product timing.

clock period no longer includes operand delivery. This targets the newly
exposed bottleneck without adding a stage to ordinary ALU or branch work.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one structural change: execute MUL, MULH, MULHU and MULHSU in MEM
from registered EX/MEM operands, and register their selected result at
MEM/WB. EX continues to forward and capture their source values, but no
live combinational multiply result feeds EX/MEM in the timed core.
Reuse the existing post-forward rs1_val and rs2_val fields as physical
multiplier operand registers. Capture multiply ownership with the same
reset, bubble and dmem-hold rules as the rest of EX/MEM. Ordinary ALU,
branches, effective-address generation, direct divide retirement and
the eight-iteration divider keep their present boundaries and behavior.

Factor the current real multiply equations and exact ALTOPS formulas into
one portable combinational multiply module declared in alu.sv so the
existing explicit unit-test source lists still compile. Instantiate it in MEM for the
core. Keep standalone ALU arithmetic tests meaningful by giving alu a
default-enabled compile-time multiply parameter; EX disables it so no
redundant combinational multiplier remains in its result cone. Preserve
the existing signed/signed, unsigned/unsigned and signed/unsigned product
semantics and widths. Do not combine this retiming with multiplier sharing,
a new divider, a predictor change or a fetch queue. The physical change is
moving multiplication after registered operands, not changing its math.

Complete result selection BEFORE the MEM/WB register: capture load_data
for a load, the completed product for a multiply, or the existing ALU
result otherwise into MEM/WB.alu_result, now the unified completed value.
Drive normal_wb_data and wb_stage.w_data directly from that registered
value; do not retain a post-register mem_to_reg mux. Keep read_data and
memory/RVFI fields as needed for verification, but the timed bypass and
RF paths use the one completed-result register. Direct divide completion
already places its result in alu_result and retains its arbitration.
No multiply asserts a memory request. Keep RF writeback and ordinary WB forwarding as
the only consumers of the completed product; do not introduce a live
MEM-product-to-EX bypass, which would recreate a long combinational path.
An older stalled memory instruction holds the multiply in ID/EX with its
forwarding sources intact until operands can be captured. Once the multiply
occupies EX/MEM it generates no dmem hold and advances once into MEM/WB,
with matching RVFI metadata and the existing hold semantics.

Reuse the existing hazard_unit logic, driving its id_ex_mem_read input
from core with mem_read OR (valid AND multiply_opcode). Treat multiplication
as a late-result producer exactly like a load for
the one-cycle immediate-use interlock. A valid multiply in ID/EX whose
nonzero rd matches either incoming raw source field holds fetch and
injects an inert ID/EX bubble, unless an older dmem or execute wait takes
hold priority. Reuse existing conservative source matching rather than
adding an unrelated decoder optimization. Disallow EX/MEM forwarding
ownership for a multiply: its result is unavailable there. On the next
advancing edge, the dependent instruction captures a MEM/WB forwarding
selector and then receives the registered product. Preserve youngest-
writer priority, x0 handling, trap-cancelled ownership and retained normal
WB data during memory holds. Back-to-back independent multiplies still
issue and retire one per cycle; a directly dependent pair has one bubble.
All four multiply opcodes follow the same schedule under ALTOPS.

Keep nret=1, in-order single retirement and exact +1 RVFI order. Preserve
all legality, alignment, memory-handshake and branch-recovery invariants.
A divide following multiplication launches only with the correct completed
operand, and the existing direct-completion arbiter must still retire
older ordinary WB first. Check the unchanged ten-cycle liveness bound,
especially multiply-to-divide, load-to-divide and consecutive divides.

The intended gain is higher Fmax from separating WB mux/forwarding from
the multiplier. CoreMark cycles can rise only through the new multiply-use
bubbles and resulting stall-sequence interactions; measure that cost.
Acceptance requires median Gowin Fmax times actual marked iterations/cycle
strictly above 176.88906 iter/s, more than 4.6 percent above 169.11.
At unchanged cycles that requires approximately 74.3336 MHz, and the
required frequency scales proportionally with the measured cycle count.
A full-width product may still limit timing after the move; divider or
branch paths may also become limiting. These are risks to measure, not
reasons to append unrelated architectural changes.

Retain every existing arithmetic and architectural assertion. Validate
all four real multiply variants against independent exact integer results,
including signed extremes, high-bit unsigned operands, mixed signedness
and seeded random vectors, and preserve exact ALTOPS constants. Exercise
dependent and independent multiply streams; MUL-to-ALU/branch/JALR/load/
store/divide; load/ALU-to-MUL forwarding; two writes to one destination;
x0; wrong-path multiplies; reset; and ready plus stalled buses. Assert one
immediate-use bubble, no bubble for independent multiplies, exact RVFI
operands/results, ordered single retirement and no duplicated stores.
Run the unchanged formal and full-RVFI cosimulation gates and canonical
CoreMark CRC/UART/address/marker checks. Standard formal uses ALTOPS and
does not prove real multiplication; keep real arithmetic unit tests and
cosimulation and run formal-deep when feasible. Verify in vendor timing
that the multiply starts at EX/MEM operand registers and ends at MEM/WB,
then report median fitness and resources rather than extrapolated Fmax.

Preliminary prototype evidence: moving only multiplication to MEM while
retaining the post-WB load/ALU mux measured 72.039 MHz median and 4,238,604
marked cycles, insufficient for the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold.
Its worst paths moved to WB-to-branch recovery. The final proposal therefore
makes result selection part of this same MEM completion boundary, before
registration, so EX consumes a single registered WB result. This is an
essential part of the proposed topology, not an optional cleanup.
With the unified result register, canonical CoreMark still completes in
4,238,604 marked cycles (0.8646 percent more than the champion), passing
all CRCs, UART, address and marker checks. This measured cycle count
requires median Fmax above approximately 74.976 MHz for acceptance.
The refined prototype passed lint, real and ALTOPS full-core pipeline
suites, the memory-stage unit suite, directed real and ALTOPS multiply
dependency tests, and selftest plus three random programs under full RVFI
comparison both with ready buses and combined instruction/data stalls.
The real and ALTOPS standalone ALU suites passed for the same factored
multiplier. The two pipeline assertions tied to the previous representation
were updated as specified below, preserving independent correctness checks.
Prototype measurements must be repeated by the final implementation.

Final prototype vendor results for the complete proposed boundary:
Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured 70.405 / 75.646 / 75.646 MHz,
median 75.646 MHz. With ten iterations in 4,238,604 marked cycles this
gives 178.46914 iter/s, a 5.53435 percent improvement over 169.11 and
above the required 176.88906. The netlist used 5,167 logic cells,
1,830 registers, zero LUT-RAM, four BSRAM and six DSP blocks. The
multiplier is no longer on the reported worst paths: option zero is
limited by operand-to-recovery/control, while options one/two expose
divide-completion control into write-first operand capture. All 53
unchanged nret=1 standard formal checks passed on this final variant.
They use ALTOPS; formal-deep was not run. The margin above acceptance
is modest, so preserve the specified structure and repeat median timing.
All temporary prototype RTL/test edits were restored after measurement;
this file is the implementation proposal, not an already-applied change.

title: Pipeline branch-predictor training to isolate execute fanout
motivation:
Direct prediction already removes most branch bubbles. Earlier trace
replay found only 54,467 conditional misses in 4,202,272 CoreMark cycles,
making accuracy alone unlikely to clear the 4.6 percent threshold.
Fresh experiments on this champion also reject another stream queue:
two entries reached 3,991,298 cycles but only 66.228 MHz median; three
entries with registered-capacity admission reached 3,988,312 cycles but
only 67.208 MHz. Their saved cycles did not compensate for timing cost.
Several near-critical paths run from forwarded EX operands through
branch resolution into the BHT counter registers. The current branch
result and advancing enable directly drive 128 local counter updates.
Isolating that training fanout is a smaller, previously untried predictor
change that leaves the instruction delivery datapath intact.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one clock of pipelining to BHT training inside if_stage. Register a
nine-bit event consisting of valid, branch_pc[8:2], and branch_taken.
Each clock capture valid = branch_update, including zero on cycles
without an advancing legal branch. Capture index and outcome only when
branch_update is asserted. Reset clears the pending event. Keep the
existing EX generation of branch_update: only a valid, legal, nontrapping
conditional branch that advances can emit an event. Do not change EX
recovery, branch comparisons, operand forwarding or pipeline holds.

Update each of the existing 128 two-bit counters from the PREVIOUS
registered event rather than directly from EX. Keep local per-counter
saturation logic, PC indexing, weakly-not-taken reset and the current
table read structure. At every edge, consume the old event once and
independently capture the next event, permitting one resolved branch
per cycle with no backpressure. Pending training must drain even while
EX or instruction fetch is held; it represents an already resolved
instruction. A recovery must not cancel its legal resolving branch's
training. Reset alone cancels pending training and initializes counters.

The resolving condition then drives one outcome flop, and the EX
advancement event drives the small event register, rather than a wide
bank of counter enables and state transitions. Counter decode and
saturation begin at the new local register boundary. This removes
predictor-update fanout from the late forwarded-operand branch path
without adding a fetch-stage mux, speculative queue or recovery bubble.
Implement the event as scalar fabric flops; do not introduce a RAM,
read-modify-write counter port or table-size change.

Deliberately allow the direction table to be one resolution event older.
Do not add an EX-to-fetch or pending-update prediction bypass, which
would recreate the timing connection. Fetch still reads pre-edge
counters, predicts legal aligned in-range BRANCH/JAL targets using the
existing guards, and freezes exactly the token used to advance PC.
EX checks that saved token using the unchanged direction-XOR recovery
and offset-four exception. Thus training latency may change prediction
accuracy, but cannot change architectural next PCs, trap behavior,
retirement or memory effects. Sequential JALR prediction is unchanged.

Preserve the current 32-bit target/address semantics, nret=1, divider
protocol, register-file and forwarding implementation, bus handshakes,
RVFI and all correctness gates. In particular, neither correct-prediction
issue nor misprediction recovery gains an extra pipeline clock.

This is a timing hypothesis, not a demonstrated fitness improvement.
The champion's worst path also crosses writeback and multiplication;
that unchanged path may limit any benefit from reduced predictor fanout.
Closely spaced branches that alias in the BHT can suffer extra misses
from delayed training. Expect a modest Fmax improvement with little
cycle change, but confidence is low until vendor timing is measured.
At the existing 4,202,272-cycle count, acceptance requires median Fmax
above 74.333 MHz; recompute that threshold using the measured cycle
count if prediction timing changes it. Require fitness strictly above
176.88906 iterations/second, more than 4.6 percent above 169.11.

Validate an independent cycle-accurate delayed-training table model,
existing formal, real/ALTOPS unit tests, ready/stalled full-RVFI cosim
and canonical stalled CoreMark. Preserve all canonical CRCs, UART text,
address bounds, timing markers and retirement-liveness checks. Measure
all three Gowin placement options on the eventual implementation.

title: Four-bit branch comparison tree with factored condition selection
motivation:
The champion scores 177.89 iter/s at 75.4 MHz with 4,238,604 marked CoreMark
cycles. Its recorded worst path runs from an ID/EX operand through EX
recovery into forwarding-selector control. Prior micro_opt attempts focused
on arithmetic and operand delivery; the latest MEM-multiply champion exposes
control resolution. Local experiments show full-width branch ordering
comparison on deep operand-to-recovery paths. Target the comparator and its
trailing condition mux as one local Boolean-mapping problem, preserving
pipeline and prediction behavior.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 177.89 iter/s at 75.4 MHz with 4,238,604 marked CoreMark
cycles. Its recorded worst path runs from an ID/EX operand through EX
recovery into forwarding-selector control. Prior micro_opt attempts focused
on arithmetic and operand delivery; the latest MEM-multiply champion exposes
control resolution. Local experiments show full-width branch ordering
comparison on deep operand-to-recovery paths. Target the comparator and its
trailing condition mux as one local Boolean-mapping problem, preserving

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only EX branch condition generation with a balanced tree of eight
parallel unsigned four-bit comparisons, followed by a factored condition
selector. This is one micro_opt of the branch decision cone. Keep forwarded
operands, target adders, alignment handling, direction-token recovery, BHT
state/encoding/training, squash rules and all instruction latencies
unchanged. Do not change ALU SLT/SLTU, multiplication, division or any
pipeline boundary.

For nibble j=0..7, compute E[j]=(rs1[4*j+:4]==rs2[4*j+:4]) and
L[j]=(rs1[4*j+:4]<rs2[4*j+:4]) in parallel. Combine adjacent high/low groups
using E=E_hi AND E_lo and L=L_hi OR (E_hi AND L_lo). Build exactly three
balanced levels: eight nibbles to four bytes, four bytes to two halfwords,
then one word. Use explicit named wires or a constant-index generate tree,
not a serial priority accumulator. Root E is equality and root L is
unsigned_less. Four-bit groups bound each local carry chain and fit the
target FPGA's small logic cells; measure the extra tree level against that
reduction.

Factor the final six-condition case into the RV32 branch funct3 bits,
avoiding separate signed/unsigned comparators and duplicated inverted
condition selection. Let f=in.ctrl.branch_op and signs_differ=rs1[31] XOR
rs2[31]. Compute ordered_less = signs_differ ? (rs1[31] XOR f[1]) :
unsigned_less. For ordering branches, f[1]=0 selects signed and f[1]=1
selects unsigned. Compute selected = f[2] ? ordered_less : equal, then
branch_cond = (f[2] OR !f[1]) AND (selected XOR f[0]). This implements
BEQ/BNE for f=0/1, signed BLT/BGE for f=4/5, unsigned BLTU/BGEU for f=6/7,
and exactly false for reserved f=2/3. Preserve this default behavior even in
stage-local tests that drive otherwise illegal controls. These factored
equations are part of the proposal, not merely changing comparison group
width.

The intended gain is fewer dependent carry and mux levels between forwarded
operands and branch outcome/recovery, without a cycle, prediction, or
throughput penalty. Do not alter branch_update qualifications or move
training in time. Preserve nret=1, trap-cancelled writes, held WB
forwarding, memory handshakes, decoder legality, exact RVFI order and the
ten-cycle liveness limit. The original table and all M-extension arithmetic
remain intact.

Validate the complete branch_cond function against the original full-width
case for arbitrary two 32-bit operands and all eight funct3 values,
preferably with a combinational SAT equivalence miter. Test equality,
opposite signs, signed extrema, every most-significant differing nibble,
lower nibbles that disagree with the winning high nibble, and both EX/MEM
and MEM/WB forwarding sources. Retain existing recovery-token equivalence,
reserved/misaligned branch, predictor, load/multiply-use, dmem-hold, imem-
stall and exact retirement assertions. Run lint, real/ALTOPS pipeline tests,
unchanged formal, full-RVFI ready/stalled selftest and canonical CoreMark
CRC/UART/address/marker checks.

Evidence and limits: a temporary four-BYTE comparator retaining the original
branch-op case was correct by SAT, all 53 standard formal checks, existing
pipeline tests and CoreMark, but measured only 74.995 MHz median. Isolated
payload/squash separation reached 72.94 MHz. Counter Boolean rewriting and
Gray recoding also regressed; combining byte comparison with Gray counters
reached 68.764 MHz despite passing all 53 formal checks, 11 pipeline
configurations and canonical CoreMark. Those variants are excluded. The
final proposal uses four-BIT groups and explicitly factored sign/condition
selection, with the original predictor unchanged. Its full vendor timing has
not been measured, and no earlier prototype result is claimed as its
performance. Confidence is low because divider or remaining branch fanout
may limit the gain.

Expect the same 4,238,604 bracketed CoreMark cycles for the same bus-stall
sequence. Acceptance requires measured median Gowin Fmax times actual
iterations/cycle strictly above 186.07294 iter/s, more than 4.6 percent
above 177.89; about 78.869 MHz is needed at unchanged cycles. Report the
actual score and critical paths rather than assuming that shorter local
arithmetic guarantees acceptance. All temporary RTL and test edits from
exploration are restored; this file is the implementation proposal.

title: Register control-transfer recovery at the EX/MEM boundary
motivation:
The champion reaches 177.89 iterations/s at 75.4 MHz and 4,238,604
marked CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at ID/EX rs1,
traverses EX, and ends at a forwarding-selector register. The current
combinational EX recovery drives front-end squash, while JALR target
alignment also feeds next-EX/MEM forwarding ownership. Both paths put
operand selection and control-transfer arithmetic ahead of decode
control. Structural history shows that retiming operand delivery
(r7s1) and multiply completion (r9s1) improves timing. Earlier validity
separation (r4s1) did not add a recovery register, and delayed BHT
training alone (r9s2) regressed. This proposal instead removes the
late EX-to-front-end control connection at an existing pipeline boundary.

register file, multiply completion and eight-iteration divider. EX still
computes branch conditions, JAL/JALR targets, alignment faults, actual
next PC and direction-token mismatch. Capture a recovery-valid token,
recovery target, and legal conditional-branch training event with the
advancing instruction in EX/MEM. Drive PC redirection, ID squash and
BHT training only from this registered event. A correctly predicted
transfer keeps full throughput; a misprediction costs one additional
recovery cycle. Emit each event once, qualified by valid stage ownership
and consumption, never merely by retained payload bits.

Implement this inside ex_stage.sv with two scalar flops, recovery_q and
training_q, alongside the existing EX/MEM reg_q. Reuse reg_q.pc_next as
redirect_target, reg_q.pc as branch_pc and reg_q.branch_taken as
branch_outcome. No bundle, top-level wiring or pipeline stage needs to
be added. Drive redirect = reg_q.valid && recovery_q && !reset && !stall
and branch_update = reg_q.valid && training_q && !reset && !stall.
Reset clears both event flops; stall holds them. Otherwise capture
recovery_q = advance && (direct_miss || indirect_miss || misalign_fault)
and training_q = advance && in.ctrl.is_branch && !in.ctrl.is_illegal
&& !misalign_fault. Use the existing direction-token comparison and
actual-next-PC calculation unchanged.

Recovery from the older EX/MEM instruction must suppress the younger
instruction currently in EX as well as the fetched/decode instruction.
On the recovery edge, redirect PC and clear ID/EX; replace the next
EX/MEM entry with a fully inert bubble. Preserve the recovering
instruction's transfer to ordinary MEM/WB and retirement. Gate younger
divider launch, direct divide consumption, branch training and all EX
advancement with the older recovery token. No wrong-path memory request
may enter EX/MEM. Give older recovery priority over a younger divide
wait or load/multiply dependency, and preserve recovery through an imem
stall. Keep actual older memory transactions and retained WB forwarding
stable during dmem backpressure. Only latch EX events when EX/MEM can
accept the instruction; reset clears every pending event.

Concretely, add !redirect to div_request and advance, and make
execute_wait = is_divide && !redirect && (!div_done || normal_wb_valid).
The existing hazard unit then squashes ID/EX even when the killed EX
instruction is a divide; its existing flush-over-dependency-hold priority
suffices. In the EX/MEM update, retain reset then stall priority, and
change the bubble arm to is_divide || redirect. Keep the other stage
updates unchanged. Do not freeze MEM/WB on recovery.

Remove the second late operand-to-decode path as part of this same
recovery boundary. Compute speculative next-EX/MEM forwarding ownership
from the incoming instruction's valid decoded reg_write and the existing
divide/multiply exclusions, without combinational JALR alignment or
resolved-branch control. Register actual trap-suppressed reg_write in
EX/MEM as before. Every misaligned control transfer must now schedule
registered recovery to its architectural fall-through, even if that
equals its prediction. Thus any younger instruction whose speculative
forwarding selection assumed a trapping JALR would write is killed
before executing or launching a divider. The refetched fall-through
reads the preserved architectural destination value. This mandatory
recovery on target-alignment traps is essential for correctness, not
an optional performance choice. Leave MEM's next-WB ownership based on
its actual trap-suppressed writer; do not gate retained WB ownership
with its already-cleared retirement pulse.

The exact speculative qualifier is in.valid && in.ctrl.reg_write &&
!is_divide && !is_multiply. Do not put redirect or misalign_fault in
this qualifier: recovery already squashes the captured selectors and
younger instruction. Leave forward_unit's comparisons and register
update priority unchanged.

Preserve the frozen prediction token, direct offset-plus-four exception,
full JALR target comparison and full 32-bit PC semantics. Legal branch
training travels with the same EX/MEM completion boundary and occurs
exactly once; do not add another predictor stage, prediction bypass,
table change or fetch queue. Illegal or misaligned control transfers
must not train. Traps retain the existing RVFI fall-through and suppressed
link write. Preserve decoder legality defaults, memory alignment traps,
all arithmetic including ALTOPS, nret=1 and exact in-order RVFI fields.

The intended gain is a shorter clock period from removing forwarded
compare/target-add/recovery and alignment/write-owner chains from the
front-end register inputs. The cost is an extra bubble on recovery and
one-cycle-later predictor training. Prior branch-trace evidence suggests
conditional misses are a small part of total cycles, but JALR frequency,
training changes and the fixed stall sequence must also be measured.
A temporary prototype of exactly the ex_stage-only topology above
measured 4,306,908 canonical marked cycles, a 1.6115 percent increase.
Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured 80.105 / 80.265 / 80.265 MHz,
median 80.265 MHz. Ten iterations at that rate imply 186.36340 iter/s,
a 4.7633 percent improvement over 177.89. The netlist used 5,152 logic
cells, 1,873 registers, zero LUT-RAM, four BSRAM and six DSP blocks.
Reported worst paths moved to the unchanged divider recurrence, with
ordinary forwarding-to-ALU paths close behind. The measured gain clears
acceptance narrowly; preserve the specified structure and repeat timing
after implementation rather than assuming a comfortable margin.

The prototype passed lint, all 53 unchanged nret=1 standard formal
checks, and full-RVFI selftest plus three random programs with ready and
stalled buses. Canonical CoreMark passed all CRC/UART/address/marker
checks. A separate directed full-RVFI program passed with both bus modes,
covering misaligned JAL/JALR and taken-branch traps, preserved trapped
destinations, wrong-path DIV/load/store/multiply, recovered DIV/REM and
consecutive divides. Standard formal uses ALTOPS; formal-deep was not
run. The unchanged standalone ALU suites passed in both real and ALTOPS
modes. Existing pipeline unit tests still need their stage-specific timing
oracles updated as described below. Prototype measurements do not replace
final implementation verification. Temporary RTL edits are restored;
the deliverable is this proposal.

Validate the unchanged ten-cycle retirement-liveness bound, especially
a recovered target beginning with DIV/REM, JALR-to-divide, trapped JALR
followed by a destination consumer, and consecutive divides. Add directed
wrong-path load/store/multiply/divide cases, taken/not-taken predictions,
+4 targets, misaligned taken branches and JAL/JALR, repeated memory
stalls, recovery with unavailable imem, reset and overlapping register
writers. Check exact RVFI PCs, operands, results, trap and +1 order;
stable accepted memory requests; no wrong-path divide start or training;
and exactly one extra bubble per recovery with ready buses. Adapt
stage-timing assertions to the new boundary while retaining every
architectural and arithmetic check. Run unchanged formal, real/ALTOPS
pipeline tests, full-RVFI ready/stalled cosimulation and canonical
CoreMark CRC/UART/address/marker checks. Use all scored Gowin placement
options and actual marked cycles. Acceptance requires fitness strictly
above 186.07294 iterations/s, more than 4.6 percent above 177.89.

title: Predecode predictor recovery tokens before forwarded branch resolution
motivation:
The champion reaches 177.89 iterations/second at 75.4 MHz and 4,238,604
bracketed cycles. Its reported worst path starts at ID/EX rs1_val and
ends at a registered forwarding selector, through execute and decode.
JALR currently forms a forwarded base-plus-immediate target, checks its
alignment, and compares it with PC+4 before permitting recovery. Target
alignment also controls the forwarding ownership signal through
ctrl_with_trap.reg_write. These are candidate late paths into the
younger instruction's squash and forwarding controls.
Prior predictor attempts established that accuracy has little headroom:
branch replay found about 54,467 conditional misses and 13,735 JALRs in
4.2 million cycles. Repeated fetch queues lost their cycle advantage to
timing costs, and delayed BHT training regressed to 67.487 MHz. The
successful direction-token recovery experiment instead shortened control
dependencies. Extend that principle by predecoding direct recovery
classification and making sequentially predicted JALR recovery depend
on decoded instruction kind, without adding a prediction table or stage.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move predictor-recovery classification into the existing ID/EX boundary.
Preserve the 128-entry bimodal predictor and its exact training policy.
At decode, freeze three recovery fields with the accepted instruction:
branch_prediction_xor = predicted_direct XOR decoded branch_op[0];
recovery_branch_check = legal conditional branch AND direct-target
alignment AND immediate != 4; and recovery_static_miss = immediate != 4
AND ((legal direct JAL AND (direct_aligned XOR predicted_direct)) OR
(legal conditional branch AND NOT direct_aligned AND predicted_direct)).
Compute alignment from the two low bits of PC plus immediate with
explicit modulo-four arithmetic. All fields reset/squash to zero and
hold with the instruction under backpressure; never reread the BHT.

Normalize EX's branch comparison to one equality result or one unsigned
less-than result. For ordered branches, XOR bit 31 of both forwarded
operands with NOT branch_op[1] before the unsigned comparison: this
biases signed BLT/BGE into unsigned order and leaves BLTU/BGEU unchanged.
Let branch_base select equality for BEQ/BNE, otherwise that less-than
result. Actual branch_cond is branch_base XOR branch_op[0], retaining
the reserved-funct3 default. Direct recovery instead uses
recovery_static_miss OR (recovery_branch_check AND
(branch_base XOR branch_prediction_xor)). Thus target alignment,
instruction-kind qualification, the offset-four exception and branch
polarity/prediction combination are already registered when forwarded
operands arrive. Architectural resolution and training still use the
actual branch condition. Leave the general ALU comparator untouched.

Make JALR recovery unconditional on an advancing, valid legal JALR,
while retaining sequential fetch prediction. Treat every such JALR as
an execute-stage recovery event, independent of its computed target,
whether it equals PC+4, or whether it is misaligned. This deliberately
spends one recovery bubble even for a JALR targeting PC+4 or trapping
on misalignment. Ordinary nonsequential aligned JALRs already recover,
so their cycle cost is unchanged. The hypothesis targets Fmax by
removing forwarded target arithmetic and wide equality comparison from
recovery enable, not by claiming better indirect prediction accuracy.

Keep actual_next_pc and redirect_target fully architectural: an aligned
JALR redirects to (forwarded_rs1 + imm) with bit zero cleared; a
misaligned JALR traps, suppresses its link-register write, and recovers
to PC+4 exactly as required by the current core. Preserve full-width
address arithmetic and all RVFI fields. Only recovery enable is early;
do not add a clock to target generation or retirement.

Partition direct and indirect recovery structurally. Do not feed the
shared misalign_fault, which includes rs1-dependent JALR alignment,
into the registered direct-recovery tokens or their EX predicate.
Existing IF alignment/range guards and frozen prediction continue to
handle refused out-of-range predictions exactly. Keep BHT training
qualified by the advancing legal conditional branch and its own
misalignment test, preserving training for an untaken branch whose
hypothetical target is misaligned. Keep the table and counter equations.

Cut the complementary JALR target-alignment path to the registered
forwarding selectors as part of the same recovery protocol. On JALR,
use next_ex_mem_w_en = decoded reg_write AND NOT is_divide AND NOT
is_multiply AND NOT (direct_JAL AND direct_target_misaligned).
Do not mux the shared ctrl_with_trap.reg_write back into this hint:
that can preserve the unwanted rs1-to-ownership timing cone. Conditional
branches already decode with reg_write zero; direct misaligned JALs
still lose forwarding ownership. This is ONLY the speculative
next-owner hint used while preparing younger ID/EX forwarding; keep
architectural EX/MEM control and every actual write suppressed on trap.
It is safe because every advancing JALR unconditionally squashes that
younger ID/EX instruction and clears both forwarding selectors; while
JALR is held, forwarding capture is disabled. Preserve the existing
trap-aware ownership for other instructions and all load/multiply/divide
availability rules. Assert this implication explicitly in tests.

Preserve advance gating, reset, older dmem hold priority, divider holds,
and recovery priority over imem stall and load-use. Recovery must clear
ID/EX controls as well as validity, keep redirect out of instruction-bit
masking, and never permit a wrong-path store, register write or retirement.
No fetch queue, RAS, BHT-size/training change, pipeline stage, arithmetic
retiming, interface change or nret change belongs to this proposal.

An isolated prototype of this complete recovery-token design measured
77.196/80.437/80.437 MHz across Gowin placement options 0/1/2, median
80.437 MHz. Canonical stalled CoreMark retained exactly 4,238,604
marker-bracketed cycles for ten iterations, with all CRC/UART/completion,
address-bound and marker checks passing. This implies 189.77239
iterations/second, 6.68 percent above 177.89. Option zero used 4,964
logic cells and 1,832 registers, versus 5,067 and 1,831 in the champion;
LUT-RAM/BSRAM/DSP counts remained 0/4/6. The additional token fields
replace timed uses of old prediction metadata, so their net register
cost is small rather than three entirely additional timed bits.

The prototype passed strict Verilator lint, both real and ALTOPS
pipeline suites, the direct-recovery equivalence unit test, and a
decode-token test covering all branch funct3 values, aligned/misaligned
PCs, offset four, signed offsets, boundary/wrapped targets, holds and
squash. All eight full-RVFI selftest/random-program comparisons passed
across ready and jointly stalled buses. All 53 unchanged single-channel
riscv-formal checks passed, including liveness, uniqueness, PC and
register consistency. Arithmetic implementation is unchanged.

These are prototype results, not approval of the eventual implementation.
The late JALR target still drives the fetch-PC data input, and direct
branch comparisons remain. Extra recovery on a fall-through or trapping
JALR can cost cycles on other instruction streams. Preserve every gate
and rerun real/ALTOPS tests, formal, full-RVFI cosim, canonical stalled
CoreMark and all three vendor placement options on the final RTL.
Final fitness must be strictly above 186.07294 iterations/second,
exceeding 177.89 by more than 4.6 percent. At the measured cycle count
this requires median Fmax above 78.868951 MHz; recompute if cycles change.

implementation_notes:
# Predictor recovery tokens

Implemented the complete recovery-token protocol in `cores/bench/rtl/core_pkg.sv`,
`id_stage.sv`, and `ex_stage.sv`. Extended only `cores/bench/test/test_pipeline.py`.

## Implementation

- ID/EX now freezes `branch_prediction_xor`, `recovery_branch_check`, and
  `recovery_static_miss` with the accepted instruction. Direct alignment uses a
  two-bit PC-plus-immediate sum, explicitly truncated modulo four. Existing
  reset/squash/hold priority applies to the complete bundle. Original prediction
  metadata is retained for independent checks.
- EX shares one equality comparison and one unsigned ordered comparison, with
  both operand sign bits biased for signed branches. Branch polarity is applied
  with XOR; reserved branch funct3 values retain the false architectural outcome.
  Direct recovery uses only the registered tokens and the base comparison.
- Every advancing valid legal JALR recovers, including sequential and misaligned
  targets. Full-width target arithmetic, bit-zero clearing, trap fall-through,
  architectural link-write suppression, and RVFI remain unchanged.
- The speculative EX/MEM forwarding-owner hint uses decoded register-write
  ownership, divide/multiply exclusions, and direct-JAL alignment only. It has no
  dependency on JALR alignment or shared trap controls. Architectural EX/MEM
  controls remain trap-aware. Tests explicitly require that an advancing JALR
  squashes all younger ID/EX controls and both forwarding selectors, and that a
  held JALR disables capture and recovery.
- BHT training uses the advancing legal conditional branch and its own taken
  target-misalignment test. The 128-entry table and all counter equations are
  unchanged, including training untaken branches with misaligned hypothetical
  targets.

Implementation detail relative to the formulas: decode legality is established
by the existing validated `dec_is_branch` and `dec_is_jump` kind flags rather than
adding redundant `!dec_is_illegal` terms. The decoder is unchanged; reserved
branch and JALR encodings are explicitly tested. This equivalent factoring gave
the best measured timing. Less successful combinational expressions were
discarded; the final ordered comparison is a single full-width unsigned `<`.

The declared `nret: 1` interface is unchanged. No arithmetic unit, pipeline stage,
fetch queue, predictor table, interface, retirement path, or evaluation contract
was modified.

## Final RTL verification

- Strict Verilator lint: PASS, both real and `RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS` configurations.
- `pytest -q cores/bench/test/`: **15 passed**, including both real/ALTOPS pipeline
  and arithmetic suites, direct-recovery equivalence, decode tokens, forwarding,
  reset/hold/squash, decoder legality, and hazard-priority checks.
- `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=8 bash formal/run_all.sh`:
  **53 passed, 0 failed** on the final RTL. No failing formal attempt or
  counterexample; no formal fix retries were needed.
- `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench`: PASS, five ELFs. Selftest and all three random
  programs passed full-RVFI comparison in both ready and jointly stalled modes
  (eight comparisons). Canonical stalled CoreMark passed CRC, UART validation,
  completion, address-bound, and timing-marker checks. `make bench TARGET=bench`
  built the random-program ELFs before the final cosim run.
- The initial plain `make cosim` invocation defaulted its harness to NRET=2 and
  failed to compile against this NRET=1 core. Supplying the existing NRET=1 build
  setting resolved the harness configuration without changing its sources.
- `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options`: all three final placement
  options succeeded with the unchanged vendor evaluation flow.

## Final measured fitness

| Placement option | Fmax (MHz) |
| --- | ---: |
| 0 | 77.823 |
| 1 | 82.887 |
| 2 | 82.887 |

Median Fmax: **82.887 MHz**.

Canonical CoreMark: **10 iterations / 4,238,604 marker-bracketed cycles**, exactly
the champion's cycle count. Final fitness:

`82.887e6 * 10 / 4,238,604 = 195.55259231577188 iterations/second`.

This exceeds **186.07294 iterations/second**, and improves on 177.89 by
**9.92894%**. At this cycle count the required median is 78.868951 MHz.

Option-zero resources: **5,048 logic cells, 1,832 registers, 0 LUT-RAM, 4 BSRAM,
6 DSP**. Its worst reported setup path starts at the benchmark instruction LFSR
and ends at ID/EX `recovery_static_miss`, through IF and ID.

## Remaining considerations

JALR target arithmetic still drives the fetch-PC data input. The deliberate
recovery bubble for a sequential or trapping JALR can cost cycles on instruction
streams other than this CoreMark workload. Placement results are sensitive to
equivalent combinational factoring; the numbers above are measurements of the
final RTL, not the supplied prototype's results.

Final RTL fingerprint (`sha256sum cores/bench/rtl/*.sv | sha256sum`):
`f12aac79ecd272c2c4d79f76861efe153b88470eea91f3dfda2b9d5c19ae9f43`.
lesson: - 2026-10-03 hyp-20261003-003-r10s2 (improvement, +9.93%): Predecoding direct recovery into ID/EX tokens and unconditionally recovering legal JALRs lets squash and speculative next_ex_mem_w_en bypass forwarded target arithmetic/alignment, improving Fmax with unchanged CoreMark cycles; the owner hint remains safe only when advancing JALRs clear younger ID/EX controls and forwarding selectors while held JALRs disable capture.

title: Squash-independent capture of the two ID/EX operand words
motivation:
The champion scores 195.55 iter/s at 82.887 MHz with 4,238,604 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. A fresh three-option Gowin run reproduced exactly
77.823/82.887/82.887 MHz. The median placement's worst paths start at
ordinary WB data, cross forwarded branch comparison and recovery, and
end at forwarding-selector reset or ID/EX reset. The shared final ID
control drives 161 loads in that report. Squashing the entire packed
ID/EX bundle places operands, PC, immediate and metadata on this late
control even though zero validity and zero controls already suppress
all architectural effects.
Prior micro_opt r4s0 demonstrated correctness and a 17.6 percent gain
for payload/control separation on an earlier core, but lost its round.
A nearby r10s0 prototype regressed on the previous recovery design, so
this is a timing-sensitive hypothesis for the current token-based core,
not a claim that removing a mux necessarily improves vendor placement.

Exploration on the current core found that separating every payload field
reached only 79.078 MHz on placement option 1 versus 82.887 MHz for the
champion; its limiting path moved to divide-completion/write-first operand
capture. Narrow the change to the sixty-four operand bits, preserving the
existing PC, recovery-token and decoded-control register implementation.
This final narrower circuit has not been timed.

title: Radix-16 divider with an independent completion grant
motivation: The champion scores 195.55 iterations/s at 82.887 MHz with 4,238,604 marked CoreMark cycles. Structural history r5s0/r8s1 demonstrated the value of parallel digit trials and overlapping divisor preparation with the narrow first nibble. The current divider nevertheless cascades two wide radix-4 subtract/select networks on each of seven iteration clocks. The r10s1 timing report and exploratory timing in this slot expose that recurrence as a near-critical limit. The current approximately 5,048 LUT4s leave area headroom for replacing serial arithmetic depth with parallel hardware. CoreMark's measured interval contains no division, so a clock improvement translates directly to fitness if the existing schedule is preserved.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the shared DIV/REM resource around a shorter recurrence and its own registered completion token: replace the two cascaded radix-4 digits with one radix-16 digit selected from fifteen parallel divisor trials. Keep exactly the existing request, eight busy clocks, done/consume protocol and direct divide retirement. Preserve the four narrow restoring prefix steps on busy iteration zero. During that same prefix edge prepare and register 36-bit multiples k*D for k=1..15 from the already registered unsigned divisor. The seven remaining clocks each consume one four-bit digit; four prefix bits plus seven nibbles still cover all 32 dividend bits.

Use full 36-bit unsigned multiples so 15*0xffffffff is represented without overflow. Shifts supply power-of-two multiples. Generate other multiples from constant shifts with one carry-propagate add/subtract where possible: 3D=2D+D, 5D=4D+D, 7D=8D-D, 9D=8D+D, 15D=16D-D, and even multiples can share shifted odd results or equivalent constant expressions. For 11D=8D+2D+D and 13D=8D+4D+D, explicitly compress the three terms into sum=X XOR Y XOR Z and carry=((X AND Y) OR (X AND Z) OR (Y AND Z))<<1, followed by one 36-bit sum+carry. This avoids creating a new two-adder preparation bottleneck. No multiply operator, table ROM or variable-index RAM belongs in divisor preparation. Let synthesis merge identical shifted register bits where possible.

On each later busy cycle form the 36-bit trial T={remainder_q,quotient_q[31:28]}. In parallel compute fifteen 37-bit differences diff[k]={0,T}-{0,multiple_q[k]}. Define ge[0]=1 and ge[k]=NOT diff[k][36]. For k=0..14, select[k]=ge[k] AND NOT ge[k+1]; select[15]=ge[15]. Select the low 32-bit remainder using masked terms and an OR reduction: T for digit zero, otherwise diff[k]. Form the four quotient bits as OR reductions over the constant digit encodings masked by select[k], then append that nibble to quotient_q[27:0]. Express balanced reductions or synthesis-friendly bitwise ORs, not a priority chain, dynamic indexed result mux, second subtraction or serial comparison of fifteen candidates. For a nonzero divisor the selected remainder is less than D and fits 32 bits. Zero divisors retain the existing explicit architectural result override.

Complete the same resource restructuring at its retirement interface. In ex_stage.sv drive div_consume = div_done AND NOT normal_wb_valid AND NOT stall AND NOT reset, and continue driving div_completion.valid from div_consume. Remove the redundant live EX is_divide/advance qualification from this grant. Keep execute_wait and advance otherwise unchanged. The divider's registered done bit already proves ownership: requests require a valid decoded divide; ID/EX is held until completion; older branches have resolved before launch; and no younger instruction can replace this owner before consumption. Thus done implies the matching valid divide still owns ID/EX. Preserve the existing older-WB arbitration, dmem backpressure, reset cancellation and retained-completion tests. Do not remove these protections or change the externally observable request/consume protocol. This avoids letting live EX opcode decode feed the direct-retirement selection and register-file write path after the recurrence is shortened.

Retain the launch-time unsigned magnitude conversion, captured dividend and signs, quotient/remainder choice, final sign correction, divide-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1 semantics exactly. Do not change multiplication, the ordinary ALU result mux, forwarding, fetch/decode topology, branch prediction, in-order architectural retirement ownership, memory interfaces or nret=1. Preserve the existing ALTOPS equations and identical eight-cycle handshake; only the real-arithmetic branch changes. Both arithmetic and control paths must retain reset, completion retention and exactly-once consumption behavior.

The intended benefit is one wide subtract-and-select depth per four dividend bits instead of two. The cost is fifteen trial subtractors instead of six, additional constant-multiple storage, and a wider one-hot selection tree. Expect a moderate area increase within the 10,000 LUT4 target. Divisor-preparation timing, selection fanout, routing congestion, and the unchanged IF-to-ID recovery-token path can limit the benefit. The single architectural angle is the shared divider resource: shorten its feedback and drive its completion interface from its own registered token. Fetch-buffer changes and the more aggressive experiment that removed completion backpressure are excluded. The radix-16 recurrence alone measured only 73.094 MHz median because timing moved to EX opcode qualification of direct writeback; the simpler completion-only experiment was also insufficient. The proposed paired structure targets these complementary paths, and its final fitness must be measured rather than inferred by adding their separate effects.

Validate every real M-extension operation with the unchanged exact arithmetic tests and additional independent randomized quotient/remainder checks, particularly large unsigned divisors, signed extremes and trial values around each digit boundary k*D. Exercise divisor values whose multiples need all 36 bits. Check the recurrence invariant and one-hot digit selection for nonzero divisors against an independent arithmetic reference. Preserve ALTOPS testing, all standard formal checks including the ten-cycle retirement liveness bound, and full-RVFI ready/stalled cosimulation. Keep canonical CoreMark CRCs, UART validation, address bounds and marker-bracketed timing unchanged. Real arithmetic must be checked independently because standard formal uses ALTOPS; do not claim that gate proves the new recurrence.

Measure all three vendor placement options and actual marked CoreMark cycles. Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 204.5453 iterations/s, more than 4.6 percent above 195.55. If the expected 4,238,604-cycle interval is retained, median Fmax must exceed 86.698653 MHz. The expected gain below remains a hypothesis until the complete structure is measured; final implementation must satisfy the unchanged gates. The recurrence prototype passed ready/stalled full-RVFI cosimulation and canonical CoreMark with exactly 4,238,604 marked cycles. These checks are evidence for feasibility, not approval of the final combined structure.

title: Split direct-prediction target arithmetic from its fast range certificate
motivation:
The champion reaches 195.55 iterations/second at 82.887 MHz with
4,238,604 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its latest reported worst
path starts at the instruction source and passes through IF into
ID/EX recovery_static_miss. The predictor currently forms a full
32-bit PC-plus-sign-extended-immediate sum before reducing its upper
twelve bits to decide whether a taken prediction is safe. That late
decision feeds both fetch selection and the newly registered recovery
tokens. Prior branch replay found only about 54,467 conditional misses
and 13,735 JALRs; accuracy alone offers insufficient headroom. Fetch
queues repeatedly lost their saved cycles to timing, and pipelining
BHT training regressed. Shorten prediction eligibility itself while
retaining the champion's successful recovery and prediction policy.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement a split direct-target generator in IF: calculate the low
twenty target bits in parallel with a fast carry-out certificate, and
derive the in-range predicate from that carry, immediate sign and
comparisons of the registered PC's high twelve bits. A predicted
target is always in the first 1 MiB, so its high bits can be zero
without waiting for a sign-extension carry chain. This is one
predictor timing change; retain the 128-entry bimodal table, exact
training, direct JAL policy, sequential JALR policy and pipeline depth.

Let P=PC[19:0], I=direct_imm[19:0], H=PC[31:20], S=direct_imm[31],
and C be the unsigned carry-out of P+I. B and J immediates both have
direct_imm[31:20] equal to twelve copies of S. The exact modulo-32-bit
target is inside the first 1 MiB iff
((H==0) AND (C==S)) OR
((H==0xfff) AND !S AND C) OR
((H==1) AND S AND !C).
Preserve all three terms, including wraparound from high addresses;
do not assume architectural PCs are already in the low memory region.
Use two-bit modulo addition for alignment. When instruction kind,
existing BHT direction, alignment and this range certificate permit
prediction, select {12'b0, low_target[19:0]}; otherwise select full
32-bit PC+4. This must be bit-for-bit equivalent to the current IF
predicted_direct and predicted_next_pc for every PC and instruction.

Produce C without consuming the twenty-bit sum or a synthesized
thirty-two-bit adder. Partition P and I into five four-bit blocks.
Form each block's generate from its five-bit zero-carry sum and its
propagate as the reduction-AND of bitwise P XOR I. Express carry-out
as a balanced prefix or parallel group generate/propagate reduction.
Keep the low-target data addition independent from this fast control
cone. PC upper-region equality terms can evaluate in parallel with
immediate decode. Do not put the general EX target adder, forwarded
operands or the actual-next-PC mux back into prediction eligibility.

Capture exactly the same prediction in ID/EX that advances the fetch
PC. Preserve reset, squash, all bus and execution holds, redirect
priority, legal-encoding qualification, out-of-range refusal and
misalignment traps. Keep architectural target arithmetic full-width
in EX, including JALR bit-zero clearing, link-write suppression and
RVFI actual pc_wdata. No top-level IO, nret or evaluation changes.

Expect roughly seven percent higher median Fmax with identical
bracketed cycles, rather than an accuracy gain. This estimate is
unmeasured: FPGA mapping of the prefix logic and other near-critical
paths can limit improvement. Validate exact IF equivalence against
the old full-width expression, existing pipeline/formal/cosim gates,
canonical stalled CoreMark and all three Gowin placement options.
Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 204.5453 iterations/second
(195.55 times 1.046); recompute the frequency requirement from the
final measured cycle count.

title: Absorb register-file write-first bypass into masked read trees
motivation:
The champion reaches 195.55 iter/s at 82.887 MHz with 4,238,604 marked
cycles. Earlier micro_opt r7s0 established that scalar fabric words and
balanced OR-tree reads can remove a register-file timing bottleneck.
Recent experiments expose writeback-to-ID operand capture among the
competing critical paths. The current read tree still ends in a
priority mux for write-first bypass and x0. Move bypass exclusion into
the leaf selects so the late write data enters through one masked OR.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Optimize only the two combinational read networks in rtl/reg_file.sv.
Keep the 31 independent synchronously reset fabric words, their exact
write enables, both read ports, all pipeline registers and all forwarding
controls. Preserve the original write-first behavior for every input
combination, including reset cycles and writes to x0.

For each physical word i=1..31 define write_i = w_en && w_addr==i.
Retain the original synchronous storage update. For read port p, change
its constant-index leaf mask to read_i_p=(rs_p_addr==i) && !write_i.
Thus a word being written is excluded from both stored-data read trees;
other words retain their ordinary selects. Keep the x0 leaf permanently
zero and retain explicit balanced OR trees over these masked leaves.

In parallel define bypass_p=w_en && (w_addr!=0) && (w_addr==rs_p_addr).
Drive rs_p_data = stored_tree_p | (w_data & {32{bypass_p}}).
The two terms are exclusive. On a bypass match the selected stored word
is suppressed; without a match exactly the addressed nonzero word is
selected; x0 has neither a stored leaf nor an eligible bypass. Do not
OR unmasked old data with new data and do not drop the nonzero guard.

Use scalar, constant-index word enables that can share the existing
write-address decode. Keep w_data out of every individual word's read
leaf: replicating a 32-bit bypass mux at all 31 words would increase
routing and defeats this proposal. There is one masked write-data term
per read port, at the root. Keep all 32 data bits and both ports.

Preserve synchronous reset priority for storage. The combinational
bypass must still follow the existing w_en/w_addr/w_data inputs even

title: Isolate JALR recovery behind dedicated target and event registers
motivation:
The champion scores 195.55 iterations/s at 82.887 MHz. Its r10s2 recovery
tokens removed forwarded JALR arithmetic from recovery enable, but the
forwarded base-plus-immediate and target-alignment mux still drive the
fetch-PC data input. Recent timing paths run from forwarding selectors
through EX to the fetch PC. Structural r10s1 established that registered
recovery is feasible and costs about 1.6 percent more CoreMark cycles
when applied to all transfers. The proposed narrower boundary targets
indirect jumps while preserving the champion's direct-branch recovery.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one structural change: complete JALR recovery through dedicated
registered target and pending-event state. Keep conditional branches and
direct JAL recovery in their existing EX cycle. Partition the fetch-PC
recovery data path so live forwarded JALR arithmetic cannot remain in
the fast direct-transfer target cone. This is selective control-transfer
retiming, with one additional recovery cycle only for legal JALRs.

In ex_stage.sv add indirect_pending_q and indirect_target_q. When a
valid legal JALR advances without older dmem backpressure or an older
pending indirect recovery, capture its actual architectural target:
sum = forwarded_rs1 + immediate; aligned target = {sum[31:1],1'b0};
if sum[1] is one, capture PC+4 instead and preserve the existing trap
and suppressed link write. Capture directly from these JALR expressions,
not from a shared branch/JAL/JALR actual_next_pc mux. Use separate scalar
state outside the packed EX/MEM register. The pending bit itself proves
valid ownership; it must only be set by that accepted legal JALR.

Define late_redirect = indirect_pending_q AND NOT reset AND NOT stall.
Reset clears pending and target. While stall is asserted retain both.
On an unstalled edge pending becomes the new accepted-JALR event, or
zero if there is none; target updates only for a new accepted JALR.
Every late_redirect edge consumes the old event exactly once. Keep the
original JALR instruction's architectural EX/MEM and MEM/WB progress,
RVFI operands, link value, trap and actual pc_next intact.

Gate advance and divider launch with NOT late_redirect. Define divider
execute_wait with NOT late_redirect too, so a wrong-path younger divide
cannot block the older recovery. When EX/MEM is not stalled, insert a
fully inert EX/MEM bubble on late_redirect, clearing controls as well
as validity. The older recovering JALR still transfers normally to WB.
Hazard control sees the recovery and clears the younger ID/EX bundle
and both forwarding selectors. Suppress younger branch training, memory
requests and direct divide consumption through the same advance gating.
Preserve older memory holds, retained WB forwarding and imem-independent
recovery priority. No wrong-path instruction may retire or start divide.

Drive redirect = late_redirect OR (advance AND direct_miss), where
direct_miss is the unchanged predecoded-token predicate. Give the older
late event priority. Its redirect target is indirect_target_q. For a
direct recovery use only PC+immediate, PC+4, direct-target alignment and
the resolved direct condition: choose PC+immediate iff that target is
aligned AND (direct JAL OR branch_taken), otherwise PC+4. This direct
target expression must exclude jalr_sum, shared misalign_fault and the
general actual_next_pc mux. Keep actual_next_pc unchanged for RVFI and
architectural EX/MEM state. Remove current-cycle indirect_miss from the
fetch recovery event, rather than issuing both immediate and late events.

Preserve the current speculative next-EX/MEM writer hint, including its
direct-JAL alignment qualification. A JALR may now let a younger operand
owner be captured, but late_redirect must squash that entire younger EX
instruction before any side effect. Keep the existing registered
forwarding selectors, load/multiply hazards, ordinary branch training,
bimodal predictor and direct offset-four exception. Preserve arithmetic,
decoder legality, all pipeline boundaries other than JALR recovery,
the direct divide retirement schedule, nret=1 and all external ports.

The intended gain is splitting the forwarded JALR sum/alignment/recovery
path at a real register boundary while avoiding extra cycles and later
BHT updates for conditional branches. Dedicated target/event flops avoid
making the shared EX/MEM next-PC mux or a live opcode qualification the
new recovery source. Costs are target storage, one extra cycle per JALR
and recovery control. Divider recurrence or direct-branch paths may cap
Fmax; confidence is low until final vendor timing establishes a gain.

Check aligned, PC+4 and misaligned JALRs, x0/link destinations, back-to-
back indirect jumps, both operand forwarding sources, and older dmem
holds. Put a store, branch, multiply and DIV/REM immediately after JALR
on the wrong path and verify no side effects or predictor training.
Exercise JALR targets beginning with DIV/REM and load-to-divide chains
against the unchanged ten-cycle retirement-liveness bound. Check reset,
imem stalls, exact RVFI PC/operand/result/trap/order and exactly-once
recovery. Adapt stage-specific timing tests while retaining every
architectural assertion. Run real/ALTOPS pipeline tests, unchanged formal,
full-RVFI ready/stalled cosim and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker
validation. Measure actual marked cycles and all three Gowin options.
Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 204.5453 iterations/s.

Prior and exploratory evidence does not establish a measured win for
this final structure. In this slot, a registered fetch buffer reduced
cycles but reached only 73.276 MHz median; a parallel-prefix radix-16
divider reached 76.8 MHz; replicated pre-forwarding branch comparisons
reached 68.316 MHz. Retiming every recovery on the current champion
passed all 53 formal checks but reached 75.086 MHz and 4,306,908 cycles.
Those changes are excluded. The final hypothesis narrows retiming to
JALR, retains immediate direct recovery/training, and gives indirect
targets dedicated storage rather than reusing shared EX/MEM pc_next.

title: Register the predicted instruction stream before decode
motivation:
The champion reaches 195.55 iterations/second at 82.887 MHz with 4,238,604 marker-bracketed cycles. Earlier branch replay found only about 54,467 conditional misses and 13,735 JALRs, so more accurate direction or return prediction has insufficient headroom. Earlier predicted-stream queues hid roughly five percent of stalled CoreMark cycles, but retained an empty-queue combinational bypass from instruction memory to decode. Their timing cost prevented adoption on later champions. The current core still combines instruction predecode, prediction, instruction masking, decoder and register-file access before ID/EX. A genuine register boundary for the predicted stream can remove that bypass path while allowing useful fetches during execution backpressure.

Fresh isolated exploration rejected conservative target-range certificates, separate B/J target arithmetic, smaller bimodal tables and an instruction-validated direct-target cache. Their best tested median was 80.968 MHz, below 82.887 MHz; none established an improvement. These circuits are not included. The final hypothesis instead changes the predictor delivery boundary, a distinction from all prior fall-through queues in the recorded history.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Introduce one two-entry, fixed-head, fully registered buffer between the existing predicted fetch stream and decode. Every instruction accepted from imem must cross this boundary before reaching the decoder; there is no empty-queue combinational instruction bypass. This is one predictor-delivery change: retain the existing 128-entry bimodal table, immediate-based direct JAL prediction, aligned low-1-MiB target guard, sequential JALR policy, EX recovery tokens and single retirement channel. Preserve arithmetic, register-file implementation, forwarding algorithm and memory completion.

Each entry holds full PC[31:0], instruction[31:0] and the predicted_direct bit that actually selected its next fetch address. Retain predicted_next_pc as saved verification metadata, or reconstruct it exclusively from the saved instruction, PC and direction for that purpose. Never consult the current BHT for a buffered entry. Entry zero is always the oldest instruction; entry one is the tail. Decode's instruction/source-address inputs come only from the registered head or a constant NOP when empty. Do not add any raw-imem bypass even on a simultaneous empty push/pop. Both an empty first fetch and a fetch after recovery become visible to decode on the following cycle.

Separate raw io_imemReady from decode availability. Expose available=(count!=0), independent of redirect and decode hold. Feed available to hazard_unit's existing instruction-availability input, while preserving load/multiply-use, dmem and divide hold priority. Supply IF with the raw bus-ready signal and decode_hold=stall_id. Normal consume is available AND NOT decode_hold. The current head and its raw source addresses must remain independent of consume to avoid a hazard combinational loop. When empty, decode captures an inert bubble using the existing unavailable-instruction behavior; when held, the head remains stable.

Normal acceptance is raw_ready AND (count<2 OR consume), subject to the exceptional-address serialization below. On consume, shift a retained tail into the fixed head. Append an accepted fetch at old count minus consume, with append winning over a shift to the same slot. A simultaneous full pop/push preserves count two. A push to an empty buffer cannot be consumed on the same edge. Advance the full-width fetch PC using the raw response's pre-edge prediction whenever that response is accepted, even during load-use, dmem or divide holds. Correctly predicted branches and JALs preserve the buffered stream; only misses cause recovery. Do not gate ordinary fetch acceptance with global stall_if, which now includes buffer emptiness.

Reset and EX redirect take priority over queue occupancy, pending boundary state and fetch-PC updates. Redirect atomically empties both slots, installs the full architectural recovery address, and retains the existing synchronous ID/EX control and forwarding-selector squash. Payload bits may be written on a redirect edge if occupancy makes them unreachable, allowing redirect to clear validity rather than reset every payload flop. Empty-buffer output must nevertheless mask stale instruction controls with a constant NOP. Preserve EX's existing advancement gate: older dmem backpressure defers redirect and training, and a recovery that can advance overrides raw imem unavailability. Retain exactly-once branch training, retirement, accepted stores and divide launch/consume semantics.

Use full-width saved PCs to avoid architectural-address truncation. Ordinary speculative run-ahead is allowed only for aligned fetch PCs below 0x000ffffc. At the last in-range word, an unaligned PC or an out-of-range PC, serialize delivery: accept a response only into an empty buffer, save its prediction, and hold the live fetch PC with a pending-advance flag until that saved instruction is consumed by decode. While pending, forbid another raw acceptance. Consumption then advances to the saved predicted_next_pc, unless recovery overrides it. This is the ordinary demand advance delayed to decode consumption, not autonomous look-ahead across a boundary. The next fetch still crosses the register boundary. Never clamp, wrap into a smaller address space or replace architectural trap/target behavior. Recovery must clear the pending flag and always remain able to make progress.

The expected benefit combines hiding ready imem opportunities during execution stalls with removing raw fetch/prediction paths from decode and register-file capture. Costs are one extra initial delivery cycle and one extra lost issue opportunity per misprediction/JALR recovery. The prior branch counts suggest roughly 1.6 percent extra recovery cycles against about five percent potential stall savings, but those are estimates from earlier designs, not a measured cycle count for this registered buffer. Whether the new boundary improves Gowin placement enough is uncertain. Expected fitness gain is seven percent with low confidence. No prototype of this final registered-buffer design has been simulated or timed; the earlier local predictor experiments are negative evidence, not validation of this proposal.

Validate an independent cycle-level FIFO/PC/prediction model, then real and ALTOPS pipeline suites, unchanged single-channel formal including the ten-cycle liveness property, full-RVFI ready/stalled cosim, and canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/marker/bounds checks. Specifically verify divider retirement spacing with the added delivery boundary; do not change any formal bound. Measure the actual bracketed cycles and all three Gowin placement options. Require median Fmax_Hz times 10/cycles strictly above 204.5453 iterations/second, more than 4.6 percent over 195.55. Keep only the registered two-entry design in this hypothesis; do not combine it with target arithmetic, BHT sizing, arithmetic-unit or retirement changes.

title: Shared radix-4 barrel shifter with predecoded shift-distance groups
motivation:
The champion reaches 195.55 iter/s at 82.887 MHz. Prior micro_opt
register-file bypass and branch-comparator rewrites regressed, and
recent divider changes expose competing branch and operand-control
paths. The ALU still describes separate left, logical-right and
arithmetic-right shifts. A shared, explicitly grouped shifter offers
an unexplored way to reduce EX selection depth and routing demand
without altering instruction latency, prediction or bus-stall behavior.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion reaches 195.55 iter/s at 82.887 MHz. Prior micro_opt
register-file bypass and branch-comparator rewrites regressed, and
recent divider changes expose competing branch and operand-control

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the combinational SLL/SRL/SRA datapath in alu.sv with a
single right-shift network using two four-way stages and one two-way
stage. Share it between left and right shifts through bit reversal.
This is one local arithmetic-mapping optimization, with no pipeline
register, new instruction, forwarding change or divider modification.

Let left=(op==ALU_SLL), fill=(op==ALU_SRA && a[31]), and
X=left ? reverse_bits(a) : a. Reverse by constant wire permutation,
not a dynamic index or shift. Decode b[1:0] into four exclusive
enables for shifts of 0,1,2,3 bits, and b[3:2] into four exclusive
enables for shifts of 0,4,8,12 bits. These small decodes evaluate in
parallel with the operand-source selection.

Stage one selects X, {fill,X[31:1]}, {{2{fill}},X[31:2]}, or
{{3{fill}},X[31:3]}. Stage two selects its input unchanged or shifted
right by 4,8,12 bits with the corresponding replicated fill bits.
Stage three uses b[4] to select unchanged data or a right shift by
sixteen bits with sixteen fill bits. All stage vectors remain 32 bits.
Use exclusive masks and balanced ORs for the four-way stages, exposing
parallel constant-wired candidates to Gowin instead of a priority
if/else chain. Do not infer a ROM or use variable shift operators
inside the grouped network. Select the final result directly for
SRL/SRA, and reverse its bits for SLL. All three ALU case arms return
this one result; preserve every other operation and default arm.

Repeated fill insertion implements arithmetic right shift exactly;
logical-right and left shifts use zero fill. Only b[4:0] controls the
distance, including register shifts whose upper b bits are nonzero.
Distance zero must return a for every shift operation, including
negative SRA inputs. The construction covers all distances 0..31,
and reversing both sides of a logical right shift implements SLL
modulo 32 bits. Preserve the existing standalone ALU interface and
both real and RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS configurations.

The intended benefit comes from sharing the directional shift hardware
and expressing the five shift-amount decisions as three grouped data
stages. Constant wiring and small parallel distance decodes may map
more efficiently to Gowin LUT/mux resources. This is an implementation
hypothesis: four-way selection is not necessarily one physical LUT
level. Extra reversal-selection muxes and control fanout can erase the
gain, and existing branch/divider paths can still set Fmax. Confirm the
actual mapped depth and resource use rather than assuming fewer RTL
stages imply faster hardware. The expected gain is low confidence.

Keep the existing ALU operand forwarding, EX/MEM and MEM/WB boundaries,
multiply and divide implementations and protocols, branch predictor,
register-file storage, memory interfaces and nret=1 unchanged. Preserve
all decoder legality, trap, RVFI ordering and liveness checks. Identical
instruction results and latencies should preserve exactly 4,238,604
marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles under the standard stall sequence.

Prove combinational equivalence of all three shift results against the
original native expressions for arbitrary a and b. Test all 32 shift
distances with zero, all ones, signed extrema, alternating bit patterns,
walking ones/zeros and deterministic random operands. Vary b[31:5] to
verify masking, and compare SRA with an independent signed-integer
reference. Retain all existing arithmetic, real M-extension and ALTOPS
checks. Run unchanged pipeline tests, formal, ready/stalled full-RVFI
cosimulation and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/address/marker checks.

A combinational Yosys SAT miter of the specified grouped network passed
equivalence against native SLL, SRL and signed SRA for arbitrary 32-bit
a and b. This establishes the equations, not final RTL integration or
vendor timing; rerun the checks on the implemented circuit.

Measure all three vendor placement options and actual CoreMark cycles.
Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 204.5453 iter/s, more than
4.6 percent above 195.55; at unchanged cycles median Fmax must exceed
approximately 86.699 MHz. No measured improvement is claimed for this
grouped shifter proposal. Earlier local branch, divider and control
prototypes explored in this session remained below the champion and
are excluded from the final change. A simpler shared shifter expressed
as one native 33-bit variable shift also regressed: option 1 measured
75.958 MHz and 4,975 logic cells versus 82.887 MHz and 5,048 for the
champion. That is negative evidence about sharing alone. The proposed
explicit four-way stages remain unmeasured; do not claim that resource
reduction or the simpler prototype establishes a fitness improvement.
