title: Eight-cycle divider with width-specialized radix scheduling
motivation:
The champion scores 195.55 iterations/s at 82.887 MHz. Its divider
processes four bits per clock through two dependent full-width radix-4
stages. CoreMark's measured interval contains no divides, so shortening
this physical feedback can improve fitness without additional benchmark
cycles. Structural r11s1's fifteen-wide-trial radix-16 design reached
only 80.433 MHz and exposed its serial first-nibble prefix. The proposed
operand-width partition avoids both fifteen wide trials and that prefix
chain while preserving the existing eight iteration clocks and direct
retirement schedule. This is one restructuring of the shared divider.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 195.55 iterations/s at 82.887 MHz. Its divider
processes four bits per clock through two dependent full-width radix-4
stages. CoreMark's measured interval contains no divides, so shortening
this physical feedback can improve fitness without additional benchmark
cycles. Structural r11s1's fifteen-wide-trial radix-16 design reached
only 80.433 MHz and exposed its serial first-nibble prefix. The proposed
operand-width partition avoids both fifteen wide trials and that prefix
chain while preserving the existing eight iteration clocks and direct
retirement schedule. This is one restructuring of the shared divider.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Partition the divider by the captured unsigned divisor magnitude, using
a registered large_divisor flag for D >= 256. Keep shared 32-bit quotient
and remainder state and the existing launch, eight busy edges, retained
done and direct-consumption interface. Every RV32M operand is handled;
this classification is independent of the benchmark and instruction PC.

For D >= 256, the top eight quotient bits are provably zero: the top
eight dividend bits are at most 255 and therefore less than D. At launch
initialize remainder_q to zero-extended dividend_magnitude[31:24] and
quotient_q to {dividend_magnitude[23:0], 8'b0}. Process the remaining
twenty-four dividend bits with exactly eight radix-8 digit steps, three
bits per busy edge. Each ordinary step forms the full 35-bit trial
{remainder_q, quotient_q[31:29]}, compares it against D through 7D using
seven parallel 36-bit extended subtractions, and uses their borrow bits
to select one digit and remainder. Define ge[k] = trial >= kD, w[0] =
!ge[1], w[k] = ge[k] && !ge[k+1] for k=1..6, and w[7] = ge[7]. Use masked
OR reductions for remainder and digit encoding, with no serial priority
selection or second subtraction. Shift quotient by three and append the
selected digit. Keep full trial/difference widths through selection;
only the selected remainder may narrow to 32 bits because it is below D.

Prepare wide multiples during the first busy edge, overlapping the first
radix-8 digit instead of lengthening launch or adding a setup cycle.
The first trial is only dividend_magnitude[31:21], at most 2047. If
registered D >= 2048, its first digit is zero and the remainder is that
eleven-bit prefix. Otherwise D is 256..2047: compute its first digit
with seven parallel narrow trials against k*D[10:0], using 14-bit
multiples/trials and 15-bit extended differences. Apply the high-divisor
zero-digit choice once after this narrow network, not inside a serial
restoring chain. Implement arithmetic and one-hot selection in fabric,
not an indexed quotient ROM. On the same edge register full-width 3D,
5D and 7D from the registered divisor, using D+2D, D+4D and 8D-D in
parallel. Use 35-bit zero extensions before shifts/additions. D, 2D,
4D and 6D then come from the divisor and registered 3D by wiring/shifts.
The remaining seven busy edges use the single wide radix-8 stage.

For D < 256, keep all thirty-two dividend bits but exploit remainder
width: for every nonzero D, remainder < D <= 255. Initialize quotient_q
to the full magnitude and remainder_q to zero. On each of the same eight
busy edges consume four dividend bits with two dependent NARROW radix-4
steps. Each trial is {remainder[7:0], next_two_dividend_bits}, ten bits;
D, 2D and 3D also fit ten bits. Use eleven-bit extended differences and
borrow-derived one-hot selection. Capture ten-bit 3D at launch, using
explicit zero extension of the low eight magnitude bits. This is a small
launch operation; do not create a wide launch-time multiples chain.
Keep each selected remainder's low eight bits and zero-extend it into
shared remainder state. This path needs no serial four-step prefix and
never places two 32-bit trial chains on one clock. D=0 uses the same
bounded schedule with the existing architectural result override.

Capture signedness, original dividend, quotient/remainder sign and
exceptional cases exactly as today. Preserve signed truncation toward
zero, dividend-signed remainder, divide-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1 results.
Iteration seven still sets done; result selection and sign correction
use stable registered state. Preserve all non-divide ALU/multiply logic.
Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS retain the exact current formulas and the same
eight-iteration handshake; real arithmetic must be tested independently.

Complete this divider-resource restructuring with a completion grant
owned by its registered done token: div_consume = div_done &&
!normal_wb_valid && !stall && !reset. Keep div_completion.valid driven
by this grant. Preserve execute_wait, advance, launch eligibility, older
WB priority, dmem holds and all metadata retention. Done already implies
that the valid matching divide owns held ID/EX; assert this property.
Remove only redundant live is_divide/advance qualification from the
consume grant, avoiding an EX opcode-to-retirement-mux path after the
arithmetic feedback is shortened. This grant has prior r11s1 precedent;
it is not evidence of a standalone performance win. Do not change the
direct retirement boundary, add a state, or increase the liveness bound.

The intended structural gain is one full-width subtract/select depth
per large-divisor iteration and two short ten-bit steps for small
divisors. Seven wide trials replace the current six, rather than the
fifteen in r11s1. Costs are a registered mode, narrow arithmetic,
divisor-multiple storage and mode selection into shared state. Signed
launch, wide multiple preparation, first-prefix selection, final mode
muxing, routing or non-divider paths can still limit Fmax. Keep the
width partition and fixed schedule explicit; do not silently fall back
to a full-width four-bit chain for any nonzero operand class.

An independent integer model checked 75,874 unsigned dividend/divisor
pairs and 20,000 signed pairs, including dense divisor coverage around
255/256 and 2047/2048, against exact quotient and remainder. It checked
the eight-iteration schedule, one-hot digit selection, prefix bounds and
remainder invariants. This validates the arithmetic construction only;
no RTL prototype, formal proof or Gowin measurement of this final
divider exists yet. Earlier recovery-address retiming probes in this
slot passed correctness checks but measured only 73.573..78.012 MHz;
those fetch/branch modifications are excluded from the final hypothesis.

Retain and extend real arithmetic tests for all four DIV/REM operations,
D=0, D=1, signed extrema, powers of two and neighboring values, D=255,
256, 257, 2047 and 2048, maximum unsigned operands, q*D plus/minus one,
and every radix-8 digit boundary. Exercise maximum-width 7D and changing
live inputs after launch. Check reset, held completion, back-to-back
operations, both mode transitions and unchanged eight-clock completion.
Pipeline tests must cover forwarded operands, load-to-divide, consecutive
divides, wrong-path cancellation, older stalled memory, result consumers,
exact RVFI operands/results/order and the unchanged ten-cycle liveness
limit. Run real/ALTOPS suites, unchanged formal, ready/stalled full-RVFI
cosim, and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/address/marker checks. Standard
ALTOPS formal does not prove the real recurrence; do not claim it does.

Preserve nret=1, every external port, decoder legality, fetch/prediction,
forwarding, memory semantics and all hard invariants. Measure actual
bracketed cycles and all three Gowin options. Expected CoreMark cycles
remain 4,238,604; at that count acceptance requires median Fmax above
86.698653 MHz and fitness strictly above 204.5453 iterations/s, more than
4.6 percent over 195.55. The expected gain is a hypothesis, not a measured
result, and must survive the unchanged evaluation gates.

changes.description:
Replace the real divider recurrence with the registered divisor-width
partition: eight three-bit radix-8 steps for D>=256, overlapping wide
multiple preparation with an eleven-bit first prefix, and eight pairs
of ten-bit radix-4 steps for D<256. Share architectural quotient and
remainder state; use explicit full widths and one-hot selection.
Preserve launch/consume, eight busy edges, signs, exceptions, reset,
retained completion, exact ALTOPS behavior and all other arithmetic.

Grant divide consumption from registered div_done, with unchanged
older-WB, dmem-stall and reset qualification. Keep execute_wait,
advancement, launch, held metadata, direct retirement and every other
EX function unchanged. Assert that done has a valid matching owner.

title: PC-only direct-target prediction with decode-time stale-entry recovery
motivation:
The champion scores 195.55 iterations/s at 82.887 MHz and 4,238,604 marker-bracketed cycles. Its recorded option-zero critical path starts at the instruction source and crosses IF into ID/EX recovery_static_miss. Current direct prediction decodes the live instruction, adds its immediate to the PC and checks the full target range before selecting the next fetch. Earlier branch replay found only about 54,467 conditional misses and 13,735 JALRs, so greater direction accuracy has little headroom. Queues, target-range rewrites and delayed BHT training have already regressed.

Local recovery experiments in this slot also lost timing: prediction-selected combinational correction reached 73.302 MHz median; registering its address reached 79.413 MHz; separate equality/ordered recovery enables reached 75.842 MHz; moving static recovery classification into IF reached 64.564 MHz. Those experiments are excluded. This hypothesis instead removes live instruction data from the ordinary prediction-address selection by using a PC-only target lookup. Unlike the instruction-validated target cache explored in r12s2, cache validation happens at ID/EX and never gates the fetch-address choice.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace immediate-based taken-target selection in IF with one 32-entry, direct-mapped branch target cache, indexed by PC[6:2]. Keep the existing 128-entry bimodal direction table and its existing exactly-once training policy. Each target entry contains a valid bit, full remaining source-PC tag PC[31:7], target word address [19:2], direct-kind bit (conditional branch or JAL), and the signed direct immediate signature imm[20:1]. All installed source PCs and targets must be word aligned. An entry is installed only for legal BRANCH or direct JAL with a non-+4 immediate and a full-width computed target in [0, 0x00100000). Consequently every installed target is nonsequential for its tagged PC, including full-width wraparound cases, and the compressed target reconstructs exactly as {12'b0, target_word, 2'b00}. Do not truncate the source tag or the architectural PC.

Lookup uses only the registered fetch PC and stored predictor state; require PC[1:0]=0 for a cache hit. On a tag hit, predict the cached target for cached JAL, or for cached BRANCH when the existing BHT counter MSB is taken. Otherwise predict PC+4. A miss has no live-immediate target fallback: the branch/JAL resolves through the existing EX recovery boundary and trains the cache. In particular, do not validate the live instruction, recompute its target, or test its target range in the fetch selection path. Cold and conflicting direct-JAL misses add a recovery bubble; this is an explicit performance cost. Keep IF/ID combinational and add no fetch queue or pipeline stage.

Use modest fabric storage with constant-index per-entry updates and a balanced read structure. A suitable implementation gates each entry's target, signature and kind by valid AND matching index AND matching full tag, then OR-reduces the leaves. Direct mapping guarantees at most one match. Reset valid bits; uninitialized payload must be masked so it cannot affect prediction or leak X into an accepted bundle. Keep the direction-table implementation unchanged. Cache training is one synchronous write/invalidation on an advancing EX instruction, independent of branch outcome for target allocation. Allocate a legal direct branch/JAL whenever its source/target alignment, target range and non-+4 checks pass, whether a branch is taken or not. Otherwise invalidate only a matching source-PC entry. Never update from bubbles, squashed instructions or held EX instructions. Never allocate a JALR target; an advancing legal JALR may invalidate an old matching direct entry. Read-before-write is acceptable because acceptance freezes the pre-edge lookup result.

Carry the exact predicted_next_pc, a used_nonsequential_cache_prediction bit, and the selected immediate signature with the accepted instruction. In decode, the authoritative decoder determines whether this actual instruction is a legal BRANCH/direct JAL. A cached prediction matches its actual direct target iff that legal-direct classification holds and the cached signature equals the decoded imm[20:1]. The source-PC tag was checked at fetch, so equal signed immediates guarantee equal full-width targets without a second target addition or a wide next-PC comparison. Branch/JAL kind need not match the cached kind: identical immediate and PC identify the same target. Branch funct3 legality must still be checked by the existing decoder.

Define stale_prediction = used_nonsequential_cache_prediction AND NOT target_signature_match. For a fresh matching cache prediction, feed predicted_direct=1 into the champion's existing recovery-token equations. For sequential prediction, feed predicted_direct=0. For a stale prediction, force recovery_static_miss=1 and disable recovery_branch_check; the instruction must recover unconditionally when it advances, regardless of its actual opcode or branch outcome. This also corrects stale predictions on ordinary arithmetic, loads, stores, illegal instructions, reserved branch encodings and changed direct immediates. Do not assume instruction memory is immutable. Always retain the architectural actual_next_pc computation as the correction address, including PC+4 for non-control instructions and misalignment traps. RVFI next PC and link values continue to use actual architectural behavior. Preserve unconditional recovery for every advancing legal JALR, including PC+4 JALRs, so its speculative forwarding-owner safety argument remains valid.

Prediction consumption must coincide with ID/EX acceptance. Preserve reset, load/multiply-use, divide and dmem hold priorities; held instructions retain the complete prediction certificate. Advancing recovery overrides imem unavailability and squashes all younger controls and forwarding selectors. Wrong-path instructions may read the predictor but cannot allocate/invalidate entries, launch a divider, issue a data transaction or retire. A stale prediction changes control flow speculatively only; the actual instruction itself still executes and retires exactly once, in order.

Guard speculative sequential advancement at the final in-range word. If an accepted fetch at 0x000ffffc has no nonsequential cache prediction, hold the fetch PC and set a boundary-wait flag instead of exposing speculative 0x00100000. Emit an inert younger bubble while waiting. Carry a force-recovery bit with that accepted instruction, and when it can advance in EX, recover to its unmodified full-width actual_next_pc even if the usual prediction comparison would report a match. Reset or recovery clears boundary-wait; an older recovery cancels this younger boundary instruction normally. A cache-predicted in-range transfer from the boundary can proceed normally. This only serializes the otherwise unsafe boundary case: it must not clamp, wrap or alter an architectural next PC, and recovery/ready handling must still guarantee progress. Test this case explicitly with cold JAL, taken conditional branch, stale entry and bus holds.

This is one predictor-architecture change: lookup before instruction inspection, followed by decode-time validation and the existing EX correction boundary. Preserve arithmetic units, register file, forwarding algorithm, memory completion, nret=1, decoder legality and external IO. The intended Fmax gain comes from replacing live-imem decode/add/range/select feedback with stored-tag/target selection. Costs are roughly 2,080 cache payload/valid bits before synthesis, additional lookup/validation logic and target-cache misses. Expected fitness gain is eight percent with low confidence; this final cache architecture has not been implemented, simulated or timed. The negative local experiments are not validation of it. An independent value-level model checked the proposed signature-match/stale/recovery equations against full predicted-versus-architectural PC comparison in 200,000 randomized cases, including alignment and wraparound. This checks the certificate algebra only, not RTL integration, the boundary state machine, cache timing or performance.

Verify an independent target-cache/prediction model including reset, tag aliases, row replacement, simultaneous lookup/training and held fetches. Exercise repeated calls and loops, direction changes, +4/zero/negative offsets, source addresses differing in upper tag bits and full-width target wrap. Change the instruction at a cached PC to a new immediate, opposite direct kind, ordinary ALU op, load/store, JALR, reserved branch and illegal opcode; verify unconditional stale recovery and exact architectural RVFI results. Cover correct and stale predictions during imem stalls, older dmem holds, load/multiply-use hazards and divide recovery. Check all architectural assertions, contiguous retirement order, exactly-once memory effects and training, and no wrong-path stores/divide starts. Retain unchanged formal including its ten-cycle liveness bound, real and ALTOPS pipeline/cosim gates, and canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/markers. Measure actual marked cycles and all three Gowin options; acceptance requires median Fmax_Hz times 10/cycles strictly above 204.5453 iterations/s. Inspect timing to establish that live imem target arithmetic is absent from ordinary next-fetch selection.

implementation_notes:
Implemented the PC-only direct-target cache hypothesis in cores/bench only.

- Added a 32-entry direct-mapped cache with PC[6:2] indexing, all 25 remaining source-PC tag bits, an 18-bit target word, a direct-kind bit, a 20-bit immediate signature, and a reset valid bit per entry (2,080 storage bits). Constant-index writes and masked leaves feed a balanced OR read tree. The existing 128-entry bimodal direction table and its training policy are unchanged.
- IF selects only a stored bounded target or the full architectural PC+4. Live instruction decode, immediate addition, target legality and target-range checks have been removed from ordinary prediction selection. Cold/conflicting JALs recover in EX.
- ID captures the exact prediction certificate and checks the signature against the authoritative decoder. Stale used predictions unconditionally recover through the original architectural actual_next_pc path, including ordinary/illegal instructions; matching predictions retain the original recovery-token equations. Every advancing legal JALR still recovers.
- EX trains or invalidates the target cache exactly once per advancing instruction. Allocation is independent of branch outcome and checks full-width target range, source/target alignment, legal direct kind and non-+4 immediate. Nonallocating instructions invalidate only a matching full source PC.
- Added boundary serialization at 0x000ffffc: a sequentially predicted accepted instruction holds fetch, emits inert younger bubbles and forces EX recovery to its unmodified architectural next PC. Reset and older recovery clear the wait state.
- Arithmetic, register file, forwarding, decoder, memory completion, retirement width and external interfaces were preserved. No architecture deviations from the proposed cache were needed. The update interface is a packed bundle instead of separate wires.

title: Prune the unused divide-to-EX/MEM ALU result route
motivation: The champion retires DIV/REM directly from the dedicated div_result output and inserts an EX/MEM bubble on every divide edge, including consumption. However, alu.sv also selects div_result onto its ordinary combinational out bus for all four divide opcodes. That bus feeds the normal EX/MEM result cone even though no dividing instruction can capture it there. Removing this redundant result route can reduce divider-result fanout and ordinary ALU output selection without modifying arithmetic, instruction latency or any valid retirement. Recent micro_opt branch-comparator, register-file and shifter rewrites regressed; this proposal instead specializes an already separate completion interface.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Introduce a default-enabled ALU parameter named ENABLE_DIVIDE_OUT. In the ALU output case, DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU return div_result when this parameter is true and 32'b0 when false. Instantiate the EX-stage ALU with ENABLE_DIVIDE_OUT=0 alongside its existing ENABLE_MULTIPLY=0. Preserve the dedicated div_result output, divider state machine, request/busy/done/consume handshake, magnitude and sign handling, special cases and exact eight busy clocks. The parameter affects only the ordinary combinational out bus, never the actual divide completion output.

The standalone ALU defaults to the original behavior, including divide values on out for existing arithmetic tests. Apply the same output-route specialization in real and RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS builds, without changing any ALTOPS formula, constant or handshake. All non-divide output case arms, including defaults and multiply configuration, remain identical.

The core-level correctness argument follows existing ownership. Whenever in.ctrl.alu_op denotes a divide and in.valid is true, ex_stage's is_divide branch clears EX/MEM instead of capturing alu_result on every non-stalled edge. On a stalled edge EX/MEM holds and does not consume alu_result. On the completion edge the same bubble rule applies, while the sole architectural result comes from div_completion.alu_result=div_result. With invalid ID/EX entries, no retirement can observe an ordinary divide result; retain and check the existing invariant that reset/flush clear side-effect controls as well as valid. Do not rely on invalid data to suppress a side effect.

Keep div_consume = is_divide && advance exactly as in the champion. Keep div_completion, retirement_w, wb_stage, normal_wb_data, register-file write-first behavior, registered binary forwarding and all pipeline control unchanged. Do not replace the dedicated div_result output with the specialized out bus. Normal-WB forwarding must still use the retained ordinary MEM/WB value; direct divide completion reaches only retirement/register-file/write-first ID as before.

This is one compile-time specialization that removes a functionally unused arithmetic-result route. It should let synthesis remove divider-result mux inputs and associated fanout from the ordinary EX result cone and avoid static paths that treat a divide as an ordinary ALU producer. It must not add result registers, alter the divider recurrence, retime completion or introduce operand masking. Preserve all branch prediction/recovery, address arithmetic, load/store handling, decoder legality, nret=1 ports and every hard invariant.

The benefit is uncertain: Gowin may already prove this route redundant through control factoring, and unchanged branch/fetch/divider paths may limit Fmax. Inspect the synthesized cone to confirm the direct divider result no longer feeds the normal EX/MEM ALU-result input, while its dedicated completion path remains. Do not count an RVFI-only pruning or circuit-neutral source change as a performance improvement. Confidence is low until all-placement vendor timing confirms a real gain.

Extend ALU tests to exercise both parameter settings. With ENABLE_DIVIDE_OUT=1, retain every original output/result assertion. With it disabled, require out==0 only for the four divide opcodes while dedicated div_result, busy/done timing, reset cancellation and held completion remain bit-exact against the independent RV32M reference. Check non-divide operations remain identical in both settings. Exercise real and ALTOPS configurations without weakening either reference.

In pipeline tests, assert that an active divide never captures an ordinary EX/MEM result: memory holds preserve the prior entry, every advancing divide edge produces the existing fully inert bubble, and only direct completion retires the correct result. Cover forwarded launch operands, load-to-divide, consecutive divides, result consumers, long older memory stalls, imem stalls, reset and wrong-path divides. Retain exact RVFI operands/results/order, register consistency, trap/side-effect suppression and the unchanged ten-cycle liveness limit.

Run strict lint, real/ALTOPS ALU and pipeline suites, unchanged formal and ready/stalled full-RVFI cosimulation, then canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/address/marker validation. No cycle-count change is intended: the standard stalled run should retain 4,238,604 bracketed cycles. Measure all three Gowin placement options. Acceptance requires fitness strictly above 204.5453 iterations/s, more than 4.6 percent above 195.55, or approximately 86.699 MHz median at unchanged cycles.

This final specialization has not been prototyped or timed. Earlier independent session probes were rejected: one-hot forwarding measured 63.286 MHz median; speculative address sums 72.138 MHz; div_done-only consumption 68.326 MHz; and byte carry-select address addition 72.739 MHz. All passed ten pipeline configurations, and the two address transformations also passed arithmetic SAT checks, but none established a fitness gain. Those RTL changes have been restored and none belongs to this proposal. Their results are not validation of the final specialization.

title: Autonomous divider completion with registered retirement ownership
motivation:
Direct divide retirement currently depends on the live held ID/EX
opcode through is_divide, execute_wait, advance and div_consume. This
completion event selects the register-file write data and write-first
decode path, so it can limit the clock even when CoreMark executes no
divides. Local structural probes repeatedly exposed paths from
ID/EX ctrl.alu_op through divide completion into RF words or operand
capture. Prior r11s1/r13s1 used a done-based grant but retained older-WB
and memory-stall arbitration and changed divider arithmetic as well.
A self-contained completion record can remove that arbitration using
the existing in-order drain guarantee, without changing arithmetic.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one structural change: treat an accepted divide as an autonomous
long-latency transaction whose registered context owns its eventual
single retirement. Move its completion metadata out of live ID/EX and
make the divider's retained done state the completion event. Keep the
existing eight busy iterations, signed arithmetic, launch timing,
result correction and direct retirement boundary. Add no cycle.

In ex_stage, allocate a divide context only on the existing accepted
div_request edge. Capture the original instruction, PC, destination,
source addresses and already-forwarded source values; compute/save
PC+4 for RVFI. Reuse div_rs1_q/div_rs2_q rather than duplicating them.
Set a context-valid owner bit on that edge, hold all context through
busy/completion, and clear ownership only on reset or consumption.
Arithmetic operands still enter the existing alu divider on launch.
No live decode field may select divide completion ownership, write
enable, destination or RVFI metadata after allocation.

Grant consumption as div_done && context_valid_q && !reset. Use this
same grant for div_consume and div_completion.valid. In particular,
remove live is_divide/advance, normal_wb_valid and stall from this
grant. This is justified by a specific existing pipeline invariant,
not by discarding an older instruction: launch requires !stall, the
launch edge moves the last older EX/MEM entry into ordinary MEM/WB
and replaces EX/MEM with a fully inert bubble, and the held divide
inserts inert EX/MEM bubbles on every subsequent busy edge. Ordinary
MEM/WB drains on the following edge, long before eight iterations
finish. No younger instruction advances while the divide waits.
Therefore done implies no older retirement and no active MEM request.
A low raw io_dmemReady during completion is immaterial because there
is no memory request; it must not delay or gate this retirement.

Establish that invariant with assertions and the unchanged formal
checks before removing arbitration. Whenever div_done is true outside
reset, assert context_valid_q, a matching held valid divide in ID/EX,
!normal_wb_valid, and an inert EX/MEM entry with no read/write request
and no effective memory hold. Assert the corresponding ownership
relationship throughout busy and that exactly one completion follows
each accepted launch unless reset cancels it. If these do not hold,
repair transaction ownership rather than deleting assertions, gating
an older retirement away, or weakening the liveness window.

Build div_completion from the saved context and the stable div_result.
Give it a constant legal register-writing control bundle: reg_write=1,
memory/jump/branch flags=0 and is_illegal=0. DIV/REM are accepted only
from the decoder's validated RV32M arms; they cannot acquire an address
alignment fault. Preserve the original instruction to distinguish the
operation in RVFI, and preserve x0 suppression at the existing RF/RVFI
boundary. All memory RVFI fields remain zero for a divide. Metadata
used only by RVFI will be pruned from the timed circuit; the intended
timing gain is the physical grant/write-owner path, not those fields.

it on the completion cycle. With the drain invariant established,
execute_wait can be is_divide && !div_done; older ordinary WB no longer
arbitrates a completed divide. Keep launch gated by validity, reset,
older memory acceptance and !busy/!done exactly as today. Keep inert

overlap younger execution or introduce a second retirement channel.

retirement mux and RF write boundary, without a path from live

cost is a small registered destination/ownership context; most saved

instruction/destination, strict order, exactly-once retirement and
memory effects, context lifetime, immediate result consumers and the

title: Banked write-behind BHT with coherent prediction forwarding
motivation: The champion scores 195.55 iterations/s at 82.887 MHz with 4,238,604 marked CoreMark cycles. Prior replay found too few direction misses for accuracy alone to clear the 4.6 percent acceptance margin. Several recent vendor paths run from forwarded EX branch operands into BHT counters. Direct EX training currently drives 128 address-qualified saturating state machines. Earlier delayed training regressed on the old multiplier topology; a fresh scalar-event probe on this champion also reached only 78.206 MHz. The proposed architectural change is a banked, predecoded write-behind direction predictor whose pending update is forwarded to prediction reads, preserving the champion's complete prediction sequence while isolating late branch resolution from counter-array update logic.

hypothesis.motivation: The champion scores 195.55 iterations/s at 82.887 MHz with 4,238,604 marked CoreMark cycles. Prior replay found too few direction misses for accuracy alone to clear the 4.6 percent acceptance margin. Several recent vendor paths run from forwarded EX branch operands into BHT counters. Direct EX training currently drives 128 address-qualified saturating state machines. Earlier delayed training regressed on the old multiplier topology; a fresh scalar-event probe on this champion also reached only 78.206 MHz. The proposed architectural change is a banked, predecoded write-behind direction predictor whose pending update is forwarded to prediction reads, preserving the champion's complete prediction sequence while isolating late branch resolution from counter-array update logic.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the physical organization and training interface inside the existing 128-entry, two-bit bimodal BHT with eight banks of sixteen counters and a one-entry registered training stage. This is one predictor architecture change. Retain the exact PC[8:2] index, four-state saturating policy, weakly-not-taken initialization, raw-instruction predecode, direct-target arithmetic and alignment/range guards. Do not add a target cache, history predictor, fetch queue, pipeline bubble, or architectural recovery stage.

Split the resolving index into bank = branch_pc[8:6] and row = branch_pc[5:2]. Register an eight-bit one-hot bank select and a sixteen-bit one-hot row select, along with valid and outcome: 26 event flops total. Capture both decodes and branch_taken unconditionally each clock, independently of branch_update, front-end acceptance and EX holds. Only valid is assigned branch_update and cleared on reset. The existing branch_update already qualifies exactly one advancing legal nontrapping conditional branch; preserve its exact qualification, including allowing an untaken branch whose hypothetical target is misaligned. Never add a combinational pending-event or EX-result bypass around this register boundary.

On every clock, each constant-index local counter consumes the PREVIOUS event iff pending_valid AND pending_bank[bank] AND pending_row[row]. Apply the same local two-bit saturating increment/decrement as the champion. Independently capture the next event on that edge. Thus one branch per cycle is supported without an event FIFO or backpressure. Drain a pending event even when instruction fetch or EX is held or a later instruction recovers: it belongs to an already advancing branch. Reset alone discards the pending event and initializes all counters to 01. Invalid event payload is irrelevant and must be masked before it can affect prediction or state. Do not hold or conditionally enable payload capture using the late branch-update signal; that signal should drive only the event-valid flop, not the counter array or event-address payload enables.

Organize fetch reads as a shallow, explicit two-level bank read. Decode fetch PC[5:2] once into sixteen row selects. Within each of eight banks, OR-reduce sixteen constant-index masked two-bit counter leaves using a balanced tree. Select the bank using PC[8:6], preferably a balanced masked-OR bank selection. Use fabric counters and local synchronous updates, not a RAM read-modify-write port. Keep row and bank address decoding separate rather than reconstructing a seven-bit dynamic array index or a flat 128-way tag comparison. The implementation should expose these groups structurally; ordinary synthesis remains authoritative, with no contract or timing constraints changed.

Make lookup coherent with immediate-resolution training using only registered pending state. Let C be the stored two-bit counter selected by the current fetch PC. A pending hit is pending_valid AND pending_bank[PC[8:6]] AND pending_row[PC[5:2]]. The direction after saturating one pending outcome differs from C[1] only when C is weak (01 or 10). Therefore effective_taken = pending_hit AND (C[1] XOR C[0]) ? pending_taken : C[1]. Use effective_taken exactly where the champion uses the BHT MSB. This forwarding adds no dependency on the currently resolving branch's combinational outcome. Preserve the complete two-bit counter in storage; forward only its prediction bit, without a second saturating-update datapath in fetch.

The state invariant is that applying the single valid pending event to the stored array yields the reference BHT trained at the champion's original resolution edge. Before each edge, both PC advancement and accepted ID/EX metadata use the same effective pre-edge prediction. At the edge, the old event updates storage while the next event replaces it. Consecutive branches to the same index, opposite outcomes, saturation and same-cycle lookup/update consequently reproduce the reference exactly; no training event is dropped or applied twice. This is stronger than accepting a one-event-stale table, and it requires the read forwarding even though the measured CoreMark trace happened to be insensitive to one clock of stale training in the simpler probe.

Leave IF prediction consumption, all reset/recovery/hold priorities, frozen prediction metadata, decode recovery tokens, direct offset-four handling, unconditional legal JALR recovery, forwarding ownership, divider, memory completion, nret=1 and external IO unchanged. No new controls need cross core.sv: use the existing branch-update inputs of if_stage. Architectural actual_next_pc and RVFI remain authoritative; speculative addresses retain the existing full-width guarded policy. No test or correctness gate may be weakened.

The intended timing gain comes from terminating late EX training at a small event register, moving bank/row decoding before that boundary, and localizing counter/read selection. The coherent read path preserves the original prediction sequence and should preserve all 4,238,604 measured cycles, so acceptance needs median Gowin Fmax above 86.698653 MHz, yielding fitness strictly above 204.5453 iterations/s. Expected gain is seven percent with low confidence: registered-update experiments have exposed other limiting paths, and the extra counter-bit read plus forwarding mux may offset the bank organization's benefit.

This exact banked, split-decoded design has not been implemented or timed. A 200,000-cycle independent software model verified coherent write-behind lookup against an immediate-training reference, including resets, pending-row hits, repeated same-row events and opposite outcomes. A second 200,000-cycle model checked the exact eight-bank/sixteen-row one-hot event representation and banked read forwarding. That is an algorithm check, not RTL or timing validation. Fresh alternatives excluded from this proposal passed selftest/CoreMark cosimulation but regressed in median Fmax: producer-generated recovery certificates 69.697 MHz, scalar delayed training without forwarding 78.206 MHz, registered opposite-path correction addresses 71.841 MHz, a one-bit last-outcome table 74.603 MHz, and scalar write-behind training with coherent forwarding and unconditional payload capture 79.839 MHz. The one-bit table also increased marked cycles to 4,267,125. Those results justify low confidence and must not be described as evidence of a measured improvement for this final architecture.

Validate an independent cycle-level reference BHT at every accepted fetch, rather than only comparing final CoreMark CRCs. Check all 128 entries, one-hot bank/row capture, reset with a pending event, back-to-back same and different rows/banks, aliasing PCs, saturation, simultaneous lookup/training, idle cycles and changing raw inputs during holds. Check stored-plus-pending equivalence to the original counter state and identical fetch PCs, predictions, recovery pulses and architectural retirements under deterministic ready patterns. Retain all existing pipeline assertions, especially exactly-once branch_update, stable held prediction tokens, reserved encodings, misaligned targets and no wrong-path memory or divide effects. Run unchanged single-channel formal including ten-cycle liveness, real/ALTOPS unit tests, full-RVFI ready/stalled cosim and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/markers. Measure all three Gowin placement options and actual marked cycles; no unmeasured fitness gain is claimed.

title: Align internal M-operation encoding with funct3 and execution class
motivation:
The current internal ALU codes place MUL variants at 11..14 and DIV/REM
at 15..18, straddling binary decode boundaries. EX repeatedly compares
these five-bit codes to identify resource classes, including on the
direct-divide-retirement path to register-file writes and ID bypass.
Recent r14s0/r14s1 and local probes show that divider arithmetic and
completion/operand-control paths compete for timing. Adding separate
registered class flags increased decode/placement cost in a local probe.
Reencoding the existing five-bit field can simplify both instruction
decode and EX resource classification without adding any state or cycle.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one micro-optimization: change the internal M-extension ALU operation
encoding to {2'b11, instruction_funct3}. Preserve the existing RV32I codes
0..10. Use MUL=24, MULH=25, MULHSU=26, MULHU=27, DIV=28, DIVU=29,
REM=30 and REMU=31. These are internal control values, not ISA encodings;
instruction bits, results, legality and every externally visible behavior
stay identical. In particular, distinguish the funct3 ordering of MULHSU
and MULHU rather than blindly incrementing the old enumeration.

Multiply membership becomes alu_op[4:2]==3'b110, and divide/remainder
membership becomes alu_op[4:2]==3'b111. Use these exact three-bit class
predicates in EX and the top-level multiply/load-use classification,
preserving the original validity qualifications and all reset, stall,
launch, consume, ownership and trap terms. EX is_divide remains
in.valid AND the divide-class predicate. is_multiply retains its original
ungated classification. Do not replace these with op[4] alone: unused
internal codes 16..23 must not become valid resource requests.

Within the decoder's existing positively validated R-type funct7=1
arm, the eight operations can assign alu_op={2'b11,funct3}. Retain
default is_illegal=1 and clear it only within the same validated legal
arms as before. Leave every RV32I, SYSTEM and reserved-instruction check
intact. Keeping the eight symbolic case assignments is also equivalent
only if Gowin demonstrably folds them into the same wiring. Prefer the
direct concatenation for the final implementation. Do not decode M operations
from funct3 without checking opcode and funct7.

Keep all arithmetic case arms symbolic. Preserve every real multiply,
divider recurrence, prefix, magnitude conversion, signed/unsigned choice,
quotient/remainder selection and exception result. Preserve the exact
ALTOPS formulas and constants under their corresponding symbolic op names.
Any simplification of signed-operation or remainder selection must match
the full five-bit equality predicates for all 32 possible internal codes,
including the now-unused codes 11..23. No arithmetic rewrite,
prefix optimization, new class flop, autonomous completion, forwarding
encoding change or additional stage belongs to this proposal.

The intended circuit change is shallower and less duplicated operation
decoding: two aligned four-code groups plus direct funct3-to-low-code
wiring. This should shorten the existing EX opcode-to-divide-grant-to-RF
path and multiply eligibility paths while preserving ID/EX width and all
pipeline timing. It may also reduce decoder logic. Mapping and routing
can still dominate; confirm that vendor synthesis actually simplifies
these cones and judge only median fitness, not gate count or RTL brevity.

Update numeric operation references inside allowed test/test_*.py files.
Do not edit test/_helpers.py, which is outside the allowed test filename
pattern. The ALU and decoder suites can define or import their corrected
internal constants within allowed test files, retaining all independent
expected arithmetic values and ISA encodings. Update the pipeline suite's
MUL_OPS, synthetic divide-control constructor (old base 15 becomes 28)
and synthetic multiply-control constructor (old MUL 11 becomes 24).
Packed field widths and every assertion remain intact. Add checks for
unique operation codes, both exact class sets and unused-code exclusion.

Run strict lint, real/ALTOPS ALU and pipeline tests, decoder legality
tests, unchanged formal, and ready/stalled full-RVFI cosimulation. Keep
all canonical CoreMark CRCs, required UART text, bounded addresses and
marker-bracketed timing. The ten-cycle liveness bound, nret=1 ports,
retirement order, retained WB forwarding, and all hard invariants remain
unchanged. Expected marked CoreMark cycles are exactly 4,238,604.

The initial prefix idea was rejected after measurement: two narrow
radix-4 prefix steps reached 74.651 MHz median, moving only its high
guard reached 75.599 MHz, and a minimized Boolean prefix reached
75.815 MHz. Separate registered divide/multiply flags reached 72.695 MHz.
Those changes are excluded. A baseline rerun reproduced 82.887 MHz.
These are negative findings, not validation of this operation reencoding.
An enum-only prototype using the related 16+funct3 assignment passed
all 13 existing ALU, decoder and pipeline configurations after updating
only test-side operation constants. It reached 76.338 MHz median, below
the champion; a different aligned 12..19 assignment reached 67.073 MHz.
Reencoding by itself therefore has negative timing evidence. The final
explicit 16+funct3 variant, including direct decoder concatenation and
class predicates, reached 73.359/78.702/78.702 MHz, still a regression.
The final candidate instead uses 24+funct3: both upper M-code bits are
one, changing sharing with base-operation decode (only SRL/SRA/LUI among
base operations set bit 3). It retains explicit decoder concatenation
and class predicates. This final bit assignment is unmeasured; the
related results are negative evidence and justify low confidence.
Its class equations match the named sets for all 32 internal codes;
this does not establish a timing improvement. The complete final circuit
must be timed and validated independently.
Success requires median fitness strictly above 204.5453 iterations/s,
more than 4.6 percent above 195.55; at unchanged cycles this requires
approximately 86.699 MHz. Confidence remains low until measured.

title: Late branch operand collection at the memory completion boundary
motivation:
The champion achieves 195.55 iterations/s at 82.887 MHz with 4,238,604
marked CoreMark cycles. Its EX forwarding, branch comparison and
recovery form one combinational timing cone. A branch immediately
following a load also pays the generic late-result dependency bubble.
A dynamic retirement trace of the canonical marked interval contains
2,922,016 instructions, 529,588 conditional branches and 135,320
adjacent load-to-branch dependencies on a nonzero destination. This
is an opportunity count, not a count of removable cycles: instruction
stalls already separate some pairs. Moving branch operand consumption
to the following stage can remove these dependencies' explicit bubbles
and place a register boundary before comparison and recovery.
Prior r10s1 merely registered already-resolved recovery events; it
added 1.61 percent CoreMark cycles without removing load-use bubbles.
The proposed late operand collection is the essential difference.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one structural change: resolve conditional branches at the
EX/MEM-to-MEM/WB completion stage, with a registered late-operand
selector that can consume the immediately preceding load or multiply
from normal MEM/WB. Move architectural recovery for direct and
indirect jumps to this same in-order completion boundary so no live
EX recovery remains on the fetch and squash control path. Ordinary
ALU, memory, multiply and divide execution keep their current cycle
boundaries. Keep nret=1, the existing BHT prediction algorithm,
architectural register file and external memory/RVFI interfaces.

In decode, classify only validated conditional BRANCH encodings as
late consumers: opcode 0x63 with funct3 in 0,1,4,5,6,7. Exempt only
those instructions from the current load/multiply-use bubble. Loads,
stores, ALU operations, JALR, reserved encodings and all other consumers
retain their present dependency interlock. Preserve imem-unavailable
masking, dmem hold priority and divide waiting. No unavailable or
wrong-path instruction may gain architectural ownership through this
exemption. Do not use raw opcode matching that accepts reserved
BRANCH funct3 values.

EX continues collecting the ordinary forwarded source values. For a
conditional branch, register those values and source addresses into
EX/MEM without consuming them in a comparator or deciding a branch
trap there. Also capture two late-source bits on the same advancing
edge. Each bit is true iff the current valid EX/MEM instruction will
actually write a nonzero rd at normal MEM/WB on that edge and its rd
matches the branch's corresponding source. Qualify with MEM's actual
trap-suppressed next_mem_wb_w_en and valid ownership; a misaligned
load must not become a replacement source. Computing these matches
before the branch's EX/MEM boundary avoids a destination comparison
in its eventual compare/recovery cycle. This can apply to all normal
preceding writers; loads and multiplies are the cases where replacing
the collected EX operand is necessary for correctness.

In MEM, a branch's resolved operand is the stable normal MEM/WB
completed value when its registered late-source bit is set, otherwise
its EX/MEM-collected source value. Use one two-input mux per source.
Both bits may select the same preceding result. The normal MEM/WB
value here is the existing retained register, not the current MEM
combinational result or the top-level direct-divide retirement mux.
There must be no combinational memory-data-to-branch-comparator bypass.
Thus a load enters MEM while its dependent branch is in EX; at the
next edge the load result and the branch's late-source selectors
register together; the branch compares that registered result in MEM
with no load-use bubble. A multiply follows the same protocol.

When an older memory request stalls, hold the branch in ID/EX with
its existing forwarding state and hold EX/MEM normally. Capture the
late-source bits only when that producer is accepted and the branch
actually enters EX/MEM. Preserve retained WB forwarding while the
branch is still in EX. A trapped preceding load must leave the
destination's prior architectural value visible: collect its fallback
using the unchanged ordinary forwarding priority, and leave its late
replacement bit clear. Divides continue to deliver to younger decode
through the existing RF write-first path; they do not occupy the
normal late-source slot.

Carry the branch operation and the existing recovery tokens through
EX/MEM: branch_prediction_xor, recovery_branch_check and
recovery_static_miss. Precompute/register PC+4 and PC+immediate in EX,
independent of operand comparison. MEM performs exactly the current
signed/unsigned/equality condition, direction-token mismatch and
taken-target alignment checks using its resolved operands. Preserve
offset-plus-four equivalence, predicted-but-untaken recovery and
fall-through on a misaligned taken target. A not-taken branch with a
misaligned hypothetical target still neither traps nor loses its
legitimate training event. Update both RVFI source values and pc_next
from MEM's resolved branch values; stale EX placeholders must never
reach architectural retirement. Train the same bimodal table exactly
once for each advancing legal, nontrapping conditional branch.

For JAL/JALR, retain EX's present forwarded target arithmetic,
alignment handling and PC+4 link result. Register the existing direct
miss or unconditional legal-JALR recovery token and resolved target
with the instruction, then issue its recovery in MEM. Preserve the
current trap-aware speculative writer qualification, including direct
JAL alignment suppression; do not replace it with unconditional writer
intent. Unconditional legal-JALR recovery now kills a younger EX
instruction before that instruction can consume a speculative link
from a trapping JALR. Keeping every recovery at MEM avoids a new
priority network combining older MEM recovery with younger live EX
recovery. Do not change target prediction, add a BTB/RAS, or add a
separate delayed BHT update stage.

A recovery from the older MEM instruction must redirect fetch and
squash both the younger ID/EX instruction and the next EX/MEM entry.
The recovering instruction still advances to MEM/WB and retires once.
Clear side-effect controls as well as validity in every killed entry.
Gate younger EX advancement, divider launch and divider consumption
with the older recovery. Gate execute_wait with its negation so a
wrong-path divide cannot block recovery; an unlaunched wrong-path
divide must never start. Recovery overrides younger dependency holds
and imem unavailability, while actual older dmem transactions retain
their hold priority. Emit redirect and training only from valid,
accepted MEM ownership, with reset cancellation and no replay of a
retained event. Correctly predicted branches sustain one instruction
per cycle, including consecutive conditional branches.

This structure separates forwarding/operand collection from the
branch compare-to-fetch path while retaining only a small late-result
mux before comparison. Its throughput benefit specifically comes
from removing branch late-result bubbles. Costs include branch target
and selector storage, one additional cycle per recovery, and BHT
training one cycle later. These costs must be measured together:
135,320 adjacent load/branch pairs are not a promised 135,320-cycle
saving. The unchanged divider, jump target capture or new MEM compare
path may limit Fmax. Confidence is low; expected net fitness gain is
eight percent, not a measured result.

Check branches after loads of every width/sign and after all MUL*
variants, either or both source matches, x0, repeated writes to the
same destination and both ordinary forwarding sources. Include a
misaligned load whose destination retains an earlier value. Check
long dmem holds, imem bubbles, branch chains, taken and untaken
misaligned targets, offset +4, JAL/JALR link consumers and traps,
reset, and direct divide completion followed by a branch. Put loads,

title: Prediction-polarity prefix resolution with predecoded recovery rails
motivation: The champion scores 195.55 iterations/s at 82.887 MHz with 4,238,604 marked CoreMark cycles. A fresh unchanged-RTL Gowin placement-option-1 build reproduced 82.887 MHz. Its worst path runs from MEM/WB operand data through EX forwarding, a full-width carry chain, recovery logic and high-fanout squash to the registered forwarding selectors. Prior replay found only about 54,467 conditional misses and 13,735 JALRs, so accuracy alone cannot clear the 4.6 percent acceptance margin. Target caches, delayed BHT training and extra recovery boundaries have regressed. Target the computation of prediction mismatch itself, preserving the champion's prediction sequence and recovery cycle.

hypothesis.motivation: The champion scores 195.55 iterations/s at 82.887 MHz with 4,238,604 marked CoreMark cycles. A fresh unchanged-RTL Gowin placement-option-1 build reproduced 82.887 MHz. Its worst path runs from MEM/WB operand data through EX forwarding, a full-width carry chain, recovery logic and high-fanout squash to the registered forwarding selectors. Prior replay found only about 54,467 conditional misses and 13,735 JALRs, so accuracy alone cannot clear the 4.6 percent acceptance margin. Target caches, delayed BHT training and extra recovery boundaries have regressed. Target the computation of prediction mismatch itself, preserving the champion's prediction sequence and recovery cycle.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the conditional-branch predictor resolver with one prediction-polarity parallel-prefix network. This is a predictor recovery architecture change, not a direction-policy change. Keep the original 128-entry binary bimodal BHT, immediate-resolution training, raw-instruction direct-target prediction, full-width guarded targets, combinational IF/ID, pipeline depth and unconditional legal JALR recovery. Do not carry over any exploratory BHT recoding, static prediction, delayed recovery, arithmetic-readiness qualification or forwarding-comparator replication.

The current recovery first computes a full-width equality/less-than branch_base, selects the comparison kind, XORs the saved branch_prediction_xor, and qualifies the result with recovery_branch_check. Instead, predecode equality recovery polarity into ID/EX and absorb ordered-comparison prediction polarity into the leaves of a balanced prefix tree. Keep all existing prediction metadata, architectural branch semantics and full-width actual_next_pc calculations.

Let P be the saved branch_prediction_xor = predicted_direct XOR branch_op[0]. Retain the existing signed-to-unsigned bias on bit 31 of each forwarded operand: XOR that sign bit with !branch_op[1], leaving the other bits unchanged. Divide these biased operands into sixteen two-bit slices. For each slice i independently compute E_i=(A_i==B_i) and M_i=((A_i<B_i) XOR P). Each leaf is a two-bit comparison with saved polarity, rather than a slice of a 32-bit ripple comparator. A pair (E,M) summarizes equality and the less-than-result XOR P for its entire bit range.

Combine adjacent summaries in exactly four balanced levels, always giving the more significant half priority: E=E_hi AND E_lo; M=E_hi ? M_lo : M_hi. Implement this as explicit small constant-index nodes, with a two-input mux or the equivalent disjoint masked OR. The root M is exactly (biased_rs1 < biased_rs2) XOR P, including the all-equal case where every leaf and the root M equal P. The root E is exact 32-bit equality. This associative lexicographic reduction propagates the already prediction-adjusted predicate, so the ordered recovery path has no full-width carry chain and no polarity XOR after the root. Use ordinary synthesizable logic, without changing constraints or requiring preservation attributes.

In decode, derive three mutually exclusive recovery enables from the existing legal/aligned/non-+4 recovery_branch_check qualification. For BEQ/BNE, register recover_equal when P=0 and recover_unequal when P=1. For BLT/BGE/BLTU/BGEU, register recover_ordered. All three must be zero for any nonbranch, reserved encoding, misaligned direct target or +4 branch. Capture these bits with the same reset, flush and hold priorities as the original ID/EX recovery metadata. Continue capturing P exactly as today; never consult a later BHT lookup for a held instruction.

In EX, compute direct_miss = recovery_static_miss OR (recover_equal AND E_root) OR (recover_unequal AND !E_root) OR (recover_ordered AND M_root). Preserve the original advance gate and the separate unconditional legal-JALR miss. Do not move decode, target alignment, the branch-kind mux or a late direction XOR back between the ordered prefix root and recovery. Keep direct JAL, +4 direct transfers, target-range refusal, misalignment traps, recovery priority and wrong-path squash behavior unchanged.

Architectural branch outcome and training must remain exact. Reconstruct unsigned-order less-than as L_root=M_root XOR P for use in the existing branch_base/branch_cond selection, or use an algebraically identical independent outcome expression. BEQ/BNE use E_root; ordered branches use L_root; retain funct3 inversion and reserved-encoding handling. Keep that outcome reconstruction outside the direct_miss cone. RVFI pc_wdata and redirect_target continue to use the architectural resolved next PC, never a predicted value. BHT training still occurs exactly once on each advancing legal nontrapping conditional branch, including untaken branches with a misaligned hypothetical target, and never on holds or bubbles.

The intended gain is shorter forwarded-operand-to-recovery latency at unchanged CPI, with sixteen small leaves and four regular reduction levels replacing the ripple comparison followed by selection and polarity logic. New decode tokens cost at most three ID/EX bits and can replace timed uses of the old generic branch-check token. Main risks are routing through the prefix tree, polarity fanout, logic duplication for architectural outcome, and the possibility that BHT training or the unchanged divider becomes limiting. Expected fitness gain is seven percent with low confidence. This final prediction-polarity tree and predecoded-rail combination has NOT been integrated into the core, simulated as a CPU or timed; no measured improvement is claimed. Synthesis may factor the common polarity back out of the leaves, so inspect the mapped recovery cone rather than assuming the intended graph survives.

Exploratory negative evidence must not be mistaken for validation of this proposal. Direction/strength BHT recoding measured 73.126 MHz median; an ordinary four-by-eight-bit comparator without absorbed prediction polarity or predecoded recovery rails measured 74.169 MHz median; selective registered conditional recovery measured 72.814 MHz median and increased marked cycles to 4,293,094. Their canonical CoreMark checks passed, but all failed the fitness target. Forwarding-parallel comparisons, static prediction and removing the generic execute-wait gate from recovery likewise failed the frequency target in placement-option-1 screening. An ordinary two-bit-leaf prefix comparator that retained the original late branch-kind/polarity recovery also measured only 72.354 MHz in placement option 1. These results argue against a comparator rewrite alone. The final proposal changes both the representation of the predicate inside the comparison tree and its registered recovery interface, rather than repeating those circuits.

A standalone Yosys SAT miter proved the proposed prefix root, architectural less-than reconstruction and three-rail direct_miss equivalent to independent signed/unsigned branch conditions for arbitrary 32-bit operands, all funct3 encodings, both prediction bits, an arbitrary branch-check enable and static-miss input. This is a combinational algebra proof, not pipeline, formal-contract or timing validation.

Before implementation acceptance, prove the prefix algebra against independent signed/unsigned RV32 branch comparisons for arbitrary operands, both saved prediction polarities and all six legal funct3 values. Verify the complete new direct_miss expression against the original token predicate, including offset +4, zero/backward offsets, source-PC wrap, out-of-range prediction refusal and alignment traps. Exercise equal operands, every possible first-differing slice, opposite sign bits, x0, all forwarding selections, held WB forwarding, load/multiply-use stalls, older dmem stalls, unavailable imem, wrong-path stores/divides and reset. Preserve the existing real/ALTOPS unit tests and unchanged single-channel formal, including ten-cycle liveness, full-RVFI cosim and canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks. Prediction, redirect and retirement sequences should remain identical to the champion for a fixed ready trace.

Keep nret=1, external IO, decoder defaults, arithmetic units, register-file implementation and every correctness gate intact. Measure all three Gowin placement options and the actual marked cycles on the final RTL. At unchanged 4,238,604 cycles, acceptance requires median Fmax strictly above 86.698653 MHz and fitness strictly above 204.5453 iterations/s. A cycle-only or single-placement gain is insufficient.
